title: Budda Baker hasn't asked to be traded, and hasn't asked not to be traded
summary: Cardinals safety Budda Baker says he's not seeking a trade.
full_text: Cardinals safety Budda Baker says he's not seeking a trade. Nor has he expressly asked to stay in Arizona. Baker, who has often been mentioned as a potential trade target multiple times over the years, told Josh Weinfuss of ESPN on Wednesday that he has not requested a trade, nor has he requested not to be traded . Baker said he hasn't talked to General Manager Monti Ossenfort "about anything." "My approach is I'm here," Baker said. "I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it." Baker knows there will be people talking about him as the November 10 trade deadline approaches. "It's a deadline for a reason," Baker said. "Teams are trying to get players, and our team might be trying to get players and getting other players. So, at the end of the day, it's a business." Baker is 30 years old and is under contract through 2027 at a salary of about $16 million a season. We'll find out in the next 12 days whether two teams think a Baker trade is good business.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cam Heyward: Jared Verse calling Steelers "dirty" will be addressed Sunday
summary: Dislike between the Browns and Steelers has been brewing for decades, so there isn't much need for any one player to fan the flames of the bad feelings between the two AFC North teams.
full_text: Dislike between the Browns and Steelers has been brewing for decades, so there isn't much need for any one player to fan the flames of the bad feelings between the two AFC North teams. Browns defensive end Jared Verse did that after the two teams played in Week 4, however. Verse explained that he doesn't "have any respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra s—t after the game" and mentioned double-teaming and sliding while calling his opponents "garbage." The two teams meet again in Pittsburgh this Sunday and Steelers defensive end Cam Heyward made it clear that Verse's comments haven't been forgotten during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show this week. "Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it . But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game," Heyward said Tuesday. "So, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say. The AFC North is on fire, and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those were words that were said, and they will be addressed." The distaste between the two teams is nothing new, but having both of them playing well at the same time is fairly uncommon. With both teams at 5-2 coming into this week, there will be more than bragging rights at stake for the winner.
author: Josh Alper

title: Justin Jefferson: You want high production, but what we're doing is working
summary: Justin Jefferson is catching fewer passes and picking up fewer yards on a per-game basis than at any other point in his career, but he's not complaining about how the 2026 season has played out thus far.
full_text: Justin Jefferson is catching fewer passes and picking up fewer yards on a per-game basis than at any other point in his career, but he's not complaining about how the 2026 season has played out thus far. The reason why Jefferson is taking his relatively limited production in stride can be explained by a glance at the standings. The Vikings are the NFL's only undefeated team and Jefferson said on Wednesday that he's had years with big numbers and few wins in the past, so he's comfortable saying that he "definitely would love winning games over having that production." Ideally, though, there'd be a balance that allows him a taste of both. “That’s something you kinda have to be in the middle ," Jefferson said. "Obviously you want to have high production. Obviously you want to be in the top category in all categories, but you have to look at the bigger picture and understand that we’re 6-0 and winning games. What we're doing right now is working. Obviously there's things to do better and things to fix on the offensive side of things, but all in all, it's coming together and we're doing things to win games." The Vikings' defense-first approach has served them well to this point, but the schedule will be thorny in the coming weeks with the Lions, Bills, Packers, 49ers and Falcons on tap in November. They're likely going to need the offense to pull a little more weight at some point in that run and finding the right way to spring Jefferson loose would be a strong step in that direction.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ashton Jeanty: Jets' defense has a couple guys who don't want to tackle
summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is having a terrible year, but he thinks he can turn that around on Sunday against the Jets.
full_text: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is having a terrible year , but he thinks he can turn that around on Sunday against the Jets. Jeanty said in the Raiders' locker room on Wednesday that he thinks there are players on the Jets' defense who don't want to tackle him, and that excites him when he sees it on tape. "I think we can definitely get the run game going," Jeanty said when asked about the Jets' defense. "Get back on track and really get after these guys. A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names." The Raiders started the season 3-0 but are now 3-4. Jeanty said that during this losing streak, he and his teammates are doing a good job of challenging each other to improve without playing the blame game. "I think the main thing is we've just to to stick together. You lose games, everybody starts questioning things," Jeanty said. "Most importantly, not pointing fingers. Everybody has to work together. It's a team sport." Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per carry this season, and that needs to improve in a hurry. He believes it can improve, against a Jets defense that allowed Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards and a touchdown last week. If it doesn't improve against a Jets defense that doesn't want to tackle, it may be time to ask bigger questions about why Jeanty can't get going.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Justin Herbert: Blame for Chargers' offense is on the players, not Mike McDaniel's fault
summary: The Chargers' starting quarterback says the new offensive coordinator does not deserve the blame.
full_text: Before the season, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh predicted that Justin Herbert would be the greatest quarterback ever . During the season, Herbert has been by some measures the worst quarterback in the NFL. That has led to plenty of talk that new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is to blame. But Herbert says that isn't the case. "It's not his fault, it's our fault as an offense," Herbert said when asked about McDaniel. "We have to do our job. It's not Mike's fault. The guys are open, plays are being made. It's on us to run, to block, to catch, to throw. It's on us as an offense." Herbert said that he's learning a lot from McDaniel, even if the results aren't showing up on the field. "Mike has been very helpful. He's such a great coach and such a great leader, to have the experience and expertise has, it's been very helpful," Herbert said. According to Herbert, the Chargers' winless season is 100 percent on the players and not at all on McDaniel. "Mike has done an incredible job of getting people open and it's on us to execute and make plays," Herbert said. "As an offense we have to come together, execute our stuff, and understand that it's on us to fix it."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Expect plenty of flags to fly on Thursday night between Panthers and Packers
summary: On Thursday night, the planets will align in a very specific way.
full_text: ' On Thursday night, the planets will align in a very specific way. And that could lead to more than a few penalties being called. When the Panthers and Packers open Week 8, the game will pit the most-penalized team (the Packers, 9.3 per game) against the fourth most-penalized team (the Panthers, (8.7 per game). The Panthers also lead the league in penalty yards per game (79.2), while the Packers are second at 78.0 yards per game. On top of that, referee Scott Novak's crew leads the league in penalties called per game (22.7) and penalties accepted per game (20.1). Throw the ingredients together, and there could be a stew of stoppages on Thursday night. Either way, it's something to monitor. Will the Packers and Panthers continue to draw an excess of penalty flags? Will Novak and crew continue to be flag-happy? It could be a good idea to take a nap tomorrow afternoon. Thursday night's game could last a little longer than usual.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay doesn't rule out having two kickers on 48-man game-day roster
summary: When you have two quarterbacks, you have none.
full_text: When you have two quarterbacks, you have none. When you have two kickers, you have a problem. The Rams, who pivoted to Brandon McManus after losing Blake Grupe (who replaced Harrison Mevis) to a torn ACL, have brought back Joshua Karty to the practice squad. On Wednesday, coach Sean McVay was asked whether he would possibly have two kickers on the 48-man, game-day roster. “We'll work through all different things," McVay said. "It all depends. When you have 48 bodies and the different guys that are filling in, you have to really ask yourself, 'Okay, does that really make sense? Does it fit?' There are a lot of layers to it so I wouldn't be ready to answer that question yet.” Karty, a sixth-round pick in 2024, lost the job to Mevis during the 2025 season. He had been out of the NFL after being released by the Cardinals on June 4. The kicker issue is one of various issues the Rams have with their special teams. In a league where so many games turn on so few moments, a single special-teams glitch can turn a win into a loss. At 3-4, the Rams can't afford to lose many more games. On Sunday, they get a golden opportunity to get to .500 against the 0-6 Chargers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love limited in his return to practice

title: New study estimates 75 percent of former NFL players who died from 2008 to 2023 had CTE
summary: A new study from JAMA Network Open by researchers at Boston University, Mass General Brigham, and the Concussion & CTE Foundation has found that an estimated 75 percent of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE.
full_text: A new study from JAMA Network Open by researchers at Boston University, Mass General Brigham, and the Concussion & CTE Foundation has found that an estimated 75 percent of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE. "Many cases may have been early stage at the time of death and possibly symptom free," the paper said, via Shwetha Surendran of ESPN. That observation speaks to one of the basic realities of CTE. It's unknown how many people have it. And it's no surprise that the vast majority of former NFL players who die with CTE symptoms are later determined to have had CTE. There's a balance to strike. On one hand, it's obvious that long-term, repetitive head trauma isn't good for the brain. On the other hand, it can be problematic to have hundreds, if not thousands, of former NFL players believing they already have — and constantly fearing the inevitable development of symptoms. Even now, years after CTE became a commonly-known term, there's much work to be done in order to understand who gets it, how it develops, and what it means to have it. Hopefully, the research will continue with the goal of better clarifying the risks that current players are assuming without making those whose careers have ended unduly anxious about the possibility that a ticking time bomb has been embedded in their brains.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay: Davante Adams "closer to the shorter term" of the 6-10 week timeline
summary: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams injured his hamstring in an Oct. 18 game against the Cardinals.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams injured his hamstring in an Oct. 18 game against the Cardinals. He recently underwent a procedure on the ruptured hamstring. "Everything's good. It went really well," Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday. "He's feeling good in the process of recovering and doing really well.” The prognosis for Adams was 6-10 weeks, but McVay said that Adams will return probably "closer to the shorter term" of the timeline. That could mean Adams returns sometime after the team's Week 11 off week. “He tells me, which I believe, [that] he's Wolverine," McVay said. "He'll heal quick and be ready to go. He's in good spirits. [He] sent me a picture the other day [of him] being able to walk already. He’s doing really well, and I think based on how everything went, on the shorter end is what is projected.” Adams, who is on injured reserve, has 30 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games.
author: Charean Williams

title: For PFT's 25th anniversary, completely re-written Quarterback of the Future is coming
summary: The 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT happens on Sunday, November 1.
full_text: ' The 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT happens on Sunday, November 1. And for those of you who have been here since the early days of the site's existence, I've made you something. I've completely re-written Quarterback of the Future , the long-forgotten football/sci-fi novel that helped lead me into this business in the first place. I won't bore you with the details of how it all happened here. (I'll bore you with the details of how it all happened here , in the official introduction to the book I'll post one chapter at a time free of charge.) Also, here's the landing page for the various chapters. The plan is to post one per day. (They're relatively short.) Depending on the response, my mood at any given moment, and whether time permits, I may accelerate the process. Regardless, it's a brand-new version of a solid story that was, frankly, not very well written. After years of writing thousands of words per day (and writing eight or nine novels — I've lost track — along with Playmakers), the second try is better. As I'm reminded whenever I flip through a copy of the original QBF , it can't be much worse. Take it for whatever it is. It should be fun. It should be enjoyable. Each chapter should make you interested in reading the next one. Give it a try. Chapter One arrives Sunday, the official 25th anniversary of the moment we first went live.
author: Mike Florio

title: Troy Aikman says there's a "50-50 chance" he won't be working in TV next year
summary: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman appeared at a Dallas event on Wednesday night with Peter King, in connection with Peter's new book, The Game.
full_text: ' Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman appeared at a Dallas event on Wednesday night with Peter King, in connection with Peter's new book, The Game . During the session, Aikman addressed whether he'd be calling NFL games in 2027. Along the way, Aikman addressed the Babar in the bookstore. Via veteran sports journalist Tim Cowlishaw, Aikman said there's a " 50-50 chance " that Aikman won't be working in TV next year. Given the circumstances, that seems accurate. Aikman's contract expires after the Super Bowl, and he has not been bashful when it comes to expressing concern (and exasperation) with ESPN's lack of interest in negotiating an extension. If he leaves ESPN, where else will he go? With CBS already deciding to make J.J. Watt the replacement for Tony Romo, a prime seat will be available for Aikman only if Prime Video opts to exercise its ability to buy out Kirk Herbstreit and pivot to Aikman. It's no surprise, then, that Aikman has been talking about possibly working for the Cowboys. He has spoken about wanting to work in a front office, and his consulting gig with the Dolphins may have been the first step toward a Matt Millen/John Lynch-style pivot.
author: Mike Florio

title: Caleb Williams hasn't been fined for Week 7, despite wearing unauthorized shoes
summary: Bears QB vows to keep wearing Caddix cleats.
full_text: The NFL fined Bears quarterback Caleb Williams $11,941 for wearing an " unauthorized logo " on his shoes in Week 6, at Atlanta. In Week 7, he wore the same brand of shoe — Caddix, which doesn't have a licensing deal with the NFL. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Williams has not yet been fined. (For Week 6, the fine was issued on the following Tuesday.) Williams explained on Wednesday his reasons for wearing shoes made by a company that doesn't have a money-for-nothing deal with the NFL. "As we've known for the past couple of years now, I’m huge into my body ," Williams said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "I'm huge into trying to stay on the field. I'm huge into trying to be healthy. It's a rough game and things like that. So the cleats, they've been great. They've been super comfy and they've worked. They are a science-type of cleat. It's something that focuses on when you plant on the hard plants on turf or grass, they call them SmartStuds, and they move when you move in these hard plants. They take tension off of your tendons, your joints and all of that. So over the course of a long career or over the course of a long year, when you can take some percentage -- it could be one, it could be 50, it could be 12, it could be whatever, you know. When you take that percentage off consistently over a period of time, you know, you get to have the chance, a higher chance of being healthy. And so that's what I focus on. "I try to be healthy. They're smart cleats. They're science cleats, and they've been working for me. A bunch of other guys wear them in the league, and they're forward-focused on making sure players stay on the field, and that's what I'm always focused on." The NFL didn't fine Williams for wearing the Caddix cleats in the preseason or in Week 1 or Week 2 of the regular season. (He didn't play in Week 3, Week 4, or Week 5 due to a hamstring injury.) Although Caddix plans to pay Williams's fine, league rules generally prohibit the payment of fines by anyone other than the person fined. Caddix could easily tiptoe around that technicality with an endorsement deal with Williams. (Then again, he's already giving the team a strong endorsement for free.) The situation has put the league in an awkward spot. On one hand, it needs to protect the shoe companies that pay the league good money for the right to outfit its players. On the other hand, if the Caddix shoes are safer, the league risks creating the perception (yet again) that supposed concerns about health and safety take a backseat to the ongoing pursuit of the almighty dollar.
author: Mike Florio

title: 18.8 million watched Cowboys-Eagles on Monday night
summary: Even with the teams entering the game at a combined 4-8, an NFC East battle between the Cowboys and Eagles delivered.
full_text: Even with the teams entering the game at a combined 4-8, an NFC East battle between the Cowboys and Eagles delivered. Per ESPN, 18.8 million viewers watched the Week 7 Monday night game between Dallas and Philadelphia. Keeping with a recent trend, ESPN announced that more than one million watched alt casts on ESPN2 and NFL Network, without specifying the audiences for the ManningCast and the Next Gen Stats production. The NFL event had competition in the form of Game 3 of the World Series, on Fox. Fox has yet to announce the viewership for Game 3. (Usually, silence from a network means there's nothing special about the numbers.) On Friday and Saturday, Game 1 and Game 2 drew 12.259 million viewers and 10.854 million viewers, respectively. Once upon a time, the NFL avoided head-to-head competition with the World Series. In the late '70s, the NFL moved the Monday night game that conflicted with the World Series to the prior Thursday night. Through 2009, the NFL avoided the first Sunday night of the World Series. In 2010, the NFL decided to take over; the World Series now plays Game 1 and Game 2 on Friday and Saturday. The smartest move for baseball would be to avoid Sunday, Monday, and Thursday when scheduling the World Series.
author: Mike Florio

title: DB Caleb Downs, WR George Pickens, DL Quinnen Williams limited Wednesday

author: Charean Williams

title: Jared Verse misses practice, Browns expect him to play against Steelers
summary: The Browns had a significant member of their defense on the sideline at Wednesday's practice, but concern is low about defensive end Jared Verse missing Sunday's game against the Steelers.
full_text: The Browns had a significant member of their defense on the sideline at Wednesday's practice, but concern is low about defensive end Jared Verse missing Sunday's game against the Steelers. title: Aaron Jones out of practice with a knee injury
summary: Reports were that Vikings running back Aaron Jones avoided a serious injury last Sunday, but his practice work is still being managed this week.
full_text: Reports were that Vikings running back Aaron Jones avoided a serious injury last Sunday, but his practice work is still being managed this week. The Vikings' first injury report of the week shows that Jones did not practice on Wednesday. Jones aggravated a knee injury in the second half of Minnesota's win over the Colts and word is that he is considered day-to-day heading into Sunday's game against the Lions. Jordan Mason led the team in rushing against the Colts and would be in line for an even bigger role if Jones isn't able to play this week. author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles place RB Dameon Pierce on IR, sign Jaydon Blue to active roster
summary: The Eagles placed running back Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Eagles placed running back Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday, the team announced. Pierce left in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game with an undisclosed injury. He will miss at least the next four games before returning. He is the fourth running back the Eagles have placed on injured reserve this season. In three games, Pierce had 37 carries for 96 yards and two touchdowns. In a corresponding move, the Eagles signed running back Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to the active roster. This is Blue's second stint on the active roster this season. He signed with the Eagles' practice squad before the season and was signed to the active roster ahead of the Week 6 game against the Panthers. The Eagles waived him from the active roster the following week, and he rejoined the practice squad. Blue, a fifth-round pick of the Cowboys in 2025, had 34 rushes for 129 yards and a touchdown in five games for Dallas. The Eagles also announced they signed offensive guard Evan Beerntsen, wide receiver Quentin Skinner and defensive back Shaun Wade to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Texans expect Jaylin Noel to miss the rest of the season
summary: The toe injury that landed Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve is likely to end his season.
full_text: The toe injury that landed Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve is likely to end his season. The Texans expect Noel to have surgery on his toe and miss the rest of the season , according to the Houston Chronicle . A 2025 third-round pick, Noel was off to an excellent start in his second NFL season. He leads the NFL with an average of 14.4 yards per target, leads the Texans with 331 receiving yards, and is the Texans' primary punt and kickoff returner. He'll be hard to replace. Helping to replace Noel will be that wide receiver Tank Dell finally returned last week from the knee injury that cost him more than a year, and that wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. was added in a trade with the Cardinals. But even with potential replacements available, losing Noel hurts, on a Texans team that is running out of time to turn its season around.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lamar Jackson a full participant in Wednesday's practice
summary: The Ravens quarterback last had a full practice on Oct. 2.

Jackson was trending toward playing last week, with limited practices in all three on-field days. The Ravens went 1-2 without Jackson, who is 3-1 with six passing touchdowns, one interception and one rushing touchdown. title: Texans place WR Jaylin Noel on IR, claim RB Emari Demercado off waivers
summary: The Texans placed wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve Wednesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Texans placed wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve Wednesday, the team announced. Noel, 24, has turf toe that will keep him out at least four weeks. He has 19 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns in seven games this season. Noel played all 17 games last season as a rookie, making 26 receptions for 292 yards and two touchdowns. In a corresponding move, the Texans claimed running back Emari Demercado off waivers from the Cowboys. Dallas cut Demercado on Tuesday. Dallas claimed Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs on Aug. 31. The Cowboys waived Demercado for the first time on Oct. 8, but re-signed him. Demercado ran five times for 15 yards in two appearances for Dallas. He had 131 carries for 834 yards and three touchdowns in 40 games for the Cardinals over the past three seasons, adding 50 catches for 324 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Titans claim DT Jonah Laulu off waivers
summary: The Titans claimed defensive tackle Jonah Laulu off waivers, according to Jordan Schultz of the Schultz Report.
full_text: The Titans claimed defensive tackle Jonah Laulu off waivers, according to Jordan Schultz of the Schultz Report. Laulu, 26, was a healthy scratch on Sunday. In five games this season, he has five tackles, three quarterback hits and half a sack. Laulu has played 110 defensive snaps and 24 on special teams. The Colts selected him in the seventh round in 2024, but the Raiders claimed him off waivers out of the preseason that year. He set the franchise record for most tackles (86) for a defensive lineman over the first two seasons. Laulu totaled 91 tackles, 5.5 sacks, eight passes defensed and 12 quarterback hits in 39 games with the Raiders.

title: With higher waiver priority, Dolphins add OL Christian Haynes
summary: Earlier on Wednesday, the Ravens announced that they had claimed guard Christian Haynes off waivers.
full_text: ''' Earlier on Wednesday, the Ravens announced that they had claimed guard Christian Haynes off waivers. But there was a problem with that — the Dolphins had, too. So, Haynes will actually be headed to Miami, as the Dolphins are higher on the waiver-claim priority list because they have a worse record. The Seahawks waived Haynes on Tuesday after acquiring Quenton Nelson via trade from the Colts. Haynes, 26, was a Seattle third-round pick in the 2024 draft. He started five games for the Seahawks this season, though the last one was the Week 6 loss to Denver before he was relegated to special teams duty for Sunday’s win over the Chiefs. In all, Haynes has appeared in 31 games with five starts over the last three seasons. As a corresponding move, the Dolphins have waived offensive lineman DJ Campbell.

title: Myles Garrett will not return to practice this week

full_text: ''' A report late last week indicated that Rams linebacker Myles Garrett was on track to practice this week, but that turned out to be off base. title: The non-political Kirk Herbstreit recently spoke at a political action committee event
summary: This age of liars, grifters, and charlatans encourages other liars, grifters, and charlatans to lie, grift, and/or engage in charlatanry.
full_text: ' This age of liars, grifters, and charlatans encourages other liars, grifters, and charlatans to lie, grift, and/or engage in charlatanry. Enter Kirk Herbstreit, who seems to think his perpetual canine shield will keep him from being scrutinized as aggressively as he should be. Last month, Herbstreit addressed the intense (and justified) criticism of ESPN's overt support for the Protect College Sports Act by pointing out that he's decidedly not a political person. “ I don’t really get into politics ," Herbstreit said the Friday after Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Tex.) was loudly booed during an extended infomercial for the PCSA during College GameDay . "It’s just not — I’m kind of an independent guy, right down the middle of the fairway. I’m for America, so whoever helps us as a country, I’m for. Whether it’s somebody on the left, somebody on the right, so I don’t really follow it. I don’t know anything about his political views. I don’t know what he’s for or against. I care about football, my family, and my faith, and my country. Those are things I love." He also loves, apparently, to make time in his otherwise non-stop in-season schedule to appear at political action committee fundraising events. Via David Covucci of FOIABall , Herbstreit served as the keynote speaker at a major Business Council of Alabama function on October 21 — the night before he called the Patriots-Bears game in Chicago. The goal of the event was to raise money for BCA’s political action committee, Progress PAC. “This cornerstone Progress PAC fundraising event commences with VIP gatherings and concludes with dinner and dialogue from a notable guest," the group's website explained, per Covucci. "This important component of Campaign 2026 provides the resources needed to support the election of pro-business candidates across the state.” In political circles, "pro-business" is code for "conservative." And, as Covucci notes, BCA endorsed 108 candidates in Alabama races. Of them, 82 are Republican. Of the 26 Democrats it has endorsed, 20 are running unopposed. The day after the event, BCA funneled $155,000 to the campaign of Republican Senator Tommy Tuberville. Look, Herbstreit can speak at any political event he wants. That's not the issue. The issue is that he responded to the blatant effort by ESPN to boost the PCSA by saying, essentially, "I don't know nothing about no politics." Whatever the specific context, bullshit smells the same in all of them. Even if Herbstreit thinks that taking his dog everywhere he goes will make people feel less inclined to call him out for it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Andy Reid on signing Justin Tucker to practice squad: "He's done his suspension"
summary: Even before the Ravens cut Justin Tucker, which happened before Tucker accepted a 10-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy based on allegations of sexual misconduct at massage-therapy sessions, Tucker's skills were declining.
full_text: Even before the Ravens cut Justin Tucker, which happened before Tucker accepted a 10-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy based on allegations of sexual misconduct at massage-therapy sessions, Tucker's skills were declining. It's no surprise, then, that he went nearly a year with only a smattering of tryouts and no offers. It was definitely a surprise when the Chiefs added Tucker to the practice squad. On Wednesday, coach Andy Reid was asked about the message he thinks the move sends to female fans in Kansas City. "Yeah, so he's done his suspension, you know, and took care of that business there," Reid said. "But I'll leave it at that for you." It's unclear what "business" he took care of, other than serving the suspension. He strongly denied the allegations from the outset, even though he eventually accepted the suspension. Reid later was asked what goes into his decision-making process when giving an opportunity to someone who's looking for a second chance. "I try to do homework on it," Reid said, "and see exactly what has been — what's taken place since, and, but, you know, I mean, the kid — he served a suspension. It's been time. There's been time involved with it, so that's how I evaluate him." Obviously, the Chiefs saw something in Tucker's workout that made them believe it was worth taking P.R. flak for adding Tucker to the practice squad. It also helps that Reid has a fistful of Super Bowl rings and is the most accomplished coach currently in the NFL. Still, for the same reasons that plenty of Browns fans had (and still have) misgivings about the presence of Deshaun Watson on the roster, plenty of Chiefs fans will be feeling a little conflicted and confused about the decision to entrust a job in which supply far outweighs demand to someone with as much if not more baggage than any kicker has ever carried.

title: Two NFL teams set to unveil a new uniform in Week 8 with special 'Rivalries' helmet and jersey
summary: The Lions and Jaguars will both be debuting new uniforms on Sunday
full_text:
Two NFL teams will be debuting a totally new look on Sunday, with the Detroit Lions and Jacksonville Jaguars both getting set to play in their "Rivalries" uniforms for the first time.
The Lions will be rocking their uniforms in an NFC North showdown with the Vikings , while the Jaguars will unveil their new look against the Colts . The Jags and Lions will both be playing at home on Sunday, and both games will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.
The new uniforms were actually unveiled back in August , but the two teams haven't gotten a chance to wear them just yet.
Both uniforms were designed as part of the NFL's "Rivalries" program. The idea was to create a new look based on a theme that's local to each team. The Lions teamed up with Nike to create a "Defend the Den" uniform featuring a white jersey, white pants and a Honolulu blue helmet.
@lions are debuting their NFL x Nike Rivalries jerseys this week against the Minnesota Vikings 👀 MINvsDET – Sunday 1:00pm ET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Iq2Anh5lKm
According to the team , the blue helmet features "Carbon fiber within the decals texture symbolizes elite performance and connects to Detroit's car and racing culture."
On the Jaguars' end, their new uniform is an ode to the city of Jacksonville and Duval County. The Jags' helmet has "Duval" written on the back bumper, while on the front end, the team added Jacksonville's "904" area code.
If you watch the Jags play on Sunday, the helmet will probably be the first thing you notice. Jacksonville will be wearing a teal helmet for the first time in franchise history.
The Teal Helmet details 🤩 @Riddell_Collect | @Jaguars | @NFL pic.twitter.com/JSBViqXNul
As for the rest of the uniform, the Jags didn't get too crazy. They'll be wearing a white jersey paired with black pants.
16 #INDvsJAX pic.twitter.com/xc3uBdtclb
The font used for the numbers was "heavily inspired by the historic music venues and southern rock influence that Jacksonville is known for," according to the team .
The Jaguars and Lions won't be the first teams to wear their new "Rivalries" uniform this year, and they won't be the last. All four teams in both the AFC South and NFC North have unveiled new uniforms, but so far only the Colts and Packers have worn them.
The Colts wore theirs during a win over the Texans in Week 3.
Another look at the @Colts NFL x Nike Rivalries jerseys 👀 @HOUvsIND -- 1pm ET on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gEWlqbBSd0
As for the Packers, they debuted their new look during a 31-7 win over the Bears in Week 5.
@jordan3love in the @packers NFL x Nike Rivalries uniforms 😮‍💨 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/BDzDTPbOPA
The Packers' win means teams are 2-0 this year when wearing their "Rivalries" uniforms.
Here's the full "Rivalries" schedule for 2026. Keep in mind that with the games below, only the home team will be wearing the new uniform:
Each team will only wear their "Rivalries" uniform once this season, but they'll be allowed to keep it in their rotation for the next three years.
The teams in the AFC East and NFC West kicked things off in 2025 when they became the first ones to get a "Rivalries" uniform. The program will run through 2028, and by that point, all 32 teams will have unveiled their new look.

We'll have to wait two more years before we see the full set of 32 uniforms, but so far, it seems like the teams have been fully embracing the concept.

title: Agent's Take: Detroit Lions' Sam LaPorta contract problem isn't going away
summary: LaPorta may have reason to wait if the Lions use the franchise tag, especially with Brock Bowers positioned to dramatically reshape the tight end market
full_text:
Tight end Sam LaPorta's interview for "Pardon My Take" created a stir last week after the podcast aired. The 2023 second-round pick voiced frustration over the lack of progress on a new deal with the Detroit Lions , indicating he would be fine playing for another team next year.
"Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f---ing back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love," LaPorta said. "…I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else."
A majority of the Lions fan base viewed LaPorta's comments as selfish, greedy, disloyal and tone deaf by airing his grievances publicly during the season. A few appreciated LaPorta's candor.
Coach Dan Campbell seemed annoyed by being repeatedly asked questions about LaPorta's comments during a press conference last Friday. LaPorta later clarified his comments when meeting with the media. He stated that he prefers to remain with the Lions.
LaPorta was a non-factor in the Lions' passing game until the final drive during Sunday's 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers . He finished with one reception for 18 yards on two targets. LaPorta isn't showing any ill effects from the herniated disc in his back, which he suffered nine games into last season, that required surgery, although it was his quietest game since early in the 2024 season. Despite the slow day, LaPorta is on pace for 79 receptions, a career-high 946 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.
LaPorta is making $5.8 million in the final year of his four-year rookie deal. Contract extension talks between the Lions and Jack Bechta, LaPorta's agent, broke off about three weeks ago. The Lions are typically among the NFL 's most proactive teams in locking up core players before their rookie contracts expire.
Bectha also represents Tucker Kraft , who is the latest relevant data point in the tight end market. Kraft, a 2023 third-round pick, received a four-year, $75 million contract extension from the Packers a day before the regular season started. The torn right ACL Kraft suffered during the middle of the 2025 season didn't deter the Packers from doing the deal.
At $18.75 million per year, Kraft is the NFL's third-highest-paid tight end. Incentives and salary escalators totaling $17 million make this $18.75 million-per-year deal worth as much as $23 million per year. Kraft's 2028 through 2030 base salaries each increase by as much as $4.25 million annually based on his statistical performance, playtime and honors earned in the previous season. There are $4.25 million of incentives in 2030 also based on Kraft's statistical performance, playtime and honors earned during that season.
For example, Kraft's 2028 base salary increases by $500,000 with at least 75 receptions in 2027. It's another $250,000 increase for hitting 85 receptions and an additional $250,000 for a total of $1 million with 95 or more receptions. Getting 800, 950, and 1,100 receiving yards generates the same escalation amounts. There are three levels with receiving touchdowns of at least seven, nine and 10 for $250,000 apiece. Having 80% or more offensive playtime is worth $500,000. Reaching 85% and 92% playtime is worth an extra $250,000, respectively. There's also a $250,000 increase for being selected to the Pro Bowl (on the original ballot) and another $250,000 for being named first team All-Pro by the Associated Press. It's the same criteria and dollar amounts as with the annual salary escalators for the 2030 incentives.
Bechta is undoubtedly using Kraft's contract as a measuring stick for LaPorta. There is a parallel between the Christian Gonzalez/Devon Witherspoon situation and LaPorta's. The $33 million per year deal Reggie Johnson got from the Seattle Seahawks for Witherspoon in the middle of August to move the cornerback market set the table for Gonzalez, another one of his clients, to sign a $33.75 million per year extension with the New England Patriots , resetting this market again in early September as the start of the regular season was approaching.
LaPorta has been the more productive of the two tight ends. He set a single-season rookie record for a tight end in 2023, with 86 receptions, a record broken the following year by Brock Bowers . Those receptions went for 889 yards and 10 touchdowns.   LaPorta was named to the Pro Bowl and earned second-team All-Pro honors in the process. Kraft's career highs of 50 catches, 707 receiving yards and seven touchdown receptions were in 2024.
LaPorta has 214 receptions for 2,438 yards with 23 touchdowns in 48 career games, while Kraft has 142 catches, 1,848 receiving yards, and 17 receiving touchdowns in 49 career games. Since entering the NFL in 2023, LaPorta ranks third and fourth, respectively, among tight ends in touchdown receptions and receiving yards.
Bectha is probably targeting more than just a nominal increase over his Kraft deal with LaPorta. It wouldn't be surprising for Bechta to look at how much of Kraft's performance bonuses LaPorta would earn based on him consistently performing like he did as a rookie in 2023. LaPorta's rookie season shouldn't be considered as a statistical outlier. His projected 2026 production is comparable to 2023's.
LaPorta would earn $86 million under Kraft's contract, using his rookie 2023 season as a baseline for future performance. A $21.5 million per year LaPorta deal would essentially be a 12.5% increase of the tight end market. George Kittle , another Bechta client, is the current standard with the backloaded four-year, $76.4 million extension averaging $19.1 million per year he signed with the San Francisco 49ers in April 2025.
Presumably, Bechta is insisting on establishing new tight-end benchmarks for overall guarantees and for the amount fully guaranteed at signing. Those are Trey McBride 's $43 million in the four-year, $76 million extension, averaging $19 million per year he signed with the Arizona Cardinals in 2025 about three weeks before Kittle and the $36 million in the three-year, $53 million deal Kyle Pitts , who was designated as a franchise player for $15 million, received from the Atlanta Falcons during June.
It remains to be seen whether LaPorta's outburst will spur additional contract talks this season. Notwithstanding LaPorta's clarification, usually the longer a player incurs the risk of injury and poor performance in a contract year, the more he will want to test the open market unless his contract demands are met. That's something the Lions may want to consider with LaPorta.
LaPorta's comments prompted some media speculation that he could be dealt before the trade deadline. It should be noted that the Lions opted against making a substantial tight end investment in T.J. Hockenson . He was dealt to the Minnesota Vikings, an NFC North divisional rival, at the 2022 trade deadline instead. Getting rid of LaPorta this season would create a big hole in Detroit's offense. Tyler Conklin and Brock Wright are LaPorta's primary backups at tight end.
Detroit balking at Bechta's demands could open the door to LaPorta becoming an unrestricted free agent in 2027. If the Lions plan on keeping LaPorta and fellow 2023 second-round pick safety Brian Branch , who just returned from the right Achilles tendon he tore late last season, one of two has to be signed to a new deal before the 15-day franchise tag designation period expires next March 3.
Using a franchise tag would be a major departure for the Lions. The last usage was in 2018 on edge rusher Ziggy Ansah.
Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement's formula for non-exclusive franchise tags, the 2027 tight end number is projected to be 4.998% of the 2027 salary cap. That's slightly up from this year's 4.995%.
The 2027 tight end franchise tag should be $16.169 million, with next year's salary cap…

title: Josh Downs landing spots after Colts WR reportedly asks out, Indy continues fire sale
summary: Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal and drawing trade interest
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have been busy this week, selling notable pieces ahead of the trade deadline, including offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. The NFL world has now turned its attention to running back Jonathan Taylor as the next Colt that could be dealt, but there's another weapon to watch in Indy.
Wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal and has reportedly fetched interest from multiple teams. With the Colts rebuilding, he seems to want out now.
"It is what it is," Downs told reporters in the Colts locker room on Wednesday, per The Athletic . "I'm here today, but whatever comes my way comes my way."
#Colts WR Josh Downs on trade rumors: “It is what it is. I’m here today, but whatever comes my way comes my way.” Did he request a trade? “Like I said, I’m open to whatever. Whatever comes my way comes my way.” “I’m here right now. I’m where my feet are. …” pic.twitter.com/pgZnRw9GID
Downs has caught 26 passes for a team-high 307 yards and zero touchdowns in seven games this season. He and Keenan Allen , along with tight end Tyler Warren , have been shouldering the load in the passing game with Alec Pierce sidelined by an ankle injury.
The North Carolina product was selected by the Colts in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft . Downs' 1,964 receiving yards from the slot since he was drafted rank second in the NFL, trailing only Amon-Ra St. Brown of the Detroit Lions , per CBS Sports Research. Downs' best season came in 2024, when he caught a career-high 72 passes for 803 yards and five touchdowns. In 54 career games played, he's caught 224 passes for 2,447 yards and 11 touchdowns.
With Downs wanting out of Indianapolis, let's explore a few potential landing spots for him.
The Los Angeles Rams are a surprising 3-4 and have become just the fifth outright preseason Super Bowl favorite in the past 50 seasons to have a losing record through seven games. None of the previous four made the Super Bowl.
Now, injuries are beginning to mount in LA, and that includes Davante Adams , who was just placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Only one wide receiver other than Puka Nacua caught a pass in the Rams' Week 7 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders , and that was Konata Mumpfield . We know Sean McVay loves his tight ends, but adding Downs would help Matthew Stafford and this passing offense.
Reuniting Drake Maye with his top college wideout makes sense. In 2022, Downs led the Tar Heels with 94 catches for 1,029 yards and 11 of Maye's 38 passing touchdowns. The New England Patriots do boast a top-10 passing attack, averaging 253.0 yards per game, but Romeo Doubs is on injured reserve, and A.J. Brown does not look completely healthy after missing time with a high ankle sprain. Brown has caught just three passes in each of his three games this season. Tight end Hunter Henry is Maye's top target this year with 296 yards and two touchdowns on 26 receptions.
Michael Penix Jr . has been great since making his 2026 debut, and he just became the fourth quarterback in Atlanta Falcons history to throw for 200 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions in consecutive games when the Falcons upset the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers . Drake London has been a monster, catching 38 passes for 616 yards and one touchdown in seven games played, but he's accounted for 29.4% of Atlanta's targets in the passing game. Free-agent addition Jahan Dotson has caught just 12 passes through seven weeks, and Zachariah Branch is behind him with 10 receptions. The Falcons could stand to make an addition at wide receiver as they continue this push for the NFC South.
When the Kansas City Chiefs signed Kenneth Walker III in free agency, it was believed he was going to make life so much easier for guys like Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton . However, Rice is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury. Worthy has caught just 24 passes for 217 yards and one touchdown, and Thornton is on injured reserve with an ankle injury. A 37-year-old Travis Kelce should not be Kansas City's leading receiver.
The Chiefs are coming off an embarrassing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , in which the offense registered zero explosive plays and zero trips to the red zone. Adding another weapon for Mahomes is necessary if the Chiefs want to return to the Super Bowl.
The Raiders may have the worst wide receiver room in the NFL. There's Tre Tucker , who has caught 29 passes for 474 yards and four touchdowns, and then Cody White , Jalen Nailor , Jack Bech and Dareke Young , all of whom haven't crossed 115 yards receiving through seven weeks. The Raiders somehow have a top-four passing attack with Brock Bowers , Ashton Jeanty, and Michael Mayer shouldering the load.
Downs is not only someone who could come in and contribute immediately for Kirk Cousins , but also someone who could pick up an extension and stay in the fold long-term. Vegas has really struggled to add receivers in the draft.

title: Jonathan Taylor's wife speaks out on Colts trade rumors: 'My mind is spiraling'
summary: Indianapolis dealt Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, leaving the star running back's family wondering if he is the next veteran on the move before the Nov. 10 trade deadline
full_text:
The Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away, and one of the best players who may or may not be available is Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor .
The trade rumors around Taylor picked up steam on Tuesday, when the 2-5 Colts traded two of their other best players away in offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . The Colts have already fired general manager Chris Ballard. Could the team be holding a fire sale?
These developments have apparently put Taylor's family on edge. His wife, Ayanna, has been posting about trade rumors on social media, and says it already feels like she's on a different team since the Colts traded away wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and linebacker Zaire Franklin this offseason. However, Nelson getting traded this week has her wondering if she should start packing her bags.
"But now Chris Ballard gets fired, Quenton Nelson is traded, is literally anybody safe on this team?" Ayanna said on Instagram. "I've never known the Colts organization without these people, and it kind of feels like rookie year all over again. So naturally, my mind is spiraling.
"Is this the start of the trading frenzy? What does this mean for my husband and I? Do I need to start packing our bags? Are we even going to be spending our daughter's first Halloween together? Will we make it to game day, or was last week the last time my husband will be putting on a Colts jersey? ...
Jonathan Taylor's wife on Instagram: "Is literally anyone safe on this team? It feels like rookie year all over again. My mind is spiraling. What does this mean for my husband and I? Do I need to start packing our bags? Are we going to be spending our daughter's first Halloween… pic.twitter.com/w2jcOpWh7h
This was not the first video Ayanna has made chronicling Indy's current situation. She has even laid out the timeline of the Colts' fall from grace. Jonathan Taylor doesn't have a problem with her speaking her mind, and he was even asked about the videos following the Colts' Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .
"I think it's been out there already, so I think her adding [to it] doesn't really change anything," Taylor said, via The Athletic . "You know everybody's on TikTok these days. So, you just have to come into work and stay focused."
Taylor joined the Colts as a second-round pick out of Wisconsin in the 2020 NFL Draft . His 8,185 rushing yards rank second in franchise history behind Edgerrin James, while his 77 rushing touchdowns rank first. Despite the Colts' struggles this season, Taylor has been productive on the ground. His 587 yards rushing through seven games rank fifth in the NFL, and his eight rushing touchdowns are tied for first.
Unlike Nelson and Buckner, Taylor is signed through 2028 and would be a massive addition for a contender if the price is right. Some teams that could be interested? According to CBS Sports' Zach Pereles , the Seahawks, Broncos and Giants could be good landing spots for the running back.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Saquon Barkley trade rumors: Should the Seahawks trade for the Eagles' running back?
summary: Here are the pros and cons of a Barkley trade for the defending Super Bowl champs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks opted not to franchise tag their top running back last season and ended up losing him to free agency. Kenneth Walker III was named Super Bowl MVP in February and shortly after joined the Kansas City Chiefs , leaving the defending champs with big shoes to fill.
They have yet to fill those shoes effectively.
Running back Zach Charbonnet is still recovering from a torn ACL he sustained last season, and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price is on IR with a chest injury. Injuries aside, the Seahawks don't have the level of talent they did in Walker last season. But one name floating around the trade deadline conversation could fix Seattle's run game woes.
Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley could find a new home, and the Seahawks are certainly a team that makes sense. Let's take a look at the case for and against trading for Barkley.
The Seahawks aren't playing as well as they hoped after their Super Bowl win in 2025. The team was sitting at .500 heading into Week 7, and a victory over the Chiefs on "Sunday Night Football" put some spark in their struggling offense. What would give them even more of a spark is a stronger run game.
After trading away Walker, their ground game is a shell of what it was. Quarterback Sam Darnold has struggled with interceptions, tied for second-most in the league (7) through Week 6. Without a strong run game, quarterbacks can be forced to throw the ball, feeling they have limited options, and that pressure can lead to poor decision-making. If Darnold has a strong running back, the entire offense would feel the impact, and defenses would be forced to game-plan for a player who can make something into nothing on the ground.
We have seen what value the combination of wide receiver Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Walker did last season, which got them all the way to a Lombardi Trophy. Adding Barkley could greatly increase the team's playoff chances.
Adding Barkley solves two problems with one player. The Seahawks would get the clear RB1 they've been missing, and the Eagles can get future picks to begin building with some youth.
Currently, the Seahawks' run game ranks second-worst in EPA per rush. Seattle just shored up its offensive line with the addition of Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . Now's a great time to add to that offensive unit.
Barkley is a solid RB1, but he does have some cons. He's older, and he does have a history of injuries. To the over-29 crowd reading this, take no offense, you're certainly not old, but for a running back, 29 is up there. Backs typically have a short career, so 29 is older in the running back world than it is for everyone else.
Now let's get to the injury part. He already missed two games due to injury this season. He isn't the most injury-prone RB out there, but as he ages, the chances of missing games will only go up.
Another reason not to trade for Barkley is that the Seahawks already have a young core of running backs they can build around. They will be getting Charbonnet and Price back soon and can see what their offense can look like with them.
Then we have Barkley's price. CBS Sports' own Carter Bahns says one version of this deal could involve the Eagles receiving Emanuel Wilson , a 2027 third-round pick, and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
Even if the Seahawks don't make a playoff run this year, the team would still be just two years removed from a championship next season. The quarterback and head coach should be the same, and they could make another run in 2027. Adding future draft picks allows them to add the pieces they need through the draft, rather than through an aging running back.
This is a trade I can see happening. The Seahawks just lost their MVP running back and desperately need to find a replacement. While Barkley won't be at Walker's level and likely doesn't have as many years left in the NFL , he provides the stability needed and perhaps even the chance at another Super Bowl appearance. They can strike while the iron is hot.
The Seahawks' run game is struggling, while in Kansas City, Walker is leading the league in rushing yards. Through six weeks, Seattle had 643 total rushing yards (107.2 yards per game), and Walker had them beat in total yards despite playing one fewer game, with 665 yards (113.0 per game). It wasn't until the Chiefs played Seattle that that changed. The numbers don't lie and show just how much of a hit losing Walker was. The Seahawks have a chance to correct the mistake of letting him walk out the door.
Now to the Eagles' side of things.
Their season isn't over, but even if they win the NFC East, which looks about as rough as it can get right now, it's hard to envision them making it past the first round of the playoffs. They may be willing to send Barkley elsewhere to load up on picks for the future or on younger players.
Philly may even be looking for a new head coach soon, with Nick Sirianni among the coaches in the league on the hot seat . Keeping future picks could be part of working toward a rebuild that I envision coming sooner than later.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Chiefs sign former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker after Harrison Butker struggles
summary: Tucker is back with a team for the first time since 2024
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are adding a new kicker to their roster following Harrison Butker's struggles . The team is signing former eight-time All-Pro and Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz confirmed.
Tucker last played for the Ravens on Jan. 19, 2025, and is regarded as one of the best kickers in NFL history. He's a seven-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl XLVII champion, and he owns NFL records for the fastest kicker to reach 300 career field goals and fastest kicker to score 1,000 points. He owned the longest field goal at 66 yards before the record was broken by Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little at 67 and 68 yards. His signing was first reported by the Kansas City Star .
NFL Media reports that the Chiefs worked out three kickers this week. They elected to sign Tucker over former Los Angeles Rams kicker Harrison Mevis , but there are some questions that come with this addition.
The Ravens released Tucker in May 2025, about four months after disturbing allegations came to light . In January of that year, The Baltimore Banner reported that Tucker had been accused by six different women of engaging in sexually inappropriate misconduct at multiple Baltimore-area spas. The number eventually grew to 16 accusers across eight spas in Baltimore. Tucker was accused of exposing his erect genitals during sessions and touching the therapists inappropriately. He was suspended for the first 10 games of the 2025 season for violating the league's personal conduct policy, but went unsigned after.
Tucker previously worked out for multiple teams, including the Indianapolis Colts , New Orleans Saints and New York Jets , but never signed a deal. In his career, the 36-year-old Tucker has converted on 89.1% of his field goals. His 417 made field goals rank 14th all-time.
This addition comes after Butker has missed six total kicks on the season, including one extra point. In Week 7's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , Butker missed a 58-yard field goal at the end of the first half and then a 45-yard field goal in the fourth quarter.
"He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football," said Chiefs head coach Andy Reid of Butker postgame. "He's off a bit, so gotta fix it."
Butker's struggles have come mostly from long range, as he's 9-of-10 this year from inside 50 yards. Still, Kansas City has been leaving points on the board.
While Butker is the Chiefs' kicker for now, the addition of Tucker to the practice squad sends a message that's hard to ignore.

title: Predicting the full 14-team NFL playoff bracket entering Week 8: Cowboys steal NFC East, Bills make Super Bowl
summary: The Bills in the Super Bowl? Here's our playoff projection heading into Week 8
full_text:
The NFL is the most unpredictable sports league on the planet, and we got a good taste of that in Week 7 with TWO undefeated teams going down ( 49ers and Chiefs ).
Last week, we had those two teams projected to land the top seeds in the AFC and NFC, but our projection has now been turned upside down. So who's going to earn the top seed in each conference? Glad you asked.
To help us figure out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 165 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
The AFC playoff projection underwent some massive changes this week. Thanks to the Chiefs' loss in Week 7, the Bills are now projected to earn the No. 1 overall seed in the AFC.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Bills (5-1) -- AFC East champion 2. Chiefs (5-1) -- AFC West champion 3. Jaguars (4-2) -- AFC South champion 4. Bengals (4-2) -- AFC North champion 5. Broncos (4-2) 6. Steelers (5-2) 7. Ravens (4-3) JUST MISSED: Patriots (4-3), Browns (5-2)
Besides the Bills moving up to the top, the other notable change here is that the Bengals are now projected to win the AFC North. The Bengals made history in Week 7 by becoming the first team in 75 years to win a game by at least 20 points after trailing by at least 13 points at halftime. One thing working in the Bengals' favor is their schedule. They only have to play one more road game against a team that currently has a winning record (Browns in Week 13).
Speaking of the Browns, they haven't won a division title since 1989, and our computer model doesn't see that drought ending this year. Our projection has them finishing 8-9 and out of the playoffs.
Last week, the 49ers were projected to get the No. 1 overall seed in the NFC, but after San Francisco's loss, that honor now belongs to the Vikings , who just happen to be the only undefeated team left in the NFL.
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Vikings (6-0) -- NFC North champion 2. 49ers (6-1) -- NFC West champion 3. Falcons (3-4) -- NFC South champion 4. Cowboys (3-4) -- NFC East champion 5. Lions (4-2) 6. Seahawks (4-3) 7. Bears (5-2) JUST MISSED: Packers (4-3), Rams (3-4)
Besides the Vikings moving up to the top, the other notable change here is that the Cowboys are now projected to win the NFC East. This marks the first time all season that we've had the Cowboys projected to finish at the top of the division. Our model basically views the NFC East as a two-horse race between the Cowboys and Giants, with Dallas given a 38.5% chance to win the division and the Giants RIGHT behind them at 37.3%. One thing working in the Cowboys' favor is that they have the fourth-easiest remaining strength of schedule.
Based on the current NFL playoff standings, the NFC North has ALL FOUR TEAMS in the playoffs heading into Week 8, but our projection doesn't think that will hold. For that to happen, the NFC North would have to earn all three wild card spots, but we have the Seahawks getting in, which means one NFC North team will be staying at home come playoff time. In this case, that's the Packers. Sorry, cheeseheads.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Vikings) and two teams (49ers and Chiefs) that have faced each other in two of the past seven Super Bowls.
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.
As you can see, this is the first time all season that the Bills have been projected to win the Super Bowl. According to our model, the Bills have a 12.97% chance of winning it all, with the Vikings sitting right behind them at 11.15%. There are only three other teams higher than 8%. That's the Chiefs (9.5%), 49ers (8.4%) and Jaguars (8.3%).

Then, in my locks of the week, I went 2-3 ATS, which brings me to 17-17-1 ATS on the year. That's the definition of middling.
It's not bad necessarily. I could own a losing record with my locks, but let's remember what they're supposed to be -- LOCKS! We've been burned by a fair share of bad beats throughout the first half of the season and lost by the hook last week in our Vikings pick against the Colts , but there's no room for excuses. It's time to roll up our sleeves and get to work with an eye towards a more productive Week 8, which, as always, begins with my five locks of the week.
Note : New Orleans, New York ( Giants ), San Francisco, and Houston are on the bye in Week 8.
The Colts are on the doorstep of selling off parts amid a 2-5 start to the year, which includes a three-game losing skid entering Week 8. It's hard to see a scenario where things change for the better this weekend, as they'll head to Jacksonville to face a 4-2 Jaguars team that'll be fresh off its bye week. Coming into this slate, the Colts have a claim to be one of the worst offenses in the NFL .
Their 4.5 yards-per-play average is tied for the worst in the league with the Eagles , and a large part of those issues lies at quarterback. Daniel Jones has yet to rekindle the version of himself from the first half of last year and has thrown an interception in all but one game so far in 2026. Jones ranks 31st out of 33 eligible quarterbacks in passer rating this season, while his EPA per dropback ranks 30th. Among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts this year, Jones is tied for the second-highest turnover-worth-per-throw rate.
He now faces a Jaguars pass defense that is just outside the top-10 in the league with an 87.7 passer rating allowed. They're also tied for the third-most interceptions (7) in the league. Conversely, you have Trevor Lawrence playing like an MVP candidate and should face little resistance from a Colts defense that has just two interceptions on the year.
Projected score : Jaguars 33, Colts 20 The pick : Jaguars -7.5
The Bengals showed us their potential during their 35-point second-half outburst in the win over Baltimore. If anything close to that version of the Bengals is on the field on Sunday, Tennessee doesn't have a puncher's chance of keeping this close. Their passing offense doesn't have the ceiling to go toe-to-toe with Joe Burrow , as the club ranks 29th in passer rating and is tied for last in yards per attempt.
While Cincinnati's offense garners much of the headlines, the Bengals' defense has been an underrated unit this season and was a key reason they were able to endure an offense-free first half in Week 7. Zac Taylor's defense has the third-best red zone efficiency (35% touchdown rate) in the NFL. That matches up well against a Tennessee red zone offense that scores a touchdown on just 47.4% of trips (27th in the NFL).
Projected score : Bengals 35, Titans 21 The pick : Bengals -10.5
In theory, the Chargers would've spent the bye week figuring out what has gone wrong over their 0-6 start to the year and come out firing in Week 8, where they'll technically be the road team but will be in their home stadium as they face the Rams at SoFi Stadium. I just don't see them putting together much of a fight, however.
Justin Herbert has been among the worst quarterbacks in the league so far this season and comes into Week 8 with a league-high 5.6% turnover-worthy throw rate. While the Rams haven't generated many turnovers, they have five interceptions on the year, showing they are more than capable of taking advantage of any opportunity Herbert gives them. The Rams are also giving up just 186.3 passing yards per game this season, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. No matter which way you slice it, it should be tough sledding for Herbert in this matchup.
That means Matthew Stafford likely won't have to do much heavy lifting to clear this 6.5-point spread. That's especially true considering that the Chargers can be taken advantage of on the ground. They're allowing 123.8 rushing yards per game, so this could be a matchup where Kyren Williams and Blake Corum become the focal point of the attack. That backfield duo is coming off a win against the Raiders where they each went for over 90 yards rushing to go along with a touchdown. It wouldn't be shocking to see similar production on Sunday.
Projected score : Rams 30, Chargers 17 The pick : Rams -6.5
The Dolphins finally got into the win column for the first time all season with a road win against the Jets . While that's great for Jeff Hafley's club to get off the schneid, I don't see the momentum from that victory turning into a two-game winning streak. Since Mike Vrabel became the head coach, New England is 8-4-1 ATS on the road. As a road favorite in games, they are 3-2 ATS with an average margin of victory of 13 points.
While they'll be on the road, the Patriots have the rest advantage in this game after playing last Thursday. They're also simply the better team. Miami is allowing 5.7 yards per play this season and 7.8 yards per pass attempt (tied for third-highest in the NFL). Drake Maye should continue to find success through the air against a Dolphins secondary that is allowing a league-high 116.8 passer rating against. So long as they don't shoot themselves in the foot, this should be a double-digit victory for New England.
Projected score : Patriots 30, Dolphins 20 The pick : Patriots -7.5
The Philadelphia Eagles have been ravaged by injuries, and they aren't getting any reprieve on the schedule either. After playing on Monday night, the Eagles will head on the road for a short week to face a Commanders team coming off its bye week. That's as lopsided a rest advantage as you'll find in the NFL this season.
The Commanders did lose No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin for the season due to a torn patellar tendon he suffered in Week 6. While the offense does take a hit in his absence, there are guys who can step up. Along with Stefon Diggs , rookie wideout Antonio Williams has flashed potential, while veteran tight end Chig Okonkwo has been an underutilized piece of the offense that I expect will see more work down the stretch.
Washington's defense won't be mistaken for one of the best units in the league, but I think they should be able to keep Tanner McKee in check. That's especially true after watching Saquon Barkley on Monday night, as the Eagles running back was clearly limited with a hamstring injury. If he suits up on Sunday, it's hard to imagine he'll be any healthier, capping the ceiling of the Eagles offense. Philadelphia is also 0-2 ATS on the road so far this season with a -8.0 average margin of victory.
