title: Cowboys news: Javonte Williams on his near retirement before signing with Dallas
summary: The running game of the Dallas Cowboys has been a positive for them for the most part since the beginning of last season, but the addition of Javonte Williams nearly didn’t happen. Dallas is making a change when it comes to their green dot on defense, and the person assigned to it is only in […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The running game of the Dallas Cowboys has been a positive for them for the most part since the beginning of last season, but the addition of Javonte Williams nearly didn’t happen. Dallas is making a change when it comes to their green dot on defense, and the person assigned to it is only in his second season. The Cowboys beat the Eagles on Monday night, and the film showed they accomplished it in several different ways. Also, a well-known pass rusher has been linked to Dallas as the trade deadline approaches. Dallas Cowboys RB Javonte Williams Admits Contemplating Retirement Before ‘Rebirth’ – Mike Moraitis, SI.com Javonte Williams rejuvenated his career in 2025 with the Cowboys. However, it almost didn’t happen as he considered hanging up the cleats. Williams entered the league as a second-round pick of the Denver Broncos in 2022, but after having success in his rookie campaign, Williams struggled with injury and ineffectiveness over his final three seasons in Denver. He would eventually sign a prove-it deal with the Cowboys, but before that, Williams said he thought about retiring. “I was really about to just hang up the cleats,” Williams said on the Downs 2 Business podcast. The Dallas Cowboys made a major change to the defensive lineup and it’s here to stay, but the new starter has a lot to fix – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Linebacker Shemar James is the new green dot on the Cowboys’ defense. With that said, he needs to improve in one particular area. What the film shows from Shemar James First things first, the positives. We’ve known James can move fast. He’s explosive, and he can look like a blur on film. You don’t really appreciate how fast he’s moving until you turn on the tape. He’s solid in coverage and appears to have a strong understanding of Christian Parker’s scheme. But what stands out the most is that the Cowboys need him to be better in the hole. You need your middle linebacker coming forward and making plays. Download the SB Nation app today! Tape Talk: Cowboys offense finds their rhythm, defense takes away big plays vs. Eagles – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dallas was able to get a much-needed win against Philadelphia on Monday night. They did so by playing competently on both sides of the ball. Tip the cap to Dallas’ offensive line, tight ends What shows up in the box score is the Cowboys running 38 times for 204 yards, led by Javonte Williams’ career-best 155 yard day. What really pops when you watch the tape back is how well the offensive line and tight ends blocked Philadelphia’s front, their best rushing performance up front all season. The Eagles’ offense was banged up, but their defense still had their stars like Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis and Zack Baun playing. The Cowboys were able to get consistent push over the course of the night, and Williams was not tackled behind the line of scrimmage once in the game because of how well the front blocked for him. Cowboys stopped making the same Jake Ferguson mistake (and it paid off) – Jason Kandel, The Landry Hat Jake Ferguson has had his struggles in 2026. As a result, the Cowboys are looking for other answers at tight end. After he tipped the game-losing interception right to Alex Anzalone in the loss to the Bucs, Cowboys fans have been waiting for Brian Schottenheimer to see the light and move Ferguson more to the shadows in favor of Spann-Ford, who is a better run blocker , costs less, and isn’t much worse as a pass-catcher. Ferguson’s route participation has been down in each of the last two weeks, and it was this week that it paid off. The offense exploded in a game where Ferguson’s drops or fumbles did not have an impact, and while it was against an Eagles defense that has struggled, early returns are encouraging. Dallas Cowboys Trade Rumor Tracker: Latest News & Buzz Entering NFL Trade Deadline – Josh Sanchez, SI.com The Cowboys need help rushing the passer. Veteran edge rusher Josh Sweat has been continously linked to them as of late. Josh Sweat, EDGE, Arizona Cardinals The buzz linking Dallas and Sweat has grown leaps and bounds in recent weeks, and it’s a deal that makes a lot of sense for both sides. The Cardinals appear poised to enter a complete rebuild after trading away star wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and Sweat is a veteran piece who can land a solid return. In Dallas, Sweat would return to a division that he is familiar with thanks to his time with the Philadelphia Eagles, and he would also be joining a unit led by Christian Parker, who was on the staff in Philly during Sweat’s tenure.

title: Roster moves that are showing up more for the Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys front office has faced its fair share of criticism over the years, with the criticism aimed at not doing enough to improve their roster. These complaints aren’t as plentiful this year as the team has been extremely diligent in trying to do everything they can to fix the team. While not every […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 8: Otito Ogbonnia #91 of the Dallas Cowboys takes the field against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers prior to an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys front office has faced its fair share of criticism over the years, with the criticism aimed at not doing enough to improve their roster. These complaints aren’t as plentiful this year as the team has been extremely diligent in trying to do everything they can to fix the team. While not every new piece has worked out as planned, there are many who are living up to, if not exceeding, expectations. And in recent games, some of these same players keep showing up. Here are some of the smart moves the Cowboys have made over the last year, who played well on Monday night and are slowly becoming a more permanent fixture of this football team. Go big Why are we still discussing Quinnen Williams? It’s because people will forever debate the Micah Parsons trade, especially when every new loss, coupled with a Green Bay win, makes fans question it more. Fortunately, Williams is starting to ball out. His presence was felt in all aspects of the game. He blew up a goal-line run, he sniffed out a screen and ran down the ball carrier, and he came up with another sack. He now has three sacks in his last four games. He also has nine tackles for a loss this year, the most by any defensive tackle. Williams is starting to produce in the way that was envisioned. Quinnen Williams leads all defensive tackles with nine tackles for a loss this year. Only edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. has more. Williams' career high is 12 during his All-Pro season in 2022. pic.twitter.com/Up3RNLP6JW — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) October 27, 2026 Another trade Most everyone approved of the trade for Joey Porter Jr. as he is a proven commodity. Some questioned the second-round cost, however, that pick is not until 2028, so it is not as steep as it sounds. But now, he is already looking like a steal. He is smothering everything, always attached to his man. His coverage fundamentals are top notch and he puts more great plays on display each week. His future with the team is unknown, but it is becoming more and more apparent that he should be a part of this team going forward, especially with the unexpected decline of DaRon Bland. #Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. has been outstanding since joining the team. He is every target in his three games with Dallas: pic.twitter.com/E3z7JKgij5 — Marcus Mosher (@Marcus_Mosher) October 27, 2026 The free agent steal Otito Ogbonnia has emerged as the team’s most consistent interior presence against the run and best offseason addition this year. Despite playing on a modest one-year deal, he has become one of the best run-stopping defensive tackles in the league. Initially thought of as a block absorber, his hand usage and lateral range have turned him into a block-shedding run stuffer. He’s making stops consistently to the point where it’s now an expected result. Among all NFL defensive interior linemen with over 100 snaps played against the run, Cowboys DT Otito Ogbonnia has the highest run-stop rate (13.0%). — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) October 27, 2026 The last-second re-up One of the team’s biggest surprises comes from a player who was already on the roster, but who has stepped into a larger role. The Cowboys gave Brevyn Spann-Ford a three-year extension right before the season began, and with each new day it looks like a better and better investment. He has been a pesky in-line blocker sealing running lanes off the edge, but he is also becoming more involved as a receiver as another safety net for Dak Prescott. He is also a key member on special teams. He is just a gritty player who shows up every game. The right backup The Cowboys have tried all kinds of things in an attempt to find a backup running back. The team was hoping second-year backs Jaydon Blue or Phil Mafah would be the guys, but they did not make the final roster. Malik Davis was that feel-good riser in camp, but an unfortunate hip injury ended his season a week before the year began. The Cowboys then claimed former Chiefs back Emari Demercado who hung around for two games, but have since pivoted to former Falcons back Tyler Goodson. It has taken a bit, but the Cowboys might have finally found a reliable backup. Since joining the team, Goodson has looked good as a high-efficiency change-of-pace runner, offering the offense an explosive element of suddenness out of the backfield. While Javonte Williams handles the heavy interior grinding, Goodson has shown nice vision to attack the perimeter on outside-zone concepts. His one-cut burst and quick acceleration allow him to get through tight creases both as a running back and as a reliable return specialist filling in for KaVontae Turpin. Swinging into action Acquired from Pittsburgh to serve as a versatile swing tackle, Broderick Jones is slowly working into the mix. He has been used in heavy-run personnel looks, specifically when the Cowboys deploy him as an eligible sixth offensive lineman. In these alignments, he gives the coaching staff incredible flexibility by shifting smoothly between the left and right sides of the line. Monday night was his best showing so far as he logged nine offensive snaps as a sixth lineman. He was quick off the snap, locked onto his man and twisted him out of the play. He also did a good job climbing to the second level to take out the linebacker. It was a small sample, but he did a good job helping the Cowboys reignite their running game against a tough Eagles front. Broderick Jones played just 9 snaps (all runs), but he helped spring some good runs, including a key 4th down conversion. It was a good game for all the former Pittsburgh trade guys. pic.twitter.com/RrbqUYQmkB — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) October 27, 2026 Don’t forget about this guy This spot would go to Jonathan Bullard had he not injured his calf in Week 3 as he was showing up as a reliable run-stopper perfect for this defensive scheme. Oddly enough, the Cowboys immediately replaced him with veteran Elijah Garcia, and the interior defensive line has not missed a beat. The team wants to keep their main three DTs fresh and having a reliable guy helps them do that, but nobody was expecting Garcia to step in and make an impact. By taking calculated risks and identifying talent that fits the current system, the front office has effectively added key pieces to their roster, both at crucial starting spots and valuable depth pieces. These acquisitions have helped give this team a fighting chance. The Cowboys still have a lot to figure out, but even if some of their initial roster adds don’t pan out, they still have a slew of guys who they can build around.

title: Brian Schottenheimer’s Cowboys offense desperately needs one thing
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Monday night. Given that it was a Monday there is very little time to dwell on it before the next one arrives. Dwelling on anything is hardly wise, but the past can offer help for how to navigate the future. Future opponents will hardly be as depleted […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Monday night. Given that it was a Monday there is very little time to dwell on it before the next one arrives. Dwelling on anything is hardly wise, but the past can offer help for how to navigate the future. Future opponents will hardly be as depleted as the Philadelphia Eagles were on Monday night, but still some of the things that Dallas did can and should be taken into future contests. There is one thing specifically that stands out. The Cowboys offense desperately needs balance Javonte Williams carried the ball 25 times for the Cowboys in the City of Brotherly Love. He churned out 155 rushing yards which was good for his career high. It is not hard to see that the commitment to the run game really helped. Football requires balance in a number of ways and a heavier focus on the ground meant a lesser one on the aerial attack. Dak Prescott is a very talented quarterback, but asking him to throw it a ton of times like he did a week before against the Green Bay Packers is hardly a recipe for success. All told Prescott threw 27 passes in Philadelphia and as it was south of 30 it made me wonder – how often lately has Dak come in below 30 pass attempts in a game? Stathead to the rescue . Monday night was Prescott’s 24th game with Brian Schottenheimer as his offensive play-caller, and it was only the third instance in which he did not throw at least 30 passes in a given game. What’s more is that one of the other two was last season’s finale, a meaningless contest against the New York Giants. This means that there are now only two games of consequence where the Cowboys and Schottenheimer did not have Prescott hit at least 30 attempts in a game. These are the last 12 games in which Prescott was below 30 attempts per game, that was just where I cut off the screenshot and it was not for any specific reason, and you can see that this phenomenon was quite common in 2022. It was in 2023 when this became less prevalent. You can almost see where the Cowboys defense stopped being a point of reliability. That required Dak and the offense to have to score more, and the overall domino effect has taken us to our current moment in time. The point here is that the Cowboys must find a way to be more balanced offensively. As noted it isn’t sustainable for Dak to throw 30 passes a game and have everything work out. Javonte Williams doesn’t have to set a career high every week, but the running game absolutely has to be a factor.

title: Cowboys vs Eagles one big takeaway: Javonte Williams finally got the workload he deserved
summary: The Cowboys ran over Philadelphia in Week 7, after six weeks of the Dallas Cowboys struggling to establish a consistent running game. That inconsistency left QB Dak Prescott to carry an offense that too often became predictable. On Monday night, Brian Schottenheimer finally committed to a different approach, and Javonte Williams showed exactly what this […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cowboys ran over Philadelphia in Week 7, after six weeks of the Dallas Cowboys struggling to establish a consistent running game. That inconsistency left QB Dak Prescott to carry an offense that too often became predictable. On Monday night, Brian Schottenheimer finally committed to a different approach, and Javonte Williams showed exactly what this offense can look like when Dallas gives its running back room to work. Williams delivered a career night against the Philadelphia Eagles, rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown as the Cowboys earned a much-needed 38-21 divisional victory. Williams’ performance was not just a personal milestone. It was a reminder of what Dallas had been missing throughout the first six games of the season: a physical, dependable rushing attack capable of controlling the pace, wearing down a defense and opening opportunities for the passing game. The Cowboys entered Monday averaging just 76 rushing yards per game, ranking near the bottom of the league. Against Philadelphia, they piled up 204 rushing yards on 38 carries, averaging 5.4 yards per attempt. That is the kind of offensive identity Dallas has been searching for, and Williams was at the center of it. Williams showed what happens when Dallas commits to the run Javonte Williams right through the hole for 34 yards! DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZTecZRX8fw — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 Williams finished the game averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His workload was just as important as his production. After receiving only 11 carries against Green Bay the previous week, Williams finally got the repeated opportunities needed to establish a rhythm and punish a defense that struggled to adjust. Javonte Williams puts the Cowboys up three scores 🤠 DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/imLAU5GWEh — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 The fourth-quarter numbers tell the story. Williams ripped off a 34-yard run that helped Dallas extend its lead, then continued to move the chains as the Cowboys leaned on the ground game to close out the victory. With the Eagles struggling to get off blocks, Williams repeatedly found open space and made Philadelphia pay. Troy Aikman even pointed out just how thoroughly the Cowboys’ offensive line had won the battle up front. On one run, left guard Tyler Smith was left looking for someone to block as the running back raced past him into the open field. It was a striking image of the control Dallas had established at the line of scrimmage. It feels like forever since we’ve seen that. Williams deserves plenty of credit for taking advantage of those openings. He ran with decisiveness, showed the acceleration to turn successful blocks into explosive gains and continued to make positive plays as the game wore on. But the performance was also a testament to the offensive line, which created the kind of running lanes that had been largely absent during the Cowboys’ early-season struggles. Week 7 was the best performance I've seen from Javonte Williams since he joined the #Cowboys . He led the NFL in rushing yards over expectation (50) this week, and it's not hard to see why. Here are all of his rushing attempts against the Eagles on Monday Night Football: pic.twitter.com/aDGS65CGgU — Marcus Mosher (@Marcus_Mosher) October 27, 2026 The running game made life easier for Dak Prescott The most important consequence of Williams’ performance may have been what it did for the rest of the offense. After Prescott threw four interceptions across the previous two games, Dallas needed a more balanced attack that did not require its quarterback to manufacture every scoring opportunity. Prescott responded with 212 passing yards, three touchdown passes and zero interceptions, finishing with a 118.1 passer rating. He connected with CeeDee Lamb for two touchdowns and George Pickens for another, while the running game forced Philadelphia to respect the possibility of a handoff on every possession. Dallas finished with 416 total yards and scored on seven of its nine possessions. That is a significant improvement for an offense that had scored just 29 combined points in its previous two games. The balance was the difference. When Williams and the offensive line consistently gained yards on the ground, Prescott did not have to drop back and face an obvious passing situation on every important down. The Cowboys could use play-action, attack mismatches and give their receivers more opportunities to make plays against a defense that could no longer focus exclusively on the passing game. Williams had his first game of the season with more than 20 carries, and Dallas looked far more comfortable offensively as a result. It is a reminder that play-calling is not only about finding the perfect individual play. It is also about giving your best players enough opportunities to influence the game. Williams had been productive in scoring situations before Monday, but he had not consistently received the volume needed to take over a game, until Monday. This needs to become the Cowboys’ identity One victory does not erase the problems Dallas showed in its first six games. The Cowboys still have to prove they can execute consistently, avoid costly penalties and produce this kind of performance against opponents that aren’t as banged up as the 2026 Eagles. Even so, the Eagles still had much of their starting defensive front and secondary available, including Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. Yet Philadelphia failed to record a sack, a quarterback hit or a tackle for loss against the Cowboys’ offense. Dallas controlled the line of scrimmage, protected Prescott and repeatedly created opportunities for Williams to make explosive plays. Williams’ career night was the headline, but the larger takeaway is about how Dallas should operate moving forward. The Cowboys have the talent to be dangerous through the air, and Prescott remains capable of producing big numbers when the offense is functioning properly. What they needed was a way to make the entire offense work together. Against Philadelphia, they found it. Now the challenge is to make sure this was not simply a one-night breakthrough. If Williams continues to receive a meaningful workload and the offensive line keeps creating room to run, the Cowboys have a much clearer path toward becoming the balanced offense they expected to be when the season began.
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Flaws and flash carry the Cowboys past the Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys delivered a performance against the Philadelphia Eagles that was both encouraging and concerning, showcasing their offensive potential and their lingering bad habits on defense. While a 17-point win over a bitter divisional rival is always pleasing, a closer look at the film shows a team still trying to completely put it all […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys delivered a performance against the Philadelphia Eagles that was both encouraging and concerning, showcasing their offensive potential and their lingering bad habits on defense. While a 17-point win over a bitter divisional rival is always pleasing, a closer look at the film shows a team still trying to completely put it all together. Let’s highlight some specific elements that jumped out at us after further review. The offensive line completely dominated the line of scrimmage from the first play of the game. They were routinely getting to the second level, sealing off running lanes, and overpowering defenders, and that says a lot because the Eagles’ defensive interior is no slouch. They were great in pass protection, as Dak Prescott was never sacked, and the group remarkably never gave up a single tackle for loss the entire game. That’s fantastic. That elite blocking gave Javonte Williams a fighting chance to run the ball, and he looked like a different running back because of it. Williams showed an immense amount of patience before hitting his holes, while doing a much better job of jump cutting and churning his legs for extra yards. His shiftiness allowed him to navigate through defenders and turn smaller gains into bigger gains. When the Cowboys weren’t running the ball, Prescott did a good job spreading the ball around. He is very fortunate to have two amazing wide receivers with elite body control and ball-tracking ability. His first two touchdown passes of the night were outstanding plays. Ryan Flournoy was also super efficient despite only seeing four targets. He caught all four of them for 70 yards and just seemed to be in the right place at the right time whenever Prescott needed him. We are also starting to see more and more of Brevyn Spann-Ford, and we like it. He played with a lot of toughness. The dude never gives up on a play. His juggling act turned an incompletion into a manageable 2nd-and-4. The team appears to slowly be transitioning to more of Spann-Ford, as he logged a career-high 53% of the snaps compared to a gradually dipping Jake Ferguson, who played 56% of the snaps. The passing game wasn’t perfect. Prescott is still throwing into coverage much more than he should be. He had two passes on slant routes that caromed off a defender and flew up in the air. He was lucky they were not picked off and returned for touchdowns. The slants have been his bread and butter at times, but he needs to do a better job reading the coverage because opposing cornerbacks have been sitting on these plays, just waiting to jump the route. Word on the street is that Brian Schottenheimer is an elite playcaller in this league, but sometimes his decisions seem a little bizarre. Quite honestly, his playcalling and game management were questionable throughout the night. The team’s ineffectiveness when they get deep into opponents’ territory is mind-boggling. Settling for a field goal inside the 10-yard line happens, and nobody is perfect, but it should not happen because of poor playcalling or bad clock management. And it just keeps happening. Please stop doing that. On the defensive side of the ball, it started off horribly. On the first possession of the game for the Eagles, they went 75 yards on just four plays. With a depleted offensive group. What was going on? As a whole, the defense was terrible on catch-and-runs due to poor angles and poor tackling. They were fortunate that Tanner McKee is Tanner McKee. He was off with his throws, as there were multiple incompletions thrown either behind or directly at the feet of his receivers. There were some good things, though. The Cowboys’ defensive tackle group looks better than they have in a long time. The way they clogged lanes, chased down screens, and blew up running plays was highly impressive. It is a true group effort. Quinnen Williams looked amazing on several plays, and Elijah Garcia continues to be a meaningful piece to this defense alongside Otito Ogbannia. When they employed their Rhino package by putting four defensive tackles on the line during a goal-line stand, they simply did not let anything pass. Behind the line, Joey Porter Jr. continues to play well. Someone finally completed a pass on him, but it was short of the sticks on third down. He is absolutely smothering out there. His pass breakup along the sideline against Hollywood Brown was textbook coverage, demonstrating great technique. It’s so enjoyable to watch a corner who sticks his hand out at the last second to break up a pass. The Cowboys finally have a true fundamentalist in the secondary. The rest of the defense was a bit of a mixed bag. DeMarvion Overshown had a blend of good and bad plays. His interception was obviously a massive highlight, and he had a nice batted-down pass right in McKee’s face. On the downside, Overshown struggled with his angles against the run and was washed out of plays at times. A similar thing could be said about Shemar James, who played 88% of the defensive snaps compared to just 32% from Jaishawn Barham. It’s unclear what that was all about, but James speed was helpful at times, though his overall play was a little inconsistent. Special teams looked great. Brandon Aubrey was perfect with his kicks, and his kickoffs helped pin the Eagles back multiple times in the game. Thanks to Aubrey, the Cowboys have the best opponent starting field position in the league at 26.79 and a muff rate of 15.4%, also the best in the league. Those dirty kicks are pretty dirty. No one else is doing what Brandon Aubrey and the Cowboys are doing on kickoffs this year pic.twitter.com/1niP0wa4Xe — Jake Kemp (@NotJackKemp) October 27, 2026 We also got a little spark from Tyler Goodson on kickoff returns. Goodson seems a lot better at finding holes than we are used to seeing. While it didn’t count due to a holding penalty, his return for a touchdown was still a great play. He flew through the opening and made several sharp cutbacks to extend the play. Far too many times we have seen KaVontae Turpin just run out of bounds when it looks like there is nowhere else to go. Goodson is an intriguing piece going forward. This was a much-needed win for the Cowboys. A loss would have absolutely sunk them. But even in victory, there are things that are still concerning for this team. It feels like a broken record, but unless the team can clean up some of these ongoing problems that have plagued them all season, they are still a ways away from doing anything meaningful, divisional winner or not.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys rookie report: Quieter roles in much-needed win over Philadelphia
summary: Dallas got the result it needed on Monday night, beating Philadelphia 38–21 to move to 3–4. The veterans supplied the biggest moments, while the rookie class had a quieter evening. Jaishawn Barham’s workload dropped, Caleb Downs had tackling issues to clean up, and Camden Brown finally made his NFL debut.  But here is how each […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas got the result it needed on Monday night, beating Philadelphia 38–21 to move to 3–4. The veterans supplied the biggest moments, while the rookie class had a quieter evening. Jaishawn Barham’s workload dropped, Caleb Downs had tackling issues to clean up, and Camden Brown finally made his NFL debut. But here is how each rookie fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. Caleb Downs (56 defensive snaps | 5 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 pressures | 0 QB hits) Downs contributed three solo tackles, two assists, and was credited with one run stop. The concern was finishing where he was also charged with two missed tackles against the run. There was useful involvement, but those missed opportunities kept this from being a clean performance. Malachi Lawrence (30 defensive snaps | 1 tackle | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits) Lawrence contributed a run stop, although the box score recorded his tackle as an assist. His impact remained modest, with no sacks or quarterback hits. Dallas got its two sacks from Quinnen Williams and Donovan Ezeiruaku, meaning Lawrence still needs to turn his opportunities into more decisive plays. Jaishawn Barham (21 defensive snaps | 2 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 pressures | 0 QB hits) Barham played a smaller role with DeMarvion Overshown back, while Shemar James also received substantial playing time. Barham was also charged with one completion for 12 yards on two targets. He avoided a costly coverage total, but two tackles and no disruptive plays made this a quiet contribution. LT Overton (23 defensive snaps | 1 tackle | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 1 pressure | 0 QB hits) Overton supplied one pressure across 16 pass-rush snaps, giving Dallas a little disruption from its rotation. His only tackle was an assist, and he did not produce a stop behind the line. He was also charged with a critical penalty near the goal line. There was a contribution, but limited production overall. Camden Brown (4 ST snaps | 0 targets | 0 receptions | 0 receiving yards | 0 TD) Brown finally made his regular-season debut after being inactive through the opening six games. His opportunity came entirely on special teams, so there was no receiving performance to judge. Getting onto the field was a first step, earning offensive work is the next challenge.
author: Mike Poland

title: DeMarvion Overshown’s interception sealed a great return to action
summary: Philadelphia was moving the ball, the game was still within reach, and the Cowboys needed someone to shut the door. DeMarvion Overshown answered. His fourth-quarter interception of Tanner McKee thwarted a promising Eagles drive and secured a 10-point lead. In a game Dallas ultimately won 38-21, this takeaway propelled the Cowboys firmly into the driver’s […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Philadelphia was moving the ball, the game was still within reach, and the Cowboys needed someone to shut the door. DeMarvion Overshown answered. His fourth-quarter interception of Tanner McKee thwarted a promising Eagles drive and secured a 10-point lead. In a game Dallas ultimately won 38-21, this takeaway propelled the Cowboys firmly into the driver’s seat, leaving Philadelphia to chase both the scoreboard and the clock. The final score makes this look more comfortable than it felt heading into the fourth quarter. Philadelphia had opened the second half with a 17-play touchdown drive that consumed over nine minutes and gave them a 21-20 lead. However, Dallas responded with CeeDee Lamb’s second touchdown, followed by Dak Prescott’s two-point conversion, which moved the Cowboys ahead 28-21. Brandon Aubrey extended the lead to 31-21 with a 24-yard field goal. While the Eagles had given Dallas some breathing room, their next possession quickly threatened to reverse the momentum. McKee connected with Dallas Goedert for 18 yards, propelling the Eagles to the Cowboys’ 32-yard line. A touchdown would have narrowed the gap to just three points with time left in the fourth quarter. With 7:55 remaining on first-and-10, McKee looked towards Goedert on an out route to the right. Overshown intercepted the throw and returned it to the Dallas 34. Philadelphia had moved into scoring territory, only to leave without a point. The Cowboys capitalised on this, taking the ball back at the precise moment the Eagles needed an answer to keep their two-possession cushion. The importance of that play went beyond the turnover itself. Philadelphia could no longer build patiently toward a score and trust there would be enough time for another possession. Every empty drive now carried greater consequences. Dallas could lean on its running game, make the Eagles use more time and force McKee to bring them back through the air. The Cowboys did punt on the possession after the interception, but Philadelphia’s opportunity had become considerably harder. Starting from their own 16, the Eagles were pushed backward by an eight-yard Quinnen Williams sack. They eventually faced fourth-and-nine and failed to convert. Overshown’s takeaway had preserved the lead, the next defensive stand gave Dallas the chance to finish the job, which they did. Overshown’s significant contribution in his first appearance since Week 1, following a hamstring injury, served as a reminder of his enormous talent when healthy. He played on 65% of the snaps on Monday, eating into rookie Jaishawn Barham’s snaps. He finished tied for the lead in tackles with six. He was also credited with a tackle for loss and two passes defensed. Plus, the all-important interception. Overshown staying healthy could be a turning point for the defense.
author: Mike Poland

title: Flawed Cowboys defense does enough versus Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense was far from perfect. But they did enough, contributing to a big win against their hated division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 21 points to the Eagles. The first two Philadelphia drives resulted in two touchdowns. After that, the defense would go on to surrender just […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defense was far from perfect. But they did enough, contributing to a big win against their hated division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 21 points to the Eagles. The first two Philadelphia drives resulted in two touchdowns. After that, the defense would go on to surrender just one more touchdown on the night. Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception. The Eagles converted 23 first downs but were 5-of-12 on third down. Dallas allowed 4.8 yards per carry on 25 rushing attempts, totaling 121 yards on the ground. Individual stat leaders on defense DeMarvion Overshown had one of the best games of his career on his return to the lineup, accounting for six tackles, one interception, two passes defended, and one tackle-for-loss. Shemar James saw plenty of snaps as well, tying Overshown for the team lead in tackles. Quinnen Williams recorded three tackles-for-loss and one sack. This may have been his best performance of the season. Donovan Ezeiruaku also recorded his first full sack of the season. Advanced analytics SumerSports recorded the Cowboys defense finishing with a -.05 EPA/play allowed. This is their best EPA allowed on the season. Furthermore, the Eagles finished with a -.10 EPA per drop back and +0.13 EPA per designed run. The pass defense limited Philadelphia while the Cowboys run defense struggled. The Eagles struggled in success rate, finishing the night at 38.7%. For reference, the league average is typically between 45-50%. Final grade: C This Eagles offense is in absolute shambles at this point in time. They are down one franchise quarterback, two starting receivers, multiple offensive linemen, and too many running backs to count. This needed to be a game where the Dallas defense started fast and never looked back. They eventually got going, but it took too much time against a terrible Philadelphia offensive unit. The Eagles came out and punched the Cowboys defense in the mouth right from the start. The first drive took just four plays in just over two minutes to go 75 yards for a touchdown. A horrendous start that had us pulling out our hair (if you had any left). The next drive went 13 plays for 76 yards and took half a quarter off the clock, also resulting in a touchdown. Multiple key penalties kept this Eagles drive alive. Insane laughter from Cowboys fans ensued as our worst nightmares came alive at Lincoln Financial. But then the defense buckled down, forcing punts on the next two Eagles drives. The half would end with the Cowboys up 20-14. The first drive of the second half would be the last time Philadelphia scored on the night, walking their way down the field on an absurd 17-play, 84-yard drive, consuming over nine minutes of game clock. Short crossing routes to Makai Lemon proved to be a thorn in the Cowboys’ side on the drive, with the touchdown going to the rookie receiver on a well designed pick play. After that horror show, the Cowboys defense had finally had enough. They would go on to force a three-and-out on the next Eagles drive, allowing Dak Prescott and the offense to go up multiple scores. As one could anticipate, asking Tanner McKee to play keep up would prove to be a recipe for disaster, as the backup quarterback would throw an interception on the next drive to DeMarvion Overshown. The Eagles never recovered from that point. They would turn the ball over on downs on their very next drive, deep in their own territory. Dallas accepted the gift and put an exclamation point on the board with a Javonte Williams touchdown run. This is the third straight week where the Cowboys defense has kept their opponent under 24 points. That’s all we asked for last season – an average defense. It’s unfortunate that the defense could not capitalize earlier on the state of the Eagles offense, but they eventually found their way to an interception and a pair of sacks late in the game, closing out the win in Philadelphia. The defense looked average once again, and so once again, they’ll receive an average grade this week. Christian Parker’s unit earned a moderately disappointing C for their efforts against a banged up Eagles offense. I had personally hoped for a higher grade this week, considering the state of their opponent. But the defense continues to struggle early and tighten up as the game goes on. The Cowboys will take on a struggling Cardinals team next week, likely led by QB Jacoby Brissett according to Arizona’s coach.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones happy with the run game
summary: Javonte Williams had a career performance against the Philadelphia Eagles. It was the first time since 2016 that a Dallas Cowboys running back ran for more than 150 yards in a single game. That caught the attention of the Cowboys owner, who believes balance to the offense is a winning formula moving forward. Jerry Jones […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images Javonte Williams had a career performance against the Philadelphia Eagles. It was the first time since 2016 that a Dallas Cowboys running back ran for more than 150 yards in a single game. That caught the attention of the Cowboys owner, who believes balance to the offense is a winning formula moving forward. Jerry Jones on Cowboys’ run game, potential deadline moves, Troy Aikman & more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com If Dallas can run the ball like they did on Monday, they should be able to go on a run over the next few weeks. Jones said that the Cowboys offense is one that is run-first, because it allows different aspects of the playbook to open up if they have success. “That lets us have the opportunity to get Dak under center a lot more, and that’s a big key too,” Jones said. “That presents a different defensive challenge for the opponent if he can get under center a lot. We saw that happen acceptably well.” Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer denies media criticism affected his demeanor vs. Eagles – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys head coach was noticeably out of character during his post-game press conference. Schottenheimer was asked about it again Tuesday and whether there was something said or written in the media that prompted his demeanor. “No, I’ll be honest. I really do a good job of blocking you guys out,” Schottenheimer said. “I think it’s a big game for us. We’re motivated as a football team. I’m motivated as a head coach to get our guys playing to the standard that I know they’re capable of playing. Intense game against a real rival. But no, at the end of the day, in this business you get paid to deal with the criticism and things that come with the job.” Download the SB Nation app today! Exclusive: Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. takes in ‘surreal’ start to Dallas tenure – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star Telegram Joey Porter Jr. is just happy to be in Dallas, and the feeling is certainly mutual. “It’s just so unreal, so surreal,” Porter said to the Star-Telegram while looking at the room. “I can’t even really explain it. Sometimes it’s hard for me to be in the moment and realize what’s all going on because everything is moving so fast. I’m happy where I’m at. I’m happy where this team is headed.” Jerry Jones insists Troy Aikman holding significant role with Cowboys is ‘very possible’ – Brandon Contes, Awful Announcing Could the Hall of Fame quarterback go from the booth to the Cowboys front office? Shariff asked Jones a direct question: whether he would ever bring Aikman in for a “major significant role with the Cowboys” if he were interested. “Yes, I could and would,” Jones confirmed. “It’s that simple, because I do think that much of him, with his basic command and understanding and knowledge of NFL football. He certainly is qualified to do any of the things that have been mentioned, and I think he’s outstanding at what he focuses on right now, and that’s giving the story and narration of football games. 5 things to know about the Arizona Cardinals ahead of Week 8 matchup with Dallas Cowboys – Abraham Nudelstejer, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys’ rush defense could struggle if Jeremiyah Love returns for Sunday’s game. Rushing offense The Cardinals have struggled to move the chains on the ground. They rank 22nd in the league with 622 rushing yards. Jeremiyah Love has carried much of the load, with 67 carries for 272 yards, an average of 3.7 yards per carry. Love has not played in Arizona’s past two games because of an ankle injury. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight have handled the lead-back duties in his absence.

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Chiefs and the rest of Week 8
summary: Welcome back to the eighth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 7—I fared a bit better than Week 6. However, I picked 9 of 14 games right. I was wrong with my 49ers, Panthers, Texans, Jets, and Chiefs predictions. Let’s see if I can do any better this week. […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Quinn Meinerz #77 after scoring a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the eighth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 7 —I fared a bit better than Week 6. However, I picked 9 of 14 games right. I was wrong with my 49ers, Panthers, Texans, Jets, and Chiefs predictions. Let’s see if I can do any better this week. This week there are just 14 games again with the Texans, Saints, Giants, and 49ers all on their bye week. Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers — Thursday Night Football Both of these teams are coming off Week 7 losses and need to find a way and rebound. Carolina’s defense continues to be a major problem. Even though Green Bay’s offense is still struggling a bit, I like their odds of earning a victory at home in primetime. Winner: Packers Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Colts continue their downward spiral and may very well be tanking. They’ve lost three in a row and already traded DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson. It’s quite possible Jonathon Taylor and Josh Downs are next in line. All things considered, I think Jacksonville takes care of business here. That’ll put them at five wins and a huge lead in the AFC South. Winner: Jaguars Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets — Sunday (Early Game) After a great start to the season, the Raiders have lost four in a row. Meanwhile, the Jets are coming off a loss to the Miami Dolphins and are now 2-5 on the season. I think Klint Kubiak and his team find a way to win on the road and get back to being a .500 ball cub. Winner: Raiders Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills — Sunday (Early Game) I wouldn’t have predicted the Ravens would be dead last in the AFC North to date, but that’s where they are at with a 4-3 record. I have significant doubts they will be able to get back on track and defeat Josh Allen and the Bills on the road. Buffalo’s defense is mess, but they keep finding ways to win due to a high-powered offensive attack. I believe they’ll take care of business at home against Baltimore. Winner: Bills Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Sunday (Early Game) Both these NFC South teams have losing records but are coming off Week 7 victories. Somehow, the Falcons were able to take down the undefeated 49ers, and the Buccaneers absolutely throttled the Panthers. This should be a relatively close game. The Falcons for the most part have been great shutting down the run, but that’s what propelled Tampa Bay to victory next week? I think Bucky Irving has another strong game and gets Tampa Bay a win. Winner: Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys — Sunday (Early Game) The Cowboys still have a lot of issues to figure out on defense, but their offense is doing enough to help them win games. I think Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, and CeeDee Lamb continue to build upon their great outings in Week 7 and earn a big win at home to stay in the NFC East title race. Winner: Cowboys Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Early Game) The Vikings are the last undefeated team remaining in the NFL with the Chiefs and 49ers losing last week. They’ve been absolutely fantastic on defense and are gutting out close wins even with an offense that is still quite inconsistent on a week-to-week basis. The Lions are 4-2 with a great offense, but a lot of issues to figure out on the other side of the ball. That being said, I think this week is the one where Minnesota finally loses. I’ll take Detroit at home. Winner: Lions Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals — Sunday (Early Game) The Bengals are in the thick of it in the AFC North at 4-2, whereas the Titans continue to plummet and are 1-6 on the season. Usually, a lot of my ‘easy picks’ have backfired this season, but I’m very confident in taking Cincinnati in this one. I just don’t see them losing this game. Winner: Bengals Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers — Sunday (Early Game) This AFC North rivalry game is a battle for first place. Both teams are 5-2 and are riding multi-game winning streaks. I’m pretty sure this is going to be a close game as well. I’m going to pick the Steelers, who are a little bit better on offense. Winner: Steelers Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams — Sunday (Afternoon Game) I would be very surprised if the Chargers found a way to beat the Rams even with an extra week of preparation. They’ve got too many issues and are decimated by injuries. I think the Rams get their fourth win of the season here and get back to an even record. Winners: Rams New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Dolphins earned their first victory of the season over the Jets, and the Patriots are coming off a Thursday Night Football loss to the Bears. I think Drake Maye and New England find a way to get back in the win column in their Week 8 primetime matchup. Winner: Patriots Kanas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This AFC West matchup will determine who is the top team in the division halfway through the season. The Broncos really struggled on Monday Night Football in Week 1 to start the season, but they’re starting to hit their groove in all phases. Denver has been tremendous at home the past several seasons and I think the homefield advantage makes a huge difference in this one. I’ll be taking the Broncos. Winner: Broncos Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders — Sunday Night Football It’s a battle of the NFC East bottom dwellers when the Eagles head on the road to take on the Commanders on Sunday Night Football . Both teams have their fair share of injuries and are missing key players. The Commanders are four-point favorites in this one, and I think they’ll find a way to get their second win of the season. Winner: Commanders Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks — Monday Night Football This might be one of the best matchups of Week 8. I think it’s the perfect finale for the slate of games. Caleb Williams and the Bears are roaring on offense with a 5-2 record. The Seahawks toppled the Chiefs in Week 7 due to a dominant defensive performance. Oh, and they traded for Quenton Nelson, who should immediately provide them a much-needed boost in their offensive trenches. I think Seattle’s run game stays strong, and the 12th man and home field advantage will make a difference here too. I’ll pick the Seahawks. Winner: Seahawks

title: Malcolm Roach is having a great season

full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Malcolm Roach (97) of the Denver Broncos catches his breath after a pick six by Talanoa Hufanga (9) on a pass by Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 30-26 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 regular season with a lot of question marks. A big one was wondering how they would replace John Franklin-Myers. A key player in Denver’s trenches the past several seasons, Franklin-Myers earned a well-deserved payday in free agency from the Tennessee Titans. That left a pretty big void in Denver’s defense. Thankfully, the Broncos had several players in house ready to help replace his productivity. This season, the Broncos have rotated lineman a bit more than you have seen in past seasons. That’s helped keep players fresh and their efforts strong to date. One player that has really stood out is seventh-year defensive tackle Malcolm Roach. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton talked about his improvement and what he means to the team’s defense. “I think I would say this: he does a lot of things well. The other thing as an NFL player, you know exactly what you’re getting that’s very helpful then when you’re putting a gameplan together,” stated Payton. “Then all the other things with his personality and you guys have been around him, he’s consistent. I think that’s important to find those type of players in your front.” Known primarily for his run stopping ability, Roach is arguably having the best season of his NFL career. In seven games, Roach already has 20 tackles. On top of that, there have been great strides made as a pass rusher. He boasts 2.5 sacks and a new a career-high with 11 quarterback hits. A few years ago, he was playing only 40-percent of the team’s defensive snaps. This season? 55-percent. His development and high level of play is a big reason why Denver’s defense has been strong to start the season. The Broncos will need him and his teammates to play at a high level to find a way to topple the Kansas City Chiefs in their Week 8 rematch on Sunday. As always, thank you for reading. title: Statistical review of the Broncos struggles on third downs
summary: The Denver Broncos are currently second to last in third down conversion rate at 31.1 percent. Only Washington is worse at 30.9 percent. The Broncos have converted on 28 of 90 3rd downs (not counting conversions by penalty on third down). By game here is how that went: There were two good games and five […]
full_text: The Denver Broncos are currently second to last in third down conversion rate at 31.1 percent. Only Washington is worse at 30.9 percent. The Broncos have converted on 28 of 90 3rd downs (not counting conversions by penalty on third down). By game here is how that went: at KC – 2/12 JAC – 4/10 LAR – 7/13 at SF – 8/17 at LAC – 1/12 SEA – 4/14 at ARI – 3/11 There were two good games and five bad ones. Over the last three games (all wins) the Broncos have converted eight of 37 – 22 percent. The league is converting on 40.6% on third down so far this year. The Bengals currently lead the league at 50.6 percent. What makes this even worse is that the Broncos offense is only 14th in yards needed on 3rd down at 6.9. The 49ers are first at 5.3 and the Eagles are worst at 8.4. The Broncos are tied for 16th at converting on 3rd and short (1-3 needed) at 61.5 percent. However they are tied for 31st at converting on 3rd and medium (4-6 needed) at 25.0. That is pathetic. Only the Falcons are worse at 21.7 percent. The Bills convert at 64.7 percent on 3rd and medium to lead the league. The Broncos are tied for 31st at converting on 3rd and medium – at 25%. Only the Falcons have been worse. pic.twitter.com/vvK9VbnZAK — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) October 28, 2026 While that was bad, it gets worse. The Broncos are dead last at converting on 3rd and long. They have only 13 of 63 or 20.6 percent. Buffalo is converting those at 46.7 percent or better than twice the rate that Broncos are. The Broncos have actually had a conversion on 3rd and long in every game with the exception of the game against the Cardinals. Four of their thirteen came in the game against the 49ers. The only other games with more than one conversion on 3rd and long were the wins over the Rams and the Seahawks. Apparently the Broncos can only convert 3rd and longs against the NFC West, with the exception of the Cardinals. Here is a look at conversion on 3rd and long by the Bronco offense of the last six seasons: 2026 (7 games) – 20.6 % 2025 – 35.8% 2024 – 30.4% 2023 – 28.6% 2022 – 22.3% 2021 – 28.1% 2020 – 31.7% This is the worst 3rd and long performance by the Bronco offense this decade although 2022 was close. On the other side of the ball the Bronco defense is currently is tied for 21st allowing 3rd down conversions at 42.1 percent. The Bears defense has been the best so far at 26.1 percent while the Cowboys defense has been the worst at 52.9 percent. The Bronco defense finished second last season in 3rd down conversions allowed at 33.8 percent. The Seahawk defense led the league last year at 32.1%. The Bronco defense has moved into a five-way tie for the league lead in sacks with 21, but three of those teams have only played 6 games (Bengals, Lions, and Vikings). The Broncos still have a shot at leading the NFL in sacks for a third straight season. No team has ever done that. The Broncos are currently seventh in QB pressure rate at 25.2 percent. The Vikings are leading the league at 35.7 percent while the Giants and Colts are tied for last at 17.7 percent. In terms of protecting Bo Nix, the Bronco OL has allowed pressure on 22.3% of dropbacks which is tied for 17th with the Cardinals. The Broncos are 4th in sacks allowed at 9. Three teams have only allowed 7 sacks so far this season, and one of them is the Bronco’s next opponent, Kansas City. The Browns have allowed the most sacks at 25.

full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos runs across the field during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport, Denver Broncos star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle suffered an aggravation of his previous chest injury during Sunday’s victory over the Cardinals. Rapoport adds that Waddle’s availability this week will be based on how practice goes. 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis also adds that Waddle is expected to be listed as questionable for Sunday’s game vs. the Chiefs, but there is hope that he can play . Klis adds, “It’s the Chiefs after all.” #Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, suffered an aggravation of his previous chest injury on the reverse last week and his status for Sunday vs the #Chiefs will be determined at a later time, sources say. Waddle’s availability will be based on how practice goes. pic.twitter.com/OKC4BCVQLA — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 28, 2026 As we know, Waddle injured his shoulder on a late 4th-quarter reverse call where Waddle bobbled the ball and landed hard on his chest/shoulder when recovering the ball. After the play, Waddle was slow to get up and was in obvious pain. After the game, Broncos head coach Sean Payton called the play “dumb” and asked the media why they did not ask him about the play call. “Why didn’t anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? That would be one of the first calls. Alright, I’m going to answer. Everyone ask the question. It was awful. I’m sorry. If you look it up — in 2008, in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse, (former Saints RB Reggie Bush) fumbled (and) Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play. That would have been a good question.” Thankfully. Waddle’s injury seems like a short-term thing, and there is hope that he can play vs. the Chiefs on Sunday. However, we need to pay attention to the injury report this week to determine his status. Klis notes that he will be questionable, but it seems like his availability will come down to pain tolerance. We don’t know the exact chest/shoulder injury he suffered, but he was limited for two practices before practicing fully on Friday. So, we will have to see if Waddle will be limited for today’s practice or not. A DNP to start the week would not be a great sign for his availability on Sunday. This game vs. the Chiefs will be a big one. First, the Broncos will look to bounce back after their embarrassing Week 1 loss to the Chiefs to open the season. More importantly, if the Broncos were to win this game, they would move to the top of the AFC West. A loss would put them at 5-3, two games behind the Chiefs in the loss column, and they would have the tie-breaker due to the in-season sweep of the Broncos. So, it’s a bit of a must-win game for the Broncos if they want to win the AFC West. Hopefully, Waddle can go and play through this injury, but we will have to wait and see. The Broncos have their first practice of the week today and we will see whether or not is able to practice today. Stay tuned to Mile High Report for today’s injury report and any and all updates on Waddle’s status for this Sunday’s game vs. the Chiefs.

summary: The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a play against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second half of an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn’t tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that’s basically a pick ‘em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday’s game?

title: Broncos News: Why are we talking about the Broncos making a trade?
summary: With the NFL trade deadline looming, all the talk is about your team making a trade for a good player from a bad team in order to help improve their roster. The buzzphrase is that your team is in “win now mode.” Yes, the Broncos are absolutely taking a big swing at making a run […]
full_text: With the NFL trade deadline looming, all the talk is about your team making a trade for a good player from a bad team in order to help improve their roster. The buzzphrase is that your team is in “win now mode.” Yes, the Broncos are absolutely taking a big swing at making a run for a Super Bowl. Yes, it is fun to think about making a trade for a Jonathon Taylor or Saquon Barkley. Yes, either of these players, or some of the other names thrown around like new Seahawk Quenton Nelson, would look great in a Broncos uniform. I’m just curious why anyone is getting their undies in a twist about the Broncos making a trade. “They need a guard like Quenton Nelson!” Why? They have a very solid group of linemen that are veterans. Their problem so far this year has more to do with execution, not a lack of ability. They also have guys like Alex Palczewski and Kage Casey in the wings ready to step in next year if we lose a guard. And let’s not forget that with Coleman running the ball, the line sure did look pretty decent. “The one thing the Broncos need is a better running back” I’m very much not sure on this one. They need a better back than 2026’s version of JK Dobbins. With Jonah Coleman healthy and looking like a stud so far in his one game back, I think they already have an answer. They also get Tyler Badie back somewhere around week 12 or later. The big problem is the cap space The Broncos currently have less than $5M in cap space available. Many of these players that people are talking about trading for have contracts far north of that this year, with possible considerable impact on the next couple of years. That’s not to say that the Broncos front office can work some numbers magic to make room, but they are already poised to lose some key players next season like Riley Moss, Ben Powers, and Evan Engram. Bringing in an expensive free agent may not be tenable with a team that is building a long-term winning culture. title: Lions, Vikings Week 8 injury report: Jahmyr Gibbs sits with shoulder injury
summary: The Detroit Lions (4-2) will host the Minnesota Vikings (6-0) in Week 8, and both teams were on the practice field on Wednesday, preparing for their Sunday afternoon battle at Ford Field. The Lions have only a few injured players this week—Amon Ra St. Brown and Ennis Rakestraw were injured in Week 7—but they also […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (4-2) will host the Minnesota Vikings (6-0) in Week 8, and both teams were on the practice field on Wednesday, preparing for their Sunday afternoon battle at Ford Field. The Lions have only a few injured players this week—Amon Ra St. Brown and Ennis Rakestraw were injured in Week 7—but they also elected to rest several injured players on Wednesday; most, if not all, are expected to return to practice this week. “We’re going to do a walkthrough and then roll right into practice for a little bit here,” Lions coach Dan Campbell explained at Wednesday’s press conference. “I think those guys (St. Brown and Rakestraw) will be at walkthrough, but I don’t see them out there during the practice portion. I’m going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they’ll be at walkthrough.” Additionally, the Lions received terrific news on Wednesday, as All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is now healthy enough to practice, and the team has started his injury evaluation clock , making him eligible to practice. Let’s take a look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date with what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Injured list updates RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December OL Giovanni Manu (Undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — Injury evaluation clock started on October 28 S Thomas Harper (Ankle, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time After a few hints on social media, Kerby Joseph is officially returning to practice. Here’s coach Campbell on the decision: “We’re going to start Kerby’s clock today. So, he’ll be running around. Start working him in. He’s put in a lot of work; it’s been a long, hard road for Kerby. So, just being able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit. But we will kind of progress him as we go, each week here, just to get him back in the flow, the movement, the flow, the pounding, and all of it. But he’s passed every test to this point, and the next thing is to get him running around now. The strength in the knee is good, and the thigh, the quad, and all of that. So it’ll be great to get him back out there with all the guys.” Joseph has 21 days to be evaluated by the team before they need to decide on his status, but they can return him to the active roster at any time. N o practice RB Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) — Injured in Week 7 WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) — Injured in Week 7 OT Penei Sewell (rest) DT Alim McNeill (rest) DT Tyleik Williams (illness) EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (rest) EDGE DJ Wonnum (rest) Jahmyr Gibbs had an injury scare after an awkward slide against the Packers, but told reporters he was fine after the game. This shoulder injury appears to be something different, and it’s unclear how concerning it is, especially considering it was not a noticeable problem in the locker room after the game. Additionally, considering the Lions had a lot of players resting, the concern level should remain low. While St. Brown was injured in Week 7, his absence from Wednesday’s practice was planned, and he is expected to return to practice on Thursday , as Campbell explained on Monday: “(St. Brown) and Ennis, I think those guys will probably sit Wednesday, but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think that they’ll be fine. They should be good.” Williams is dealing with an illness, and it’s hard to project how that will progress as the week goes on. Though it’s noteworthy that the Lions did add nose tackle Taki Taimani this week to the practice squad . As for the other four starters, Campbell also noted that their absences are temporary and they are also expected to return to practice this week. This rest day was designed to “get them off their feet” and allow them an extra day to rest their bodies. Limited practice RB Jacob Saylors (neck) — Injured in Week 7 CB Ennis Rakestraw (ankle) — Injured in Week 7 S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 20 Saylors did not appear to suffer an injury during the game, but can often creep in after the game concludes. Fortunately, a limited practice is a good sign. While Campbell said he didn’t expect Rakestraw to practice Wednesday, the corner was able to give it a go. An encouraging sign when combined with Campbell’s optimism on Monday: “It’s not major, he’s got a little ankle here. We feel like, as of right now, he’ll be at practice on Thursday. That’s kinda what we’re looking at. But we don’t feel like it’s major as of today.” No longer on the injury report C Cade Mays (Wrist) CB Rock Ya-Sin (Hamstring) S Brian Branch (Achilles) The players in this section are healthy enough that they no longer need to be included in the Lions’ injury report. title: Dan Campbell compares his 4th down philosophy to ‘Uncle Buck’
summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has faced a lot of criticism—and a fair amount of praise—for his bold decision to go for it on fourth down late against the Green Bay Packers, despite being backed up at his own 24-yard line in a tie game. Though the Lions didn’t convert, the strategy worked. As Campbell […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions smile while answering questions from reporters during the Detroit Lions Training Camp at the Lions Headquarters and Training Facility on July 29, 2022 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has faced a lot of criticism—and a fair amount of praise—for his bold decision to go for it on fourth down late against the Green Bay Packers, despite being backed up at his own 24-yard line in a tie game. Though the Lions didn’t convert, the strategy worked. As Campbell said after the game, he knew if they didn’t convert, they’d still get the ball back for possibly the final possession. Detroit did, and they made it count with the game-winning field goal. Campbell was asked about his overall fourth-down philosophy again on Wednesday, and in the midst of talking about his years of experience in the league and influences like Sean Payton, he also made a hilarious pop-culture reference. He said that he views his affinity for fourth-down aggression much like John Candy titular character in the movie “Uncle Buck” views his iconic trapper/ushanka hat. “You guys ever seen ‘Uncle Buck?’” Campbell starts. “I think I’m a little bit like—his fedora, you know that hat he wears? It’s a little bit of a flavor.” Then he paraphrases a quote from the movie: “Just the mere sight of it bothers a lot of people.” “So I always think a little of ‘Uncle Buck, ’ man, when John Candy’s wearing that hat. ‘Is it the hat?’” Campbell’s analogy wasn’t all that clear, but fans of the movie may remember this specific scene, where Uncle Buck talks about how he believes people judge him simply based on the hat. “A lot of people hate this hat. It angers a lot of people, just the sight of it,” Candy’s character says. Perhaps he believes people just hate fourth-down aggression without even thinking about it. Or they see Campbell as a meathead, and his fourth-down process as a reflection of surface-level thinking. Or maybe it’s just Campbell’s little quirk that you either love or you hate. Either way, it’s just another iconic moment in a Dan Campbell press conference.

title: Detroit Lions return Kerby Joseph to practice
summary: After just over a year on the sidelines dealing with a recurring knee injury, Detroit Lions All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is officially returning to practice. On Wednesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell announced that the team is starting the 21-day injury evaluation clock on Joseph, allowing him to begin practicing while still remaining on the Physically […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) walks towards the field for practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, July 21, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After just over a year on the sidelines dealing with a recurring knee injury, Detroit Lions All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is officially returning to practice. On Wednesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell announced that the team is starting the 21-day injury evaluation clock on Joseph, allowing him to begin practicing while still remaining on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) injury list. “We’re going to start Kerby’s clock today,” Campbell said. “So, he’ll be running around. Start working him in. He’s put in a lot of work; it’s been a long, hard road for Kerby. So, just being able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit. But we will kind of progress him as we go, each week here, just to get him back in the flow, the movement, the flow, the pounding, and all of it. But he’s passed every test to this point, and the next thing is to get him running around now. The strength in the knee is good, and the thigh, the quad, and all of that. So it’ll be great to get him back out there with all the guys.” "He's put in a lot of work." -Coach Campbell on Kerby Joseph returning to practice pic.twitter.com/Y96q54HmnL — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 28, 2026 Joseph injured his knee in 2025 training camp, but despite toughing it out for the first month of the season, he could no longer play after Week 5. He appeared to make significant progress during the offseason and appeared to be nearing a return during 2026 training camp, but was unable to build the proper strength in his knee to sustain the physicality of the NFL. However, the strength appears to have returned enough to test things out, and the Lions will now have 21 days to evaluate his status. During this window, Joseph can practice but will remain on the PUP list and won’t be eligible to play in games until he is removed from the PUP list and activated to the 53-man roster, which can happen at any time. “It was always about getting him to the point where we felt like we had gotten that leg strength to a point where it was equal with the other leg,” Campbell continued. “And it was always, ‘we got to get it there,’ because that’s part of your shock absorbers, that reduces some of the stress on the knee. And (we’re) starting to work him a little bit, where (he got) a couple of back-to-back days, a little more pounding. Then, how does the knee react? Is there swelling? Is there not? Is he ready the next day? And he’s passed all those tests. […] so, he’s checked all those boxes and the rest is ‘how does he react to football?’”
