title: The Good and the Bad from Chiefs’ loss in Seattle
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their first game of the season in Week 7, 20-3, to the Seattle Seahawks. Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Mansoor Delane in a trail position The Chiefs had few bright spots on offense, defense, or special teams. […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their first game of the season in Week 7, 20-3, to the Seattle Seahawks . Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Mansoor Delane in a trail position The Chiefs had few bright spots on offense, defense, or special teams. However, I do think rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane deserves recognition for playing a very good game overall. Going back to his film at LSU, one of Delane’s best skills is his ability to win in trail position. Delane isn’t often behind a play, but that can happen occasionally as a cornerback, depending on your leverage. The Chiefs are in a Cover 1 bracket here, bracketing wide receiver Jaxon-Smith Ngijba with a single-high safety. Delane is in outside leverage, with help over the middle. Delane gets about a step behind the wide receiver, but he closes that space and gets his arm in the way to break up the pass. Delane’s recovery speed is great, and he does a great job poking the ball out with late hands. The Chiefs send a blitz this time with a Cover 2 man coverage call behind it, putting Delane in inside leverage. He recognizes that Smith-Njigba is trying to get Delane to shift outside so he can get inside positioning on the slant, but Delane sits all over it and boxes Smith-Njigba out of getting inside positioning. Delane covered Smith-Njigba on both his go routes along the sideline, but truthfully, that wasn’t bad coverage. Smith-Njigba is the best receiver in the NFL, and Delane had to cover him one-on-one on a two-way go. Most guys get beat there. Because Smith-Njigba is so good in the middle of the field, Delane has to worry about not letting Smith-Njigba cross his face, which lets him get a step downfield. Delane is still in fine position and makes an attempt to knock the ball out; the throws and catches are just better. You’ll take this coverage every time. The Bad L’Jarius Sneed playing man coverage in the slot L’Jarius Sneed was resigned this offseason to provide cornerback depth, but with the Chiefs not knowing who to start in the slot, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo elected to go with the veteran Sneed. Sneed started his career in the slot, and his physicality and blitzing make him well-suited to that position. Sneed played great from the slot against the Denver Broncos in Week 1, but since then, he’s been a total liability in coverage. Sneed’s snaps have also been slowly reduced, with only 14 against Seattle and almost none after halftime. Despite only playing 14 snaps, Sneed’s play hurt the Chiefs. At this stage of his career, he can’t cover in man-to-man anymore, and Seattle knew it. The veteran allowed 83 yards over five receptions in the first half alone, according to Sumer Sports . Farzin Vousoughian on X noted that Sneed has also allowed the most receptions in the NFL this season and the fourth-most receiving yards (378). The Chiefs are running a Cover 2 man coverage again, where Sneed bluffs the blitz and drops to coverage. Sneed has inside positioning on Smith-Njigba, so a slant shouldn’t be able to cross his face. But Sneed’s footwork and change of direction are much slower than they used to be, leaving him flat-footed when Smith-Njigba runs inside. He has no chance of recovering, and this turns into a first down. Another play where Sneed is slow to click and close on a slant, and the receiver easily crosses his face. It was a theme in the loss, especially on third down; site manager Ron Kopp Jr. a few more plays where Sneed was beat earlier this week. Sneed can’t play in the slot anymore. If he’s going to play, he has to play outside, where he has more chances to defend vertical routes. Move Delane to the slot more if necessary. I would play Chris Rolland-Wallace more, and either play Jaden Hicks in Dime over Sneed or kick Delane inside and Sneed to the boundary. The Chiefs’ pass rush The most frustrating part of this game was that the Chiefs pass rush did nothing against a shaky Seattle offensive line. The Chiefs finished with zero sacks and only one player hitting Darnold (defensive end George Karlaftis had two quarterback hits, per Pro Football Reference ). Watching the game back, the thing that was noticeable was that the Chiefs got no interior pressure in this game. Sam Darnold never had to throw in muddy pockets. He could step up freely to avoid R Mason Thomas and George Karlaftis off the edge. The stats back this up. Chris Jones finished this game with zero pressures. Peter Woods had zero pressures. Khyris Tonga had one and Felix Anudike-Uzomah had two to lead their interior pass rush. The 250 lb edge player. The issue is, this has been the case all year. Jones has 13 pressures in six games . That’s a low amount for a player like Jones. Jones only had 18 in six games to start last year and then turned it on when the season was desperate. But he hasn’t looked great this year. It looks harder for him to get upfield and turn the quick corner that he used to be great at. Woods has also brought no juice as a pass rusher this year. He has two pressures all year and has a 2.3% pressure rate . The Chiefs put Anudike-Uzomah on the field on third downs over Woods because Woods has struggled to get any pressure. The issue with this is the Chiefs defensive ends aren’t big enough to rush inside. Anudike-Uzomah is 250 lbs and struggles to move guards backwards. Ashton Gillotte got chances to do that in this game and it didn’t look great. You want Thomas and Karlaftis running around the edge because they are good at that. But if there isn’t any interior pressure, you allow quarterbacks to freely step into the pocket and hit receivers. The Chiefs need their defensive tackles to play better for this to be a great defense.
author: Nate Christensen

title: What to know about the Chiefs signing Justin Tucker to the practice squad
summary: On Wednesday morning, we led “Arrowheadlines” with rumors that the Kansas City Chiefs would be bringing in competition for kicker Harrison Butker. Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star followed up a few hours later with a more notable name than anyone expected: Justin Tucker, reportedly being signed to the practice squad today. In his […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday morning, we led “Arrowheadlines” with rumors that the Kansas City Chiefs would be bringing in competition for kicker Harrison Butker. Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star followed up a few hours later with a more notable name than anyone expected: Justin Tucker, reportedly being signed to the practice squad today . In his 13-year career with the Baltimore Ravens , Tucker is a five-time first-team All-Pro, seven-time Pro Bowler, and a member of the All-Decade team from the 2010s. He also hasn’t played football since 2024, a primary factor being the 10-game suspension the NFL hit him with in the summer of 2025; the discipline stemmed from 16 accusations of “inappropriate sexual behavior” by massage therapists. Tucker has denied the allegations. He had a rough final season in Baltimore, and the Ravens called cutting ties with their all-time placekicker a “football decision” at the time, but it’s hard to overlook the suspension-worthy allegations, which ranged from 2012-2016, according to McDowell’s report in The Star . The Chiefs worked out several kickers Tuesday and Justin Tucker went 30-for-30 — a reminder of what one of the most accurate kickers in NFL history can do. Tucker already served a 10-week suspension last season, so if the Chiefs need him, he’s eligible to kick Sunday. pic.twitter.com/eUAgLdyeLH — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 28, 2026 After a Pro Bowl campaign in 2023, a season that ended in an AFC Championship loss to the Chiefs, Tucker’s field-goal percentage dropped to 73% in 2024 with multiple missed point-after attempts for the first time in five years. Earlier this season, he tried out for the Miami Dolphins , but the winless Dolphins (at the time) went with Zane Gonzalez instead. According to Jesse Newell of The Athletic , the Chiefs were the fifth team since his suspension to host him for a tryout. In Kansas City, Tucker reportedly beat out former Missouri Tigers kicker Harrison Mevis — who was released by the Los Angeles Rams a few weeks ago — and Ben Sauls, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network . On Wednesday afternoon, head coach Andy Reid answered questions about the signing of Tucker, starting with the team’s stance on Tucker’s allegations of sexual misconduct. “He’s done his suspension, he took care of that business there,” Reid said. “I’ll leave it at that for you.” “We try to do our homework the best way we possibly can,” Reid assured. “Talk to a lot of people, make sure things are okay.” First look at Chiefs practice squad kicker Justin Tucker, who was shagging kicking balls before practice Wednesday. pic.twitter.com/oazhubGDp6 — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) October 28, 2026 Reid shared with local media that Tucker “did really well” in his tryout against two other kickers, but clarified that Butker is still the active kicker. He said Butker “will probably go his week” when asked if Tucker would be ready to contribute immediately. Reid added that Butker would “get most of the reps this week,” suggesting Tucker will get practice time with the starting field-goal unit. Butker has struggled over the last two games, missing three field goals and a point-after attempt. “Harrison, we love Harrison… he’s one of my favorite guys,” Reid shared. “Sometimes, things don’t go quite the way you want them, and you work at that. He understands the business and how it works, and we had a practice-squad position open, so for security, we brought him in and put him in that spot that we had open. Butker gets it, and he knows that that’s part of this business. He’s struggled a little bit, and he gets it; he needs to pick it up here a little bit.” “He’s been up and down a little bit; this happens,” Reid continued. “Like anybody else in this business, myself included, you have to pick it up and do better. So he gets that, and that’s where he sits right now.”‘ “Right now, his technique is off a bit; it’s not as consistent as he wants it,” Reid shared. Travis Kelce told Justin Tucker he needed to move because their QB Patrick Mahomes had to warm up. So Kelce kicked his ball away and threw his helmet. 😂 pic.twitter.com/pFF0DC1yA7 — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) January 28, 2024 The most memorable moment in Tucker’s career in relation to the Chiefs was the pre-game antics from the 2023 season’s AFC Championship. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce kicked and threw equipment of Tucker’s away from where they were warming up on the field. Currently, Tucker appears to be insurance for the possibility that Butker cannot improve moving forward.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Third-down failures doomed the Chiefs’ offense in Seattle
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their first game of the season Sunday night to the Seattle Seahawks, 20-3. The game was one of the Chiefs’ worst offensive showings in the franchise’s current era, and they’ll need to regroup. No phase of the offense was good, but the Chiefs’ inability to sustain drives and convert on […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their first game of the season Sunday night to the Seattle Seahawks , 20-3. The game was one of the Chiefs’ worst offensive showings in the franchise’s current era, and they’ll need to regroup. No phase of the offense was good, but the Chiefs’ inability to sustain drives and convert on third downs doomed them. The Chiefs converted just three of 11 third downs, which helped them muster only a field goal in a game where each team had just eight total offensive drives. With so few possessions, every third down carried extra weight, and while the Chiefs converted two fourth downs, third-down issues stalled drives and kept them from even coming close to the end zone. A look at the film The Chiefs converted their first third-down look of the game, but an untimely illegal shift called on tight end Travis Kelce eliminated a 12-yard reception from Kenneth Walker and would have set up a third-and-12. Kelce attempted to redeem himself, but Mahomes pass was off line. The Seahawks were playing zone, but Kelce did a good job of finding an open space and found himself open between the defender and the sideline. At the line of scrimmage, Seattle showed multiple rushers, but ended up only bringing four. Khalil Benson and Josh Ezeudu both get help from chip blocks, and they pick up the Seahawks’ pass rush. Mahomes has time and room to step up in the pocket, but his pass sails wide and flies out of bounds. Mahomes is likely no more frustrated with the throw than anyone, and the early wasted opportunity would set the tone for what followed. On the Chiefs’ next drive, Seattle’s pass rush would get the better of the backup tackles. Without help from a chip block, Ezeudu ends up going against Seattle edge Derick Hall. The defense walks up players at the line of scrimmage pre-snap, forcing Mahomes to switch from a slide right to a “man-on-man” look. With Creed Humphrey on the nose tackle and Trey Smith going agaisnt the three-technique, this leaves Ezeudu one-on-one with Hall, who is rushing from wide. Building speed, Hall hits his bend point and slips past Ezeudu, laying a big hit on Mahomes. The pass falls incomplete, and the quick pressure prevented the Chiefs from getting anything going. Third and long was not kind to the Chiefs, and neither was third and short. On an early third-and-short, the Chiefs actually had a chance at a deep shot, but Seattle was ready to stop it. From under center, the offensive line sells run initially while Mahomes boots out, and Walker heads to the flat. This look has been effective for the Chiefs in short-yardage situations through the years, but Seattle was ready and packed the flats tightly, while ensuring a quick throw from Mahomes. Unfortunately for the offense, wide receiver Xavier Worthy was on track to be open for a potential chunk play due to the space between him and the high safety. Mahomes ultimately didn’t give the deep ball much of a chance and tried to thread one to Walker. The offense converted on fourth and short the next play, but this was one of its few chances for a chunk play all day. The failure to execute was consistent, but Seattle’s defense deserves credit for taking away go-to looks and baiting them into certain situations. On third-and-7, the offense goes to a familiar look, a mesh concept designed to create separation underneath for receivers and yard-after-catch situations. This play is best against man defenses, or when teams bring pressure. On the snap, Seattle pressures only four, and the offensive line does a good job picking up the slant to the right while Benson washes Hall upfield. This opens a void to the left, and reading the man defense, Mahomes takes off. The trap was set. Mahomes expects cornerback Devon Weatherspoon to run with Worthy, but at the last second, Weatherspoon steps up and forces Mahomes to slow up while the safety picks up Worthy from depth. Mahomes retreats and tries to look downfield, but he is blindsided by Hall, who was hot in pursuit. The hit results in a strip, and Mahomes is lucky to get the ball back. The Seahawks induced Mahomes into leaving the pocket early and were rewarded for the deception. The bad offensive day continued for Kansas City, and toward the end of the game, the Chiefs sacrificed route runners to ensure that Mahomes could remain upright in the pocket. Emmett Johnson and Travis Kelce both give help with chip blocks, delaying them off the line of scrimmage. Seattle’s secondary plays the sticks, and all three Chiefs receivers stop their routes at the sticks, effectively taking themselves out of the play. Mahomes steps up and fires a pass, but Kelce doesn’t expect it, and the ball flies off his chest, incomplete. The bottom line The Chiefs offense has issues, and third-down struggles highlighted them. The strain of having two players lining up at tackle who weren’t in the conversation to start the season before camp remains, even with Benson playing well as a rookie. Injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice have severely limited the downfield passing game, and with Walker and the run game stuffed early, the team quickly abandoned the run, especially when they fell behind on multiple possessions. Not every defense the Chiefs face will be at the same caliber or speed as Seattle’s, but the team must find a solution to the problems they face on Sunday night. As the trade deadline approaches, it will be worth watching whether the team goes after help at skill positions or adds depth along the offensive line.
author: Caleb James

title: The AP Staff’s Week 8 NFL Power Rankings, Halloween edition
summary: There is now one remaining undefeated and one remaining team yet to taste victory this season. And just like everyone expected, the Minnesota Vikings are the lone unbeaten, while the Los Angeles Chargers are winless. We say it each week, but the NFL is unpredictable and uncertain. It’s full of tricks and treats. Halloween is […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is now one remaining undefeated and one remaining team yet to taste victory this season. And just like everyone expected, the Minnesota Vikings are the lone unbeaten, while the Los Angeles Chargers are winless. We say it each week, but the NFL is unpredictable and uncertain. It’s full of tricks and treats. Halloween is this Saturday, and it’s spooky season. So, it’s time for a Halloween edition of the Arrowhead Pride power rankings. On Halloween night, some houses are known for giving out the good candy. Similarly, some teams have given their fans king-size candy bars, while others have kept the porch light off and given little to cheer about. Although the Vikings remain undefeated, they are far from a perfect football team. Every NFL team has warts and reasons to worry. In this Halloween edition of the power rankings, we ask: what should frighten each fanbase for the remainder of the season? Biggest riser: Tampa Bay Buccaneers +7 Biggest faller: Baltimore Ravens -7 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. Buffalo Bills (3rd) James Cook’s fumbling issue. He has four fumbles on the season. 2. Minnesota Vikings (4th) They may be 6-0, but the (second) quarterback they shipped out of town is now playing better than the current quarterback under center. 3. San Francisco 49ers (1st) Their first loss on the season coming in a trap game against the middling Atlanta Falcons . 4. Seattle Seahawks (10th) Guard Quenton Nelson’s arrival should help their running game. But outside of his throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Sam Darnold hasn’t played well this season. 5. Chicago Bears (5th) Caleb Williams can clearly make any throw on the football field. But is their defense good enough to carry them in the loaded NFC North? 6. Kansas City Chiefs (2nd) I could write an essay on what Chiefs fans fear after that dreadful performance on Sunday night. Top of the list is the seemingly never-ending issue at wide receiver, and the lack of a pass rush. Oh, and the rapid decline of the once-reliable kicker Harrison Butker. This is just to name a few. 7. Jacksonville Jaguars (8th) Brian Thomas Jr.’s career has fallen off a cliff since a great rookie debut. 8. Cincinnati Bengals (9th) I don’t like the rumors I’m hearing about the Bengals trading for Jonathan Taylor. That would shore up one of the only perceived weaknesses on their roster. 9. New England Patriots (7th) The lack of chemistry between quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver AJ Brown. Brown has missed time this season due to a high ankle sprain. But in three games, he has only 9 receptions for 101 yards. 10. Pittsburgh Steelers (14th) Aaron Rodgers is having a respectable season for his last dance. But throwing your employer (and all other NFL owners) under the bus in your post-game press conference is not a great look. 11. Denver Broncos (11th) Bo Nix has regressed and Jaylen Waddle has been a non-factor since joining the club. 12. Detroit Lions (13th) Their defense seems to be improving, but it remains a major liability if they’re to be a serious NFC contender. 13. Baltimore Ravens (6th) Lamar Jackson’s health. When will he return to the lineup? Jackson has started only one full season in his nine-year career. 14. Green Bay Packers (12th) An offense that relies on the deep ball and a defense that can’t rely on Micah Parsons’ availability. 15. Cleveland Browns (16th) Their slow starts. They look inept for three quarters before turning it on in the fourth. 16. Los Angeles Rams (17th) They’ve suffered four more losses so far than some in the media thought they would for the entirety of the season. They’ve had major injuries on both sides of the ball. But beyond the injuries, they’ve just continued to shoot themselves in the foot. 17. New York Giants (20th) Putting their hopes in JJ McCarthy seems risky. 18. Atlanta Falcons (21st) Potentially more offensive weapons than any team in the league—but unable to put it together on a weekly basis. 19. Carolina Panthers (15th) A team that just can’t seem to get over the hump and take the next step into formidable contender. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (27th) A 30-point divisional win is nothing to scoff at. But Baker Mayfield threw for only 64 yards in his return. Is he healthy and ready for the remainder of the season? 21. Houston Texans (18th) Their defense is not what it was billed to be before the season. It was assumed they would turn it on after an 0-4 start, but the hole is pretty deep. I’ve said it before—but fortunately for them, they play in the AFC South. 22. Las Vegas Raiders (19th) They haven’t won a game since head coach Klint Kubiak declared at halftime against the Chiefs they would win the game (they didn’t). 23. Dallas Cowboys (22nd) A defense that only looks formidable against backup quarterbacks. 24. Philadelphia Eagles (24th) Legal ramifications from the handling of Jalen Hurt’s blood clot medical emergency. 25. New Orleans Saints (23rd) Quarterback Tyler Shough is playing good football—good enough to win. But the Saints’ running game is pathetic. Their effort on Sunday? 17 rushes for 18 yards. 26. Indianapolis Colts (26th) Who will be playing for this team—or coaching this team in November? The fire sale has already begun in Indy. Josh Downs to Kansas City, anyone? 27. Washington Commanders (29th) Jayden Daniels has not won a football game in over a calendar year. A real concern for your franchise quarterback—not to mention the repeated elbow injuries. 28. New York Jets (28th) Head coach Aaron Glenn losing the football team. 29. Arizona Cardinals (25th) A top five running back who can’t stay on the field, and has yet to burst onto the scene. But they’re good for a win to knock you out of your Survivor league every 2-3 weeks. 30. Miami Dolphins (31st) Potentially losing the number one overall draft pick by winning a game. Although did the ‘72 Dolphins pop open their champagne the Dolphins wouldn’t go 0-17? 31. Tennessee Titans (30th) Head coach Robert Saleh’s devotion to Cam Ward. He just hasn’t looked good, and certainly not what he was billed to be as the first overall draft pick. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd) They have more players listed on their injury report than fans at their home games.
author: Dakota Watson

title: Chiefs Mailbag: Will other teams follow Seattle’s game plan?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The Chiefs are now 5-1 after falling 20-3 to the Seattle Seahawks in possibly the worst performance of the Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes pairing. Let’s see what’s on […]
full_text: Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs are now 5-1 after falling 20-3 to the Seattle Seahawks in possibly the worst performance of the Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes pairing. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds. Papajazz asks: Did the Seahawks show the rest of our opponents how to beat us? Granted they have a ferocious defense but still….. The Seattle game showed us that the best way to beat the Chiefs is to have a defense that ranks in the top two in expected points added (EPA) in both run plays and pass plays. Seattle is currently ranked second in both categories with a -0.22 defensive EPA on pass plays and a -0.16 EPA against the run (these figures do count their dominant performance against Kansas City). While Kansas City’s effort was especially embarrassing, Seattle’s combination of talent at all three levels should allow the Seahawks to have a top-notch game plan against any team. Every team would love to do what Seattle did. But the reigning champs may be the only squad able to pull off what they did for four quarters. I think Seattle was so rested and prepared that they would have won that game against almost anything the Chiefs could have done. But I think Kansas City’s offensive performance would have been more respectable with the top passing game option in Rashee Rice available and Jaylon Moore available at right tackle. Denver’s defensive staff surely watched the game for some ideas on what they can do after being embarrassed in Week 1. I am sure the Broncos will come out with a Walker-focused game plan after he torched them for 177 yards to open the season. But the same middle-of-the-defense problem remains. Denver is currently fifth-worst in the league in run defense EPA and is averaging 133 rushing yards allowed per game (29th). Stopping Walker will probably require formations that put their top-five pass defense at a disadvantage. I have concerns coming out of Sunday. But I also think Seattle is so good defensively that I am going to treat it as a one-of-one occurrence until other teams are having similar success against Kansas City. Sadeeki asks: Last nights game gave off Tampa Bay/Philly Super Bowl vibes. Every team has a “bad game” here and there but do we have a solid fix for the O line? I won’t put all the blame on the offensive line for Sunday. Every concern the Chiefs’ first five games have raised — tackle play, wide receiver depth, inconsistent pass rush, leaky third-down defense, undependable kicking — played a part in the loss. In both those infamous Super Bowls, the Chiefs had already shuffled the offensive line to the point that the depth was exhausted. The Chiefs have performed admirably on the offensive line in the absence of left tackle Josh Simmons, who I would be surprised to see play in 2026 for the Chiefs (if ever again) at this point. However, the absence of Jaylon Moore seemed to push the overall system past the point of functionality. Other than the remote possibility Simmons returns later this season, there is not really a fix. Joshua Ezeudu did not perform well in his first start of the season, but he is a veteran who hopefully would perform better if he gets a second chance (likely against a less dangerous defense). Rookie Diego Pounds is a total unknown, and I would be surprised to see him called upon unless absolutely necessary. We probably won’t know what the team thinks about him until next year’s training camp. OzarkEd asks: Will we address any of our shortcomings before the trade deadline? Reading our comments and other Chiefs-related social media, we should be fine if general manager Brett Veach can just add a starting left tackle, one elite wide receiver (or two good ones), a tight end that can be a successor to Travis Kelce, an edge rusher capable of double-digit sacks, a linebacker and a starting safety at the trade deadline. Obviously, Veach is not going to be able to pull off much, if any, of this list. I do predict a couple of players will be acquired via trade. I am fully expecting to be underwhelmed with anyone coming in. But I do think that if the Chiefs could add a wide receiver with the potential to be a cornerstone in what will probably be a rebuilt passing game in 2027, they would probably consider making a major trade. There are signs that this may be a less active trade deadline than previous years, although the Indianapolis Colts are off to a strong start. The main thing that I could see being a barrier to trades is how many teams will still be firmly in the running for division races on November 10. Three divisions — the AFC North, NFC North and NFC South — are wide open for all four teams. So many teams having clear paths to the postseason could mean fewer teams are motivated to sell — and that more teams are competing for the fewer players who are available. Andyreidsmustache_ asks: Up until this season I’ve been patient with Butker since his injury, but it really can’t be denied anymore. He’s more than, “just a bit off” as Andy would put it. Cutting him isn’t an option as he’d essentially be around 7 million in dead money (space we can’t afford). What realistic options do we have? We have covered Butker’s contract multiple times in this column. Cutting Butker at this point would be cap neutral. The Chiefs would still owe him the remainder of his 2026 base salary, and then they would lose cap space when his replacement was signed. Even if Butker finishes the season on the roster, I very much expect Butker to be released in the spring as the Chiefs start making 2027 salary cap moves. Missing two field goals in a game that was still a two-score game entering the fourth quarter should raise the stakes in how the Chiefs approach Butker moving forward. Kansas City has real questions on both sides of the ball, and the team will probably be in multiple close games in the difficult stretch of the season ahead. With an open practice squad spot, perhaps the Chiefs add a kicker to give Butker some urgency to improve his performance. I still suspect that adding a kicker would be accompanied by Butker going on the Reserve/Injured list with a conveniently previously unknown ailment. DualBlock asks: How badly will Broncos quarterback Bo Nix torch us next week? I am much more concerned about a talented Broncos defense rising to the occasion on Sunday than I am about Nix. Nix currently has a -0.1 EPA per dropback. The third-year pro is completing less than 60% of his passes and averaging less than six yards per attempt. Three times this season, Nix has failed to pass for 150 yards. The Broncos are coming off of their best full-game performance of the year in defeating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on Sunday. They are a much better team than what we saw in Week 1. But I would also be willing to bet that, should Denver take a significant step forward Sunday in defending their AFC West crown, it will be because of the defense building on what happened in Week 7, rather than Nix. Nix will probably play better than he did in Week 1. But I will also be surprised if the Chiefs surrender a 62-yard rushing touchdown to him as Arizona did. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be back after the Chiefs face the Broncos in a game that could ultimately determine how the AFC West is won. Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.
author: Jared Sapp

title: Chiefs News: Harrison Butker may have competition amid struggles
summary: Last week, before the Kansas City Chiefs’ loss that featured two missed field goals by kicker Harrison Butker, the Arrowhead Pride community voiced its frustration with the team’s long-time placekicker. 71% of voters in The Feed’s poll said that they viewed Butker as a problem. The NFL Transactions Report recorded no visit from external options […]
full_text: (Photo by Bruce Yeung/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, before the Kansas City Chiefs ’ loss that featured two missed field goals by kicker Harrison Butker, the Arrowhead Pride community voiced its frustration with the team’s long-time placekicker. 71% of voters in The Feed’s poll said that they viewed Butker as a problem . The NFL Transactions Report recorded no visit from external options at kicker on Tuesday, but Jason Anderson of 810 Sports was “told the Chiefs have at least one kicker in town working out.” In the post on X , Anderson noted a practice-squad signing had likelihood. If he’s correct, we’ll likely know by this afternoon. Charles Goldman of A to Z Sports reminded Chiefs Kingdom that another player on the team has placekicking experience in a Tuesday article. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Kansas City Chiefs have in-house option to explore as Harrison Butker’s kicking issues intensify in Week 7 loss to Seahawks | A to Z Sports So what can the Chiefs realistically do to ease Butker’s burden? For starters, they might want to lean more on the other player in the specialist room: starting punter Matt Araiza. If you’re not familiar with his background, Araiza also kicked in college at San Diego State. He didn’t take over as a full-time punter until his final season, when he earned the nickname “Punt God.” Over three seasons, Araiza made 50-of-68 field goals, with a 53-yard long make. He was also 96-of-97 on extra points. These five Chiefs flaws were exposed in Seattle. Here’s how solvable they are | The Kansas City Star Jones, 32, did not tally a single quarterback pressure in Seattle. His pressure rate for the season is 7.3%, the lowest since Next Gen Stats began tracking that statistic in 2018. He is on pace for 45 pressures, if he plays a full season, which would be a considerable dip — he hasn’t finished with fewer than 58 pressures in a season since 2017. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Chargers avoided making any changes to the coaching staff at their bye week, the news we all expected to hear finally came on Wednesday. Per The Athletic’s Noah Furtado, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will retain play-calling duties despite the unit being the league’s worst scoring offense (15.0). Jim Harbaugh said Chargers OC Mike McDaniel will continue to call plays. — Noah Furtado (@bynoahfurtado) October 28, 2026 The Chargers were still in the basement of offensive rankings before their Week Six game against the Chiefs, but the six total points scored right before the bye sunk them to rock bottom in the NFL. McDaniel has been the biggest recipient of blame so far during the Chargers’ 0-6 start to the season. And if we’re being honest, it’s been for good reason. The team’s star quarterback looks like a genuine backup, the unit’s other top players are either hurt or greatly underperforming, and it’s all happening under McDaniel’s watch. The former Dolphins head coach was lauded as an offensive genius and expectations were beyond sky-high this offseason. Those expectations were also fairly unanimous around league circles. But here we are, seven weeks into one of the worst seasons for the Chargers this century, and not a single change was made during the bye. Jim Harbaugh is tethering his future to McDaniel with zero reasons to justify it. But as a longtime coach who has done nothing but win until this season, he still deserves the benefit of the doubt. But that benefit is withering away fast with each new loss.

title: Rams don’t have an impressive win on resume
summary: Seven weeks into the season and it’s still unclear exactly who the Los Angeles Rams are this year. They lost to the 49ers in a weird season opener with international travel as a confounding variable. LA also dropped close games to the Denver Broncos, Buffalo Bills, and Arizona Cardinals. Arizona aside, that’s three losses to […]
full_text: Seven weeks into the season and it’s still unclear exactly who the Los Angeles Rams are this year. They lost to the 49ers in a weird season opener with international travel as a confounding variable. LA also dropped close games to the Denver Broncos, Buffalo Bills, and Arizona Cardinals. Arizona aside, that’s three losses to teams who figure into the playoff picture for their respective conferences. Add in the wins and things get even more confusing. The Rams beat the New York Giants in Week 2. Jaxson Dart was injured early. Jameis Winston was inept in replacement, and he’s since been replaced in the starting lineup by JJ McCarthy. LA defeated the Philadelphia Eagles prior to them falling off a cliff. In Week 4 they were missing DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, and Lane Johnson entering the game. Saquon Barkley exited early and did not return. Part of the subsequent downfall of Philadelphia is attributable to Jalen Hurts’ absence, but it’s fair to question whether the Eagles were a good team before all their attrition. And then there are the Raiders, who started the season 3-0 before falling to 3-4 following last weekend’s loss to the Rams. The fact that Las Vegas is encouraged by a 3-4 start tells you they didn’t expect to compete much this season. While the Rams handled them solidly, the Raiders did show life in the second half. Overall, in one way to read it, we can say the Rams lost to the 1-4 Cardinals and then bounced back against a bad Raiders team. Their two other wins aren’t anything to hang their hat on either. The Rams have yet to beat a good team. That may be an overly pessimistic view. It certainly does not tell the whole story. The difficult truth is we might not know who the Rams truly are for some time. Wins over the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders, and Arizona Cardinals in the next three weeks for the bye don’t move the needle. Losing to these teams could confirm that LA isn’t as good as they expected to be entering the year. The Rams host the Green Bay Packers the day before Thanksgiving and then the Chiefs the following week. They have games to follow against the 49ers and Cowboys before seeing the Seahawks in two out of the three final games of the regular season. We might not know who the Rams are until the final moments before the playoffs. The coming weeks can only prove they are a pretender. Establishing themselves as a contender must come later. The encouraging news is that the Rams, if they can make it to the bye week unscathed, should expect reinforcements coming out of their bye before their schedule grows more competitive. Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson, Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, and others could potentially return in time for the daunting finale. Beating the Giants, Eagles, and Raiders doesn’t tell me who you are. We won’t truly learn much about the Rams until the calendar turns from November into December and thereafter.

full_text: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said neither Myles Garrett nor Terrance Ferguson will return to practice this week . Both players are currently on injured reserve and hey can re-join practice during a 21-day practice window without counting against the 53-man roster, but that isn’t close to happening. The Rams must move them to the roster within the 21-day ramp up period or Garrett and Ferguson would revert to season-ending injured reserve. However, this doesn’t even matter until McVay opens the 21-day window and it seems every week goes by without good news. After Sean McVay expressed optimism that Myles Garrett would practice this week… it’s another week of no practice. The wait continues. https://t.co/qv5e7SyNBa — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 28, 2026 The fact neither player is practicing could mean the team is concerned about their ability to return within three weeks. Should we expect to see Garrett or Ferguson soon? LA has three games remaining until their Week 11 bye. The Rams will host the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium, take a trip to the east coast against the Washington Commanders, and then prepare for their road rematch versus the Arizona Cardinals. In terms of the most likely outcome, it feels like Garrett and Ferguson are progressing towards a Week 12 appearance against the Green Bay Packers the day before Thanksgiving. That timing also aligns with the three-week ramp up practice window. Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson will not practice this week, Sean McVay said. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) October 28, 2026 On a positive note, McVay also provided an update on Davante Adams. Adams suffered a serious hamstring injury and recently had surgery. He’s a week into the originally reported 6-10 weeks of recovery time . McVay said the veteran receiver is trending towards the earlier side of that spectrum. The Rams must keep winning in order for future injury reinforcements to matter. Garrett and Ferguson have been absent longer than expected, although fans won’t remember how long they were out if they bolster the team into a playoff run.

title: Rams sign Joshua Karty to practice squad
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are bringing back a familiar face to their special teams unit, signing kicker Joshua Karty to the practice squad on Wednesday. The move comes just days after Los Angeles signed veteran kicker Brandon McManus ahead of Week 7, making Karty’s return an interesting development as the team continues searching for consistency […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are bringing back a familiar face to their special teams unit, signing kicker Joshua Karty to the practice squad on Wednesday. The move comes just days after Los Angeles signed veteran kicker Brandon McManus ahead of Week 7, making Karty’s return an interesting development as the team continues searching for consistency at the position. According to the team’s announcement, Los Angeles also signed long snapper Jake McQuaide and linebacker Jon Rhattigan to the practice squad. The Rams have cycled through multiple kickers amid their special teams struggles, and Karty’s return provides additional depth at a position that has become a concern. LA Rams Roster Moves: • Signed to Practice Squad K Joshua Karty, LS Jake McQuaide, ILB Jon Rhattigan • Terminated (by Club) from Practice Squad OL Austin Blaske, CB Nyzier Fourqurean, ILB Elias Neal pic.twitter.com/hUmGO4Yf8u — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 28, 2026 Karty was selected by the Rams in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Stanford. He made a solid impression during his rookie campaign, converting 29 of 34 field-goal attempts (85.3%) and 32 of 36 extra-point attempts. However, his performance declined during the 2025 season, when he made just 10 of 15 field goals and 23 of 26 extra points before Los Angeles released him. Across 25 regular-season games with the Rams, Karty converted 39 of 49 field-goal attempts and scored 172 points. NO GOOD. 😬 Rams kicker Joshua Karty misses the 53-yarder wide right — points left on the field. 🐏 #RamsHouse #NFL pic.twitter.com/2bxtms2VA9 — Aggregate (@AggregateSports) October 3, 2025 After being waived by Los Angeles in November 2025, Karty initially returned to the Rams on their practice squad. The Arizona Cardinals then signed him off that practice squad in December, giving him another opportunity elsewhere in the NFC West. Arizona re-signed Karty in April 2026, but released him in June, leaving him available to return to Los Angeles. He did not appear in a game for Arizona during his previous stint with the organization. The timing of Karty’s return is particularly noteworthy. The Rams signed McManus on October 20 after Blake Grupe suffered a season-ending knee injury during his debut against the Arizona Cardinals. McManus was brought in after Harrison Mevis struggled earlier in the season, adding to Los Angeles’ revolving door at kicker. Karty’s practice-squad signing does not necessarily mean the Rams are preparing to replace McManus. Instead, it gives the team another option while providing Karty with a chance to rebuild his confidence and potentially work his way back onto the active roster. For a Rams team trying to stabilize its special teams, reuniting with a former draft pick is a move worth watching. Whether Karty eventually gets another opportunity to kick in a game remains to be seen, but Los Angeles is clearly keeping its options open. If Joshua Karty is back to do knuckleball kickoffs I’m good with it. They were effective early last season. #Ramshouse pic.twitter.com/NEH3H6eShk https://t.co/BrnDBlMv2e — 🖤 Christine (@christinelu) October 28, 2026 The Los Angeles Rams could have a specific role in mind for Joshua Karty beyond simply providing insurance at kicker. Karty has experience using a knuckleball-style kickoff, a technique that can create unpredictable ball movement and make returns more difficult for opposing special teams. With the Sean McVay recently commenting on his frustrations with kickoff coverage, bringing Karty back could allow them to experiment with that approach while keeping Brandon McManus available for field goals and extra points. Although there is no confirmation that this is Los Angeles’ plan, Karty’s kickoff ability could provide an interesting wrinkle for a struggling unit.

title: Rams called good fit for reunion with A’Shawn Robinson
summary: The Los Angeles Rams already reunited with one defensive tackle on the 2021 Super Bowl team, is it time to trade for another? ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler named 25 players who could be traded before next month’s deadline and A’Shawn Robinson was called a good fit for the Rams. Robinson played for the Rams from 2020 […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams already reunited with one defensive tackle on the 2021 Super Bowl team, is it time to trade for another? ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler named 25 players who could be traded before next month’s deadline and A’Shawn Robinson was called a good fit for the Rams. Robinson played for the Rams from 2020 to 2022, and was a beast in the 2021 playoffs en route to winning the Super Bowl. Robinson had 22 tackles and a sack in four playoff games that year. What Fowler is hearing: Robinson is a name that a few teams floated to me because he’s still a productive interior player and a veteran who could help a contending team. He also wouldn’t cost much to acquire at this stage. He has played for four other teams — the Lions, Rams, Panthers and Giants — so he has coaching friends all over the league. Fowler gave it a 30% chance that Robinson would be traded. Analyst Matt Bowen gave Robinson a film breakdown. What Bowen sees on tape: At 6-3 and 320 pounds, Robinson is a powerful run defender who can play as a 1-technique nose or 3-technique defensive tackle. While Robinson doesn’t provide pass-rushing upside (16 career sacks), he can push the interior of the pocket. He’s an early-down defender who could help out a defensive line rotation. He even has two interceptions this season! ESPN cite the Rams, Ravens, and Giants as good fits for Robinson. Robinson has spent the last two seasons with the Carolina Panthers, playing for former Rams assistant coach Ejiro Evero. He’s 31 and has only missed one game in the past four years. This season is his first with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Robinson has 20 tackles with a sack. Tampa Bay just destroyed the Panthers and are climbing back into the NFC South race despite being 2-5. So they probably aren’t in a hurry to trade anyone. The Bucs are a top-five run defense and Robinson is an important piece in that. It may take another two losses for Tampa Bay to talk trade, but the Rams really need someone like Robinson. Aaron Donald is the best defensive lineman on the Rams this season, especially because Kobie Turner and Poona Ford are both injured. L.A. could use more beef on the defensive line. ESPN’s Dan Graziano chimed on what the Rams must be thinking after seeing the Seahawks and 49ers make trades for new starters on Tuesday: Graziano: Yeah, Tuesday was a big day in the NFC West arms race. It makes me wonder what the Rams are thinking. They obviously made their big moves in the offseason, but things haven’t worked, and everyone’s favorite superteam has fallen behind the 49ers and Seahawks in the division. I wonder whether there’s another move for the Rams to make — they could use a speedy wide receiver if one is available — and whether they still have the draft picks and/or desire to add more to a roster that was already supposed to be loaded. Jauan Jennings was another player mentioned as a trade candidate for the Rams. The former 49ers receiver is toiling away on the Vikings and not getting any targets.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Former Rams’ kicker held ‘impressive’ workout for Chiefs
summary: Former kicker for the Los Angeles Rams’ Harrison Mevis held an “impressive” workout for the Kansas City Chiefs, along with longtime NFL kicker Justin Tucker. Reportedly the Chiefs went with Tucker due to experience, and not for a lack of effort or impressiveness on Mevis’ part. It’s another example of one’s teams’ discarded kicker being […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Place kicker Harrison Mevis #92 of the Los Angeles Rams makes a first quarter field goal during the NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former kicker for the Los Angeles Rams’ Harrison Mevis held an “impressive” workout for the Kansas City Chiefs, along with longtime NFL kicker Justin Tucker. Reportedly the Chiefs went with Tucker due to experience, and not for a lack of effort or impressiveness on Mevis’ part. The #Chiefs worked out three kickers and kept both Justin Tucker and Harrison Mevis around all day, giving them both physicals after similarly impressive workouts. In the end, with the experience and resume, Tucker gets the PS spot. https://t.co/xNiMwf6wVH — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 28, 2026 It’s another example of one’s teams’ discarded kicker being another teams’ potential answer. In this case, Mevis didn’t get the job, but Tucker will seemingly get the shot to replace Harrison Butker, who has been struggling as the kicker for the Chiefs in 2026. Butker will try to hold his job down with a strong performance against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. Tucker, was not on an NFL team likely due to off the field issue s more than performance, so he’ll perhaps get a new chance with a new team after his time away from the game. For Mevis, he was solid for the Rams in 2025 with 92% of his field goals made. 2026 didn’t go so well for Mevis as he hit about 50% of his kicks before being released by the Rams after his blocked kick in overtime against the Buffalo Bills earlier this year. Sean McVay reported the kick would’ve missed regardless of the block , and that was the final straw for Mevis with the Rams. Of course, with how desperate the Rams have been to find a kicker, though unlikely, maybe Mevis one day makes his return to L.A. By all reports, Mevis is still available, and his latest workout was “impressive”. If not the Rams, then perhaps that “impressive” workout will lead to another gig in the NFL, or another gig in the NFC West.
author: Danny Stone

title: The Rams need to pursue Colts receiver Josh Downs
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams want to keep up with the NFC West arms race, they need to find a way to land Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Downs isn’t a superstar or the best receiver in the league or anything like that, but he is available. He’s attainable and he plays a position […]
full_text: If the Los Angeles Rams want to keep up with the NFC West arms race, they need to find a way to land Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Downs isn’t a superstar or the best receiver in the league or anything like that, but he is available. He’s attainable and he plays a position of major need for the Rams. While the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have already benefited from the Colts’ fire sale this week by trading for Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, it’s time for the Rams to get in on the fun. This would not be a one-for-one replacement for Davante Adams in terms of skill set. Few receivers in the NFL have the technical proficiency Adams does, even in what could be the twilight of his career. That doesn’t mean Downs would be wasted in this offense, however. This is how tightly I’m clinging onto the hope that Josh Downs’ season can get turned around by landing in a cool spot via trade pic.twitter.com/GYIlJKU9Pz — Matt Harmon (@MattHarmon_BYB) October 28, 2026 Big-play threat Downs is a slot receiver. Plenty of wide receivers are effective in the slot or run a bunch of routes there, but no one runs more routes out of the slot than Downs. According to charting from Player Profiler , Downs’s 172 slot snaps are the most in the NFL. That’s not to say that’s all he can do, though. If he plays out of the slot on 53.4% of his snaps, he’s still aligned elsewhere 46.6% of the time. That’s not nothing, clearly. And, just because he’s predominantly a slot player doesn’t mean he’s simply a dink-and-dunk stat compiler. Per Next Gen Stats, Downs is averaging 10.6 air yards per target this season, a huge number and nearly three full yards longer than his previous career high. There’s explosive potential with this player. The Rams want to create as many explosive plays as possible. They need a pass catcher, and he’s there for the taking from a team that is scrapping anything that isn’t nailed down . Of course, L.A. would have to make the dollars and cents work, but a cheap, expiring contract should be workable for this front office. NFC West arms race The other part of this is the fact that the other competitive franchises in the division have already taken swings to improve their team. In fact, both found a way to do that by dealing with Indianapolis. This is not the time for a historically aggressive front office to suddenly get complacent. Discussing the Colts fire sale that started today, on The Insiders. pic.twitter.com/koqWh99LjD — Judy Battista (@judybattista) October 28, 2026 The Seahawks shored up their offensive line Tuesday by sending a pair of picks to the heartland for guard Quenton Nelson. Shortly thereafter, the 49ers reacquired DeForest Buckner for a fourth rounder. That’s a pair of legitimate Super Bowl threats who are sitting ahead of the Rams in the NFC West right now both making noticeable improvements ahead of the trade deadline. Again, this is the time for Les Snead to act. Downs isn’t the only wide receiver who’s on the trade block. If Los Angeles can swing a trade for Brian Thomas Jr. or even someone like Jerry Jeudy , great. But time is of the essence. The Rams can’t afford to fall into a deeper hole. If this team still has Super Bowl aspirations , it can’t sit still at the deadline. Josh Downs is available and, based on the Colts’ other moves this week, he shouldn’t cost an arm and a leg. That sounds like a prime opportunity for the Rams to strike.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Should Rams give Blake Corum the start?
summary: Blake Corum is not the starting running back for the Los Angeles Rams, yet, but should the Rams give Corum a chance to start? Should the Rams give Corum the chance to see what he can do with 20-30 touches in a game? I think the bigger theme is the Rams should lean on their […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Blake Corum is not the starting running back for the Los Angeles Rams, yet , but should the Rams give Corum a chance to start? Should the Rams give Corum the chance to see what he can do with 20-30 touches in a game? I think the bigger theme is the Rams should lean on their ground game, even when trailing sometimes. Williams has been a stud for the Rams. Yes, he’s had some fumbling woes, but he also totes the rock a ton for L.A., and fumbles are a part of the game. Williams may have a bit more burst than Williams, but Williams has plenty of experience. Williams has been a stout pass blocker, Corum is still learning. Corum has likely continued to learn the playbook since joining the Rams, so perhaps he’s ready for more work. That work and development seemed to pay off this past Sunday. If you feel Corum should start over Williams then tell us why and have fun with this hypothetical exercise! Kyren Williams’ Fumble Opens Door for Blake Corum in Rams’ Backfield (athlonsports) “Locked On Rams co-host Gavin Carlson raised the possibility that the distribution reflected more than a standard rotation, pointing to Corum’s heavy involvement after a pass-heavy opening possession. Co-host Travis Rodgers said he was more open to the idea that Williams’ comments following the Arizona Cardinals loss, combined with the turnover against Las Vegas, could have prompted McVay to make a subtle point without removing his starter from the lineup. McVay still has a clear reason to keep Williams heavily involved. The Rams’ unofficial depth chart lists Williams ahead of Corum, and Carlson noted that Williams maintained a substantial edge in passing-game usage against the Raiders. Rodgers argued that pass protection remains especially important with quarterback Matthew Stafford at the center of the offense, making it difficult to treat the rushing split as a full referendum on the starting job.“ Blake Corum says Rams aren’t worried about their playoff chances (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams aren’t focused on their 3-4 record or their playoff chances as they look to build momentum following their Week 7 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . Running back Blake Corum said the message inside the locker room has been to focus on getting better each day rather than looking too far ahead. “No one’s worried about our record. No one’s worried about, oh, you know, are we going to make the playoffs?” Corum said on The Rich Eisen Show . “It’s more so like we know what we have to do. Let’s work and let’s go do it and let’s do it to our best ability.” Rams Face Mounting Trade Deadline Pressure as NFC West Rivals Make Major Moves (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams may have changed the course of their season with a win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but they still have work to do to remain competitive. The NFC West remains one of the more competitive divisions in the NFL. With the Seattle Seahawks trading for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson , and the San Francisco 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner, the pressure is on for the Rams to make a corresponding move if they want to remain competitive with the Seahawks and 49ers. While the 49ers may be the favorites to win the division, the battle for second place and a wild card spot in the playoffs is up for grabs. After the Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, it’s clear they believe they are in position to push for that spot and do what they can to try and repeat. “ Will Puka Nacua’s Body Hold Up? Rams Star Takes the Hits Jaxon Smith-Njigba Avoids (athlonsports) “The show was echoing Roddy White, who said on “Up & Adams” last week, “I don’t know how long he’s going to last in the NFL to be quite honest…he keeps running into everyone, he keeps getting hurt.” White compared Nacua to Cooper Kupp . The history backs the concern. Nacua missed five games in 2024 after re-aggravating a knee injury, sprained an ankle in 2025 and has already missed two games this season . His job doesn’t get any lighter. Nacua played 28 run-blocking snaps against Las Vegas and earned an 80.4 run-blocking grade to go with an 86.8 overall grade, according to PFF. Matthew Stafford called him the most physical receiver “that I’ve ever been around,” and with Davante Adams on injured reserve , the targets keep coming his way. Nacua led the Rams in catches, yards and targets Sunday, even as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum carried the offense on the ground.“ Rams have hardest remaining schedule in NFL based on this metric (ramswire) “The playoffs are still well within reach, but if the Rams are going to make the postseason, they’re certainly going to earn it. According to Ben Baldwin, the Rams’ remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL. That’s based on the average remaining opponent win percentage against a league-average team on a neutral field. The Rams’ schedule is clearly the toughest, with an opponent win percentage of more than 55% in such projections, while the Bengals ’ is by far the easiest, well below 45%.“ First Look: Rams host Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Week 8 (larams.com) “ Selected former Florida offensive lineman Jake Slaughter in the second round of this year’s draft: Slaughter has started every game at center for the Chargers so far this season. Originally competing for the starting left guard job in the preseason, he pivoted to center exclusively after starter Tyler Biadasz sustained a season-ending knee injury in the Chargers’ joint practice with the 49ers on Aug. 18. Top performers in Week 6 (Chargers had a Week 7 bye) Quarterback Justin Herbert completed 22 of 37 pass attempts for 204 yards with one interception in the Chargers’ 22-6 home loss to the Chiefs. Herbert also led the Chargers in rushing with five carries for 26 yards.“ Sean McVay ‘couldn’t care less’ what Chargers’ record is (ramswire) “Sean McVay knows the Chargers haven’t won a game yet, and he “couldn’t care less.” Whether an opponent is 0-6 or 6-0, McVay is fully aware that his team has to be ready because in the NFL, anyone can beat anyone. And as he has said in the past, this league can humble you in a hurry. “Humility is a day away,” McVay said of his message to the team. “This is a good team. The records and stuff, with the way that this season and the way that everything’s gone in this league, anybody can beat anybody. I would hope that we’re mature and professional enough to know that we have to be able to have the right focus, concentration, level of urgency. This is professional football. They have great players. They’re really well coached. I couldn’t care less about what their record is. We’ll get humbled if we’re not ready to go.” Matthew Stafford Jokes His Rams Touchdown Record Means He’s Old as the Chargers Come to Town (sports.yahoo) “Somewhere in Inglewood, a few longtime season-ticket holders who watched Roman Gabriel at the Coliseum just saw his name slide down a list. Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua for a touchdown in the Los Angeles Rams’ 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday, and it gave him 155 touchdown passes with the franchise, one more than Gabriel’s 154. Stafford was asked after the game what it meant. “It just means you’re old and you’ve played a lot of ball,” he said, according to MLive . He also credited the people around him, saying, “Catching touchdowns and throwing touchdowns isn’t a one-man job.” Los Angeles Rams May Have a New Backfield Question After Win (athlonsports) “Williams still produced 99 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, but his lost fumble at the Rams’ 30-yard line gave the Raiders a chance to cut into the lead. Las Vegas failed to capitalize, yet the turnover arrived after Williams had met with McVay to clarify a critical comment in the locker…

title: Raiders practice notes: Jack Bech could play Sunday
summary: Here are some notes from the Las Vegas Raiders’ work day Wednesday as they begin the work week for Sunday’s game at the New York Jets: Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said there is a chance second-year wide receiver Jack Bech could be activated for Sunday’s game. He returned to practice after missing four […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here are some notes from the Las Vegas Raiders’ work day Wednesday as they begin the work week for Sunday’s game at the New York Jets: Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said there is a chance second-year wide receiver Jack Bech could be activated for Sunday’s game. He returned to practice after missing four games with a broken forearm. When Bech is activated, someone will have to be removed from the 53-man roster. Fellow 2025 draft pick and wide receiver Dont’e Thornton is on the roster for this game as well. Reserve defensive end Patrick Johnson was the only Raiders’ player not to practice Wednesday. He suffered a stinger in a Week 7 loss to the Rams. Starting defensive end Kwity Paye was among the Raiders’ players limited in practice, because of rest reasons. Kubiak indicated some backup offensive linemen could get a chance to play as Caleb Rogers and Jackson Powers-Johnson have struggled at right guard. Trey Zuhn or Bryce Cabeldue could get a chance to play. Asked about the potential for trades before the November 10 deadline, Kubiak said Raiders’ general manager John Spytek and his staff is discussing multiple scenarios daily. He added that is the norm in the NFL. For the Jets, standout rookie pass-rusher David Bailey (groin) was among six players who missed practice with a groin injury. Standout running back Breece Hall, who has missed the past several games, was limited with a quad injury.

title: Why does Raider Nation want Kirk Cousins on the bench?
summary: Kirk Cousins has done everything the Las Vegas Raiders expected of him and more. It’s week 8 and he’s leading the NFL in passing touchdowns with 16. The offense has looked competent and is putting up points, but that isn’t enough for Raiders Nation. What is it that Cousins isn’t doing? By itself, those numbers […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins has done everything the Las Vegas Raiders expected of him and more. It’s week 8 and he’s leading the NFL in passing touchdowns with 16. The offense has looked competent and is putting up points, but that isn’t enough for Raiders Nation. What is it that Cousins isn’t doing? By itself, those numbers suggest he’s having one helluva season, which in fact he is. #Raiders coach Klint Kubiak: "Kirk is our starting quarterback. There is no controversy. He is playing at a very high level." — Paul Gutierrez (@PaulHGutierrez) October 26, 2026 Diving into the numbers According to Pro-Football-Reference.com , Cousins’ 60.9% on-target percentage is 27th in the league. Yet, the 151 on-target throws are 9th best. In contrast, the 14.1% bad throw metric is 17th in the league and a razor thin .1% above the league average. However, his 35 bad throws are 7th worst. Plagued by 11 total drops (tied for 4th most) on 4.4% of his throws, 15th most. Once again, Cousins is hanging above the league average (4.2) by a thread. Keeping him yo-yo-ing between good throws more than half the time and an above-average amount of drops. The offensive line is providing 2.0 seconds of pocket time, good enough for 20th in the league. Falling a mere .1 seconds below the league average (2.1). Cousins has put up numbers since returning to head coach Klint Kubiak’s offense. Completing 161 of 257 passes. Out of the 161 completions, 99 have gone to Brock Bowers (who missed the first two games), Ashton Jeanty and Michael Mayer. Wide receivers? Tre Tucker and his 16.3 yards per reception are sixth-best in the league; he has four touchdowns (tied for 4th most), yet only 29 catches on 47 targets. Meanwhile, the rest of the receiving corps are either decoys or just guys getting cardio on the field. Both Jalen Nailor and Cody White have eight receptions each; Jack Bech has five, Malik Benson and Dareke Young each have two. This is one of those plays that’s gonna keep Cousins up late tonight. https://t.co/NheV5C178M pic.twitter.com/CWrZ3H4Hg4 — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) October 26, 2026 While half of Cousins’ passing touchdowns (7) have gone to Tucker (4), Bech (1) and Cody White (3) it really seems as though wide receivers are not being used enough. The real question on the table is Cousin’s arm strength enough to feed his wideouts successfully? The consensus is no. For four straight weeks, defenses have blitzed him in obvious passing downs, forcing him to make off-platform throws and restricting his ability to scan the entire field. Here’s the catch-22: Cousins has been missing open receivers; in fact, due to a declining amount of pocket time, he is foregoing his progressions and locking in on his receivers between the hashes. Staring down receivers has caused them to take big hits, leading to some of those drops and as weeks progress, defenders are getting closer and closer to the football. Help Kirk help the Raiders Playing without a running game is incredibly hard to do. Possessing the escape speed of a three-legged turtle practically makes you a sitting duck. Furthermore, not having enough pocket time for receivers to beat press coverage and get open is a damning trifecta, but Cousins overcame it for as long as he could. Cousins has only 5 interceptions this season and one of them was because his receiver slipped and fell on the route. But there have been many close calls; defensive coordinators have studied his tendencies, finding ways to neutralize him while the game is still competitive. Has he missed throws? Yes. Has he missed reads? Yes. Another one of those missed opportunities in the second quarter that Cousins probably wished he had back. He had Tucker opened under neath. https://t.co/A7LsdpxDGi pic.twitter.com/8t0VYg93Lr — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) October 26, 2026 Is Fernando Mendoza going to be able to come in and play at the level Cousins has been playing at or better? Probably not. He is more physically talented; he may even be versed in the terminology and know how to get in and out of plays. Can Mendoza play and process information faster than Cousins? My money is on no, despite having otherworldly success in a play action and run-pass-option type system in Indiana under Curt Cignetti, 15+ years of experience is only gained one way. As Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said in his press conference on Monday, “Fernando is going to play football. We have a plan. We don’t have a timeline for that. Kirk is playing well, and we’re in the hunt.” So until the Raiders are out of it, Cousins can’t go, or come high water Cap’n Kirk is here to stay.

title: A look at Raiders’ defensive tackle rotation
summary: Tuesday, the Las Vegas Raiders released third-year defensive tackle Jonah Laulu. After playing 67.9 percent of the defensive snaps last season, his play time dwindled to 32 percent and he was inactive twice. Let’s look at the position as the team moves on from Laulu: Tonka Hemingway: The 2025 fourth-round pick has been the Raiders’ […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tuesday, the Las Vegas Raiders released third-year defensive tackle Jonah Laulu. After playing 67.9 percent of the defensive snaps last season, his play time dwindled to 32 percent and he was inactive twice. Let’s look at the position as the team moves on from Laulu: Tonka Hemingway: The 2025 fourth-round pick has been the Raiders’ leading snap getter at the position when healthy. In the first four weeks his snap percentage rate ranged from 52 to 73 percent. He was injured in Week 5 and missed Week 6. He was eased back into action, playing 29 percent of the snaps in Week 7. He has 15 tackles and one sack. Adam Butler: The veteran is averaging 51 percent snap play. He logged 70 percent of the snaps in Week 7, his most of the season. He is definitely a too-of-the-rotation defensive tackle. He has 18 tackles and a half of sack. Foley Fatukasi: Fatukasi, signed in training camp, has become a solid contributor. He’ playing 44 percent of the snaps. He has 12 tackles and a half a sack. Thomas Booker: He was a healthy scratch in Week 7 after he played in the first six games. His snap percentage rate ranged from 32 to 50 percent. It will be interesting to see if he remains inactive in the coming weeks. J.J. Pegues: The 2025 sixth-round draft pick has been active for three games, including the past two. He is averaging 13 percent of the snaps. He forced a fumble in Week 7. It wouldn’t be a surprise if he remains active on game days. Tim Keenan: The rookie — he was drafted in the seventh round by the Rams and signed to the Raiders’ practice squad in September after he was cut — is still on the practice squad. He was elevated for Week 7 and he played in 29 percent of the snaps. He had two tackles. He could be a candidate for the 53-man roster soon. Join the conversation! title: At least Ashton Jeanty is helping as receiver
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 35-21 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the New York Jets. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 72 percent of the snaps, a week after playing […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 35-21 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the New York Jets. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 72 percent of the snaps, a week after playing 58 percent. Jeanty struggled as a rusher again as he had just 15 yards on eight carries. He has averaged less than three yards a carry in five games this season. He did have a season high eight catches for 61 yards. He is tied for the league high among running backs. Jack Bech: The second-round pick is on the injured reserve with a fractured forearm. His practice window is expected to open this week. Darien Porter: The third-round pick played 59 percent of the defensive snaps, his least amount since regaining his starting job three weeks ago. It will be interesting to see how much he plays against the Jets. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick took over for the benched Jackson Powers-Johnson for the second straight week. He did struggle in the running game and will likely have to earn his starting job on a weekly basis. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual, but he did log four snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, was activated from the injured reserve and he will be ready to make his season debut Sunday. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick returned from a concussion he suffered in Week 5. He started and had a sack. But he didn’t have a great overall game. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the third time this season. He played 16 snaps on defense and forced a fumble. It should get him another chance to play this week, especially with Jonah Laulu being released Tuesday. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played three snaps at linebacker. It was his first defensive action of his career. He also played 16 snaps on special teams, which is his norm.

title: Two Dolphins starters in concussion protocol ahead of clash with Patriots
summary: The Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the season by defeating the New York Jets on Sunday by a score of 28-25. Unfortunately, despite the win, they didn’t escape the clash unscathed. On Wednesday, while speaking with the South Florida media, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley announced that starting left guard, Kadyn Proctor, and […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Kadyn Proctor #74 of the Miami Dolphins exits the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the season by defeating the New York Jets on Sunday by a score of 28-25. Unfortunately, despite the win, they didn’t escape the clash unscathed. On Wednesday, while speaking with the South Florida media, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley announced that starting left guard, Kadyn Proctor, and starting cornerback, JuJu Brents, both experienced concussion symptoms earlier this week and are not practicing for Miami as of yet. Proctor played all 65 offensive snaps against the Jets, and even conducted a media session on Monday — something that players who are in concussion protocol are not permitted to do. Brents missed six defensive snaps on Sunday while dealing with a stinger. Hafley didn’t clarify when either player first experienced symptoms, so it is too early to tell if one or both will be cleared in time to return for this Sunday’s showdown with their AFC East division rivals, the New England Patriots. While Proctor did not appear at Wednesday’s practice at all, Brents was apparently seen doing conditioning drills on the side — which could be an indication that he is further along in the process than Proctor currently is. We will continue to monitor injury reports throughout the week to determine if either Dolphins player will be available this weekend.
