title: How will the Giants resolve their quarterback ‘problem’ if J.J. McCarthy continues to play well?
summary: The New York Giants may very well find themselves in an awkward (or enviable, or dangerous, depending on your point of view) situation by the end of this season. They entered the 2024 NFL Draft having rolled snake eyes on their expensive bet on Daniel Jones in 2023 after his career-best 2022 season. (The Indianapolis […]
full_text: The New York Giants may very well find themselves in an awkward (or enviable, or dangerous, depending on your point of view) situation by the end of this season. They entered the 2024 NFL Draft having rolled snake eyes on their expensive bet on Daniel Jones in 2023 after his career-best 2022 season. (The Indianapolis Colts said, hold my beer, and did exactly the same thing with Jones earlier this year, and now they’re the ones who have rolled snake eyes.) Giants general manager Joe Schoen, having lost out on Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Drake Maye in the 2024 Draft, decided to pass on the other three “big” quarterbacks in that draft, including Michigan’s J.J. McCarthy, and took Malik Nabers at No. 6 instead. The Minnesota Vikings subsequently gave up a fourth and a fifth round pick to the Jets to move up from No. 11 to No. 10 and draft McCarthy (they also got a seventh rounder). By the time the bye week arrived, Jones had been released and wound up a Viking along with McCarthy. Neither one ever played a down for the Vikings in 2024, McCarthy because of an injury. Fast forward to the 2025 Draft and Schoen moved up into the bottom of the first round to draft Jaxson Dart. McCarthy became the Vikings starter (over Sam Darnold, whom Minnesota let walk to Seattle where he led them to a Super Bowl title). Meanwhile, multiple injuries limited McCarthy to 10 starts, and by this spring he had lost his job to Kyler Murray. Dart, whose pro prospects were promising or met with skepticism depending on which “expert” you asked, had a scintillating rookie season (in the eyes of Giants fans, at least) but one that was interrupted by a concussion that caused him to miss a month in mid-season. Then Dart tore his meniscus, MCL, and PCL in Game 2 this year after looking great in Week 1, and Schoen was able to trade for McCarthy, the 2024 No. 10 pick, for the small price of a Round 5 pick. I realize you know all this, but I just wanted to remind you of it because the story of all these quarterbacks’ intertwined fortunes is not over. The Giants now have both Dart and McCarthy under contract for 2027. What they will do about that is anyone’s guess. Dart thrilled Giants fans with his masterful opening week game leading the Giants to a win over Dallas, but that’s all we got to see of him in year two. Questions linger in the minds of some about both his passing and defense-reading skills, and his shelf life as well given his penchant for running and not avoiding contact. McCarthy had already been tossed onto the scrap heap of public opinion by the time of his trade to the Giants for minimal draft compensation. Yet two weeks ago he relieved Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter after the Giants’ defense had been embarrassed by the Saints and rolled up 243 yards of offense and almost an amazing comeback win. Last Sunday, in his first start, he threw for 252 yards in leading the Giants to an upset road win in Houston. Now Giants fans are salivating about their team’s prospects for an NFC East title. If you saw that coming when they traded for McCarthy, you’re better than me. The question is: Which quarterback is better, and what should the Giants do with the one who is not the answer to that question? Originally I thought there was a chance the Giants might flip McCarthy to a contending team in the other conference before the trade deadline (which is two days after the Giants’ next game, in Philadelphia). Now I can’t imagine that happening unless McCarthy and the Giants lay such a big egg in Philly that it changes the team’s view of him. So you play the GM: Assume the Giants decide to trade the lesser of the two quarterbacks next winter. But which one is the lesser quarterback? The charts below show two commonly cited metrics of a quarterback’s play: The ESPN Quarterback Rating (QBR) and the Pro Football Focus passing grade. Both are on a scale of 0 to 100. QBR is purely data-driven, based on the increasingly popular EPA (expected points added, itself calculated from historical data on how much a given play affects a team’s chances of scoring), but with corrections for quality of defense faced and whether a play was in garbage time. PFF passing grade, as most of you know, is a subjective take on the quality of each pass a QB throws, based on film study. Here are plots of the two metrics against each other for both QBs for every pro game they’ve started: The two metrics are not identical. That’s not surprising since one measures results (QBR) while the other measures process (PFF grade). Also, QBR does include EPA generated by QB runs while the PFF grade that I show is only for passing. Nonetheless, Dart’s PFF grade is correlated with his QBR with a coefficient of 0.67 while McCarthy’s correlation is 0.76. I’ve labeled a few of Dart’s games to give you a feel for what the data consider his best/worst games to be. Unsurprisingly, the win over the Eagles at MetLife last year, which was really the start of the Dart phenomenon, is ranked highest by both metrics. Both metrics also really like the Las Vegas game that helped drop the Giants to No, 5 in the draft (that seems to have worked out OK), and of course the 2026 opener vs. Dallas. Unsurprisingly, the Vikings game in which Brian Daboll was afraid to even let Dart pass against that Brian Flores defense was his worst of the season. I’ve only labeled a small subset of McCarthy’s games that Giants fans will be familiar with. Speaking of the Giants-Vikings game, McCarthy’s debut against the Giants at MetLife was nothing to write home about. However his two games for the Giants both rank very highly. QBR prefers the New Orleans game, even though it was only one quarter of work, while PFF likes last Sunday’s game in Houston better. (FYI, the point in the upper right hand corner, McCarthy’s apparently best game by both metrics, was a win in Dallas where he went only 15 of 24 but for 250 yards and 2 TDs in only 27 snaps. McCarthy had an interception in that game but PFF did not charge him with a turnover-worthy play, implying that the ball may have bounced off a receiver’s hands and was then intercepted.) Overall, McCarthy has had about as many stinkers as Dart has had in PFF’s eyes, but unlike Dart, McCarthy’s bad games have had very low QBR, i.e., he did little to put the team in position to score, while Dart’s worst games in PFF’s view mostly have higher QBR, most likely because of what Dart adds with his running game. For example, his debut as a starter vs. the Chargers was notable largely for his 54 rushing yards and rushing TD. McCarthy is a good scrambler but up to now he has not been as much a candidate for designed runs. So, Giants fans: Let’s assume that Dart will be as good as new by next spring. How should John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen handle the Dart-McCarthy situation? Trade McCarthy before the trade deadline; let’s assume they could get a second round pick for him. Trade McCarthy over the winter for a first round pick and more, assuming he leads the Giants to a playoff berth. Trade Dart over the winter for a first round pick and more Let Dart and McCarthy compete for the starter role in 2027 camp and trade the loser for a first round pick Let Dart and McCarthy compete for the starter role in 2027 camp and keep the other as backup Trade both and draft Arch Manning (only kidding) Obviously it’s too early to really be discussing this, although an offer the Giants couldn’t refuse at the trade deadline makes it of at least some near-term relevance. But during the bye week it’s fun to speculate; what else is there to do? Quenton Nelson’s already traded, DeForest Buckner’s already traded. Bonus question: If McCarthy balls out as a Giant, who is the Vikings head coach in 2027?

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants are on a bye this week. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants are on a bye this week. NFL Week 8 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we ’ re hearing | ESPN.com For his part, McCarthy did what the Giants’ coaches were hoping he’d do on Sunday. He managed the operation of the offense cleanly, led the group with confidence and stayed within the game plan. Head coach John Harbaugh pointed out after the game that there were no procedural penalties with the offense, remarkable considering how new to it the starting quarterback was. Harbaugh also used the word “joy” multiple times to describe the feeling around the Giants right now, and he practically bounced out of his postgame news conference when it was done. Look, it’s only one game (and one quarter the week before against the Saints), and it’s far too soon to fully trust what this team can be with McCarthy leading it. But they’ve clearly come together as a group in Harbaugh’s first year. They’re identifying their leaders — Abdul Carter gave the fiery halftime speech that asked his teammates to leave everything out on the field in the second half — and drawing top-level performances out of players at every level of the roster. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson put cornerback Deonte Banks on star Texans receiver Nico Collins for large parts of the game Sunday, and Banks shut Collins down. Nagy on the Jameis/J.J. relationship Ask somebody around the league for their best Jameis Winston story, and it's very rarely some silly or hilarious tale. It's stuff like this. Here's Giants OC Matt Nagy on "The Schrager Hour", taking us through the day Jameis was benched for JJ McCarthy. @OmahaProd @ESPNNFL pic.twitter.com/7OLbowUHqs — Peter Schrager (@PSchrags) October 28, 2026 Inside the Numbers: Telling stats for first-place Giants | Giants.com J.J. McCarthy had five completions of at least 20 yards in Week 7, tied for the most in a game in his career (he also had five in Week 6 when he played only the final 11 minutes). McCarthy’s 10 completions of at least 20 yards this season are the second-most in the NFL since Week 6 behind only Caleb Williams (11). Isaiah Likely has 41 catches, one shy of his career high with Baltimore in 2024. He is the third tight end in NFL history to surpass 40 receptions in his first seven games with a team (Brock Bowers and Keith Jackson are the others). Likely is on pace for 100 catches, which has happened just three times in franchise history at any position. It would shatter Jeremy Shockey’s franchise record of 74 catches for tight ends, which has stood since 2002. Mark Bavaro is the only Giants tight end to eclipse 1,000 receiving yards, doing so in 1986 with 1,001. NFL QB rankings, Week 8: Joe Burrow, Caleb Williams hit season high | NFL.com 19. J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy played much better than expected in his first start for the Giants, going toe to toe with C.J. Stroud by firing a collection of precise passes to the likes of Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields. It helped that the Giants ran for 188 yards, but we shouldn’t discount McCarthy’s performance. Now he’ll have to do it consistently in order to truly repair his reputation. John Harbaugh has sights on NFC East with Eagles, Commanders on deck | New York Daily News Winning didn’t just help the Giants’ record in the standings, either. It emboldened them. It reinforced their confidence that they can make some special of this season. “I think there’s so many guys that are hungry to win here,” said fullback Pat Ricard. “They just want to win, and they want to prove themselves, and they want to be Pro Bowlers. They want to be All-Pros. They want to be paid. And they want to win. And I feel like Harbaugh challenges everybody here and keeps you accountable so that you are focused and you’re detailed, and you put the team above yourself. And we’re all working together. I feel like you’ve seen that all year: How resilient we’ve been, and just sticking in every game, and just keep believing, and keep trying to win,” he added. “And I feel like we’ve done that.” Inside the ‘pretty uncomfortable’ John Harbaugh Giants meeting that shows what he’s all about | New York Post “Very quiet and he mentioned many times that his goal was to make it uncomfortable, so I think he succeeded in that,” said left guard Jon Runyan Jr. “It wasn’t necessarily coming from a point of trying to bring people down, but more so as looking through the lens of looking at what’s going on in our division right now and the opportunity we have to create separation every week.” Jermaine Eluemunor gives head coach his flowers John Harbaugh is the BEST Coach in the NFL – Jermaine Eluemunor @JEluemunor | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/uibsdH051M — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) October 28, 2026 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Lions retain top spot | PFF 17. New York Giants (no change). The Giants’ offensive line was solid this week, but given the defensive line it went up against in the win over the Houston Texans, that in itself is a big achievement. This was the best we’ve seen from rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa, with the first-round draft pick compiling an 87.8 PFF pass-blocking grade and giving up no pressures from 32 pass-blocking snaps. Why Giants still aren’t favored to win NFC East despite leading division at 4-2-1 | The Athletic The situation at quarterback is the main source of the market’s resistance. After losing Dart in Week 2, backup Jameis Winston started the next four games before the Giants handed the reins to J.J. McCarthy against Houston. The third-year QB was acquired in a midseason trade with Minnesota, which drafted him 10th overall out of Michigan, where he won a national championship with Harbaugh’s brother, Jim, as the head coach. Another part of the equation is a weak division. The Cowboys sit in second place with two more losses, including one head-to-head to the Giants, and have a defense that ranks in the bottom third in several categories. The 2-5 Philadelphia Eagles have lost five straight games and Jalen Hurts is out for the season, while the Washington Commanders are 1-4-1. title: NY Giants trade candidate: WR Josh Downs wants out of Indianapolis
summary: Wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts, hoping to be part of the exodus as the 2-5 Colts enter a tear down after trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Should the New York Giants be interested in the 2023 third-round pick? Why it would work It is […]
full_text: Josh Downs | Getty Images Wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts , hoping to be part of the exodus as the 2-5 Colts enter a tear down after trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Should the New York Giants be interested in the 2023 third-round pick? Why it would work It is easy to forget that the Giants had a big role planned for 5-foot-9, 162-pound slot receiver Calvin Austin before he suffered a season-ending torn ACL in late August. The Giants have also lost wide receivers Gunner Olszewski and Braxton Berrios for the season, and they have no one on the roster who fills Austin’s role as a truly elusive, impactful, traditional slot receiver. The 5-9, 171-pound Downs would. In three full seasons with the Colts, the fewest receptions Downs has had is 58. Despite their offensive success in recent weeks, including four straight games of 27 points or more and three straight games of at least 400 yards gained, the Giants have seemed one receiver short all season. In addition to the injuries, the Giants moved on from Darius Slayton and their short-lived reunion with Odell Beckham Jr. didn’t last. The Giants could use one more potential play-making weapon on the outside. Downs is in the final year of his rookie contract. Financially, he would cost only the pro-rated portion of his $3.924 million base salary for the remainder of the 2026 season. The Giants and Downs would then have the option of working out a long-term deal. In terms of draft capital, it is hard to imagine that acquiring Downs would cost more than a late-round pick. Why it wouldn’t work The Giants have become a team that uses multiple tight ends, or a tight and fullback Patrick Ricard, on a high percentage of plays. Isaiah Likely is listed as a tight end, but has really become the slot receiver. Per Pro Football Focus, Likely has aligned in the slot on 255 of his 370 snaps this season. Malik Nabers has also been increasingly aligning in the slot. Over the past three games, Nabers has been in the slot 50 times — almost 17 times per game. Downs can also play on the outside, but would the Giants want him to take snaps away from Malachi Fields or one of their tight ends? Would Downs be a player you would like to see the team add, Giants fans?

title: Survey: Which position should the Giants target on the trade market?
summary: The New York Giants are off this week, enjoying a much-needed and well deserved bye week. The Giants stunned much of the football world with their overtime upset of the Houston Texans in Week 7, and now have control of the NFC East no matter what happens in Week 8. The Giants simply out-played the […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. catches a touchdown | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The New York Giants are off this week, enjoying a much-needed and well deserved bye week. The Giants stunned much of the football world with their overtime upset of the Houston Texans in Week 7, and now have control of the NFC East no matter what happens in Week 8. The Giants simply out-played the Texans despite being 10.5-point underdogs on the road. Their win, and how they went about it, has many around the media landscape reconsidering their playoff chances. The 4-2-1 Giants are now considered (slight) favorites to win the NFC East as of this writing, edging out the 3-4 Dallas Cowboys. This, in turn, has some wondering if the Giants should go “all in” on the trade market to reinforce their roster before the trade deadline. ‘With that in mind, we want to know what position you think the Giants should target as we approach the trade deadline. Running back – Cam Skattebo’s response to his non-benching may have changed John Harbaugh’s perception of the Giants’ backfield. However, it’s still possible that the Giants’ head coach wants the kind of “bellcow” back that he enjoyed throughout his time as the Baltimore Ravens head coach. The Giants have been using a running back rotation throughout the season, but it’s clear that Harbaugh would like one runner to shoulder most of the load. The giants could also use an explosive option out of the backfield to threaten and stretch defenses. Colts’ star running back Jonathan Taylor has been brought up as an “All In” option for a number of teams, while Tennessee Titans back Tony Pollard has been brought up as a possible “budget” option. It’s also possible that the New York Jets could consider trading Breece Hall in light of Braelon Allen’s recent success while Hall has been injured. Wide receiver – The Giants’ receiving depth chart is dangerously thin and good defenses may be able to take Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers away, forcing Fields and Mooney to carry the load. Adding another WR 1b or WR 2 could make it tougher for good defenses to limit J.J. McCarthy’s options. Likewise, Malik Nabers has been remarkably productive out of the slot this year. Adding a second big perimeter receiver would allow Nabers to play in the slot more often, getting him matchups against more slot corners. At the same time, another field-stretching wide receiver would play to J.J. McCarthy’s strengths as a deep ball passer. The Jaguars seem to be in the process of moving on from 2024 first round pick Brian Thomas Jr., who has rare length and speed, as well as a close relationship with Malik Nabers from their time together at LSU. Offensive guard – The Giants’ offensive line has been… Uneven. Their pass protection has generally been strong, however their run blocking hasn’t consistently lived up to expectations. It’s understandable for rookie Sisi Mauigoa to be inconsistent, however veteran Jon Runyan Jr. has struggled mightily with missed blocks over the past few weeks. It might be awkward — considering the Giants just extended him — but should they try to find an upgrade on the trade market? Quenton Nelson’s name was tossed around as a possible target, but he’s now a Seattle Seahawk. Defensive tackle – It’s fair to say that the Giants’ defensive line has outplayed expectations. D.J. Reader has turned the clock back and is not just a stout run defender, but also one of the best pass rushing defensive tackles in the NFL. Shelby Harris has played well, Darius Alexander continues to flash and improve as is C.J. Okoye. But there’s also room for improvement and the Giants could likely use another player to raise the ceiling and improve their depth. A player like Indianapolis NT Grover Stewart could help improve the Giants’ run defense as well as help to keep Reader fresh later in the season. There may also be bigger name tackles who surprisingly become available. None – The Giants don’t have much in the way of draft capital with picks in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd rounds, as well as a pair of 6th round picks. The Giants are anticipating a 4th round compensatory pick, but they don’t have that yet. The 2027 NFL Draft is anticipated to be a remarkably deep and talented one, and the Giants could get good players at each of these positions in the first three rounds. They might also have enough confidence in the current roster to bypass the trade market and prefer to save their resources if getting longer-term answers is prohibitively expensive. Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country. What should the Giants target? Are you confident in the Giants? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys:

title: NFL trade deadline: Should the NY Giants go all-in for 2026?
summary: Should the New York Giants go all-in at the NFL trade deadline to try and improve their chances of winning the NFC East this season? It’s a tricky question with defendable “yes” and “no” answers. Let’s look at both sides. Why they should go all-in The Giants are 4-2-1, leading a division where it looks […]
full_text: Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images Should the New York Giants go all-in at the NFL trade deadline to try and improve their chances of winning the NFC East this season? It’s a tricky question with defendable “yes” and “no” answers. Let’s look at both sides. Why they should go all-in The Giants are 4-2-1, leading a division where it looks like only one team — the Dallas Cowboys — is likely to really push them for the NFC East crown. The Giants, of course, already have a victory in hand. Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, star edge defender Brian Burns, and other key players the Giants have shown the resilience and toughness, what former Giants star and current radio analyst Carl Banks likes to call the “mental stamina” to make big plays in critical situations. “The players have earned the right,” GM Joe Schoen said on Tuesday, referring to the Giants having meaningful games coming up in November. “They were able to finish some of these games or make plays at the end of games or whatever it may be through their preparation and hard work and practice and dedication to the team and seeing how things play out on Sunday. So, they’ve earned that right to be in these games, and I know they’re excited about it.” They have also earned the right to have the organization support them by getting them some help, supplementing the roster in whatever way they can to give the team the best chance to finish what this gritty, under-manned, group has started. “We’re going to be in this thing until the end now,” head coach John Harbaugh said after Sunday’s overtime victory over the heavily-favored Houston Texans. Opportunities don’t come along every year, and sometimes they come along when you don’t expect them. The Philadelphia Eagles, NFC East champs three of the last four years, with a Super Bowl title and two Super Bowl appearances along the way, appear broken. GM Howie Roseman won’t let them stay that way. They will be back. Right now, though, their situation has opened a window in the division. The Washington Commanders don’t appear capable of taking advantage. The Cowboys probaby have more talent than the Giants, but do they have the grit, the resilience, and the coaching to get out of their own way long enough to be what they have the talent to be? The answer for most of the last 30 years or so has been “no.” The Giants aren’t paying Harbaugh $20 million annually to settle for seven wins when something bigger and more memorable is within reach, to say “no thanks, we’ll pass” when an opportunity to do something unexpectedly good comes along. They are paying Harbaugh to win. And, they are staring at a chance to do that, despite all of the obstacles that have been placed in their way. The Giants started down the “all-in” road by giving the Minnesota Vikings a 2027 fifth-round pick for J.J. McCarthy. The big “all-in” prize would be Indianapolis Colts’ running back Jonathan Taylor. It is clear after the Colts dealt away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner on Tuesday that the Colts are in tear-down mode after firing general manager Chris Ballard. Harbaugh has said he would love to have a “Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley circumstance” at running back. Cam Skattebo had a career-best 124 yards rushing on Sunday, but that was his first 100-yard game. He isn’t Henry or Barkley. Or Taylor. Taylor has rushed for more than 1,000 yards four times — each time in his first six years he has been healthy enough to play a full season. He has 29 career 100-yard rushing games, three of those for more than 200. What the Giants do need to be careful of should they employ an “all-in” approach that requires giving up premium draft assets — which a Taylor trade obviously would — is that they don’t do so for a short-term fix. Taylor is still just 27 years old. He signed a two-year, $44 million extension through 2028. If the Giants traded for him, they would owe him the pro-rated portion of his $6.98 million 2026 salary, and roughly $34 million over the 2027 and 2028 seasons. That is not bad for a running back of that ilk, sitting right between Henry ($15 million) and Christian McCaffrey ($19 million) in average annual value. Taylor would be the kind of investment likely to pay dividends beyond the remaining 10 games of this season. There are other areas the Giants could supplement — defensive line and perhaps wide receiver topping the list. Opportunities don’t come along all the time. The Giants have one, and the players have earned the organization’s support. That is the best argument for going all-in. Why they shouldn’t No matter what move, or moves, Schoen, Harbaugh, and the Giants make they are almost certainly not winning the organization’s fifth Lombardi Trophy of the Super Bowl era this season. They must remember that. The idea is not to be a nine-win team, make the playoffs, get bounced quickly, and have bankrupted yourself of future assets that could help the team continue to ascend. The idea is to put the Giants in position to be an annual contender, to be a team always considered capable of making a deep playoff run if things break in their favor. The Giants went down a similar road just a few years ago. In 2022, first-year coach Brian Daboll took the Giants on an unlikely playoff run, even winning a playoff game. The Giants followed that up by more or less abandoning the long-term build they had planned, giving Daniel Jones a big contract and trading draft assets for a 30-something tight end. That blew up in their collective faces. The Giants are now Harbaugh’s show, and if he wants an “all-in” move he will get one. Schoen, though, often talks about the lessons he has learned five seasons into his stint as general manager. Being honest about what you really are, and what the right path is to get where you really want to go is one of those lessons Giants fans should hope he has learned. And that he makes Harbaugh aware of. The Giants are not operating from a position of strength when it comes to draft capital. 2027 Giants’ draft picks (via Spotrac) Round 1 Round 2 Round 3 Round 4 ( projected compensatory selection ) Round 6 ( own ) Round 6 ( via Jaguars ) 2028 Giants’ draft picks (via Spotrac) Round 1 Round 2 Round 3 Round 4 Round 5 Round 6 Round 7 ( via Chiefs ) Schoen would love to replenish, if possible. “Obviously you want to have as many picks as you can. But, again, we’re glad we have Malachi Fields. We’re glad we have J.J. So, the utilization of those draft picks that we gave up to get those two players, we’re happy we have them,” Schoen said. “There are always options to regain capital down the road, whether it’s from players on the roster at the trade deadline if people call and it’s something that makes sense for us, through the offseason. If there’s trades being made around draft time, you can move back in the draft. There’s other ways that we can regain the capital, the compensatory formula, too. We’ll see how that plays out. “But, yeah, if it makes sense right now for us to do something in the short term and long term, we’re going to look at any opportunity that we can to upgrade the roster. And, again, there’s avenues that we can try to recoup draft picks down the road.” The Giants can’t fool themselves into believing that they possess a championship roster, or that one short-sighted move can make them one. title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 8
summary: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The Bills had their bye in Week 7, and they benefited from the 49ers’ loss in Atlanta. No. 2 — San Fransico 49ers (5-1) | (1st) 📉 1 spot The 49ers lose their No. 1 ranking after losing 29-20 in Atlanta. San Francisco is […]
full_text: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The Bills had their bye in Week 7, and they benefited from the 49ers’ loss in Atlanta. No. 2 — San Fransico 49ers (5-1) | (1st) 📉 1 spot The 49ers lose their No. 1 ranking after losing 29-20 in Atlanta. San Francisco is injured; their receiver position is decimated. George Kittle contributed eight catches for 88 yards, and Christian McCaffrey was in and out of the game with a lower-body injury. They’re a good team that hit a speed bump, but the casualties are mounting. No. 3 — Minnesota Vikings (6-0) | (4th) 📈 1 spot Minnesota has to be kicking themselves watching J.J. McCarthy perform as he did for the Giants. Kyler Murray and this Vikings offense are difficult to watch. Aaron Jones hurt his knee and is day-to-day, but Jordan Mason did return to action. Still, Brian Flores’ defense is elite, and it dictates and harasses every week. The Vikings escaped with a 16-10 home victory, as Murray threw for just 150 yards. No. 4 —Chicago Bears (5-2) (5th) | 📈 1 spot Chicago defeated the Patriots, 30-24, on Thursday Night Football. Luther Burden III caught four passes for 130 yards and a touchdown. Caleb Williams tossed two touchdowns as Chicago earned a high-quality win against a top-10 team. No. 5 — Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) | (9th) 📉 2 spots Kansas City couldn’t get much going against Seattle. Still, the Chiefs are a top-five team in the NFL, but their wide receiver problems remain tough to overcome. Their defense remains elite despite the loss to the next-ranked team. No. 6 — Seattle Seahawks (4-3) | (9th) 📈 3 spots Seattle had a statement 20-3 win against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Jaxson Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards with a score, and the defense held Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker to just 213 total yards. No. 7 — Denver Broncos (5-2) | SAME The Broncos scored 30 points against the Arizona Cardinals, but the offense still appears to be struggling. A 62-yard touchdown run by Bo Nix helped Denver secure the win. The three-headed backfield is leaning toward rookie Jonah Coleman, who rushed for 54 yards on nine carries, but it was J.K. Dobbins who scored the other rushing touchdown for Denver. No. 8 —Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) | SAME The Jacksonville Jaguars had their bye in Week 7. No. 9 — Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) | 📈 6 spots The Bengals scored 35 second-half points and shut out the Baltimore Ravens in the second half, allowing Joe Burrow and the Bengals to secure the 23-13 win. Tee Higgins went off for 148 receiving yards on six catches with a touchdown. Cincinnati’s defense is playing much better, and the Bengals shut down the Ravens after surrendering a 13-0 lead. No. 10 — New England Patriots (4-3) | (8th) 📉 4 spots New England is having an odd and streaky season that is highlighted by their Week 4 29-26 win over Buffalo. The Patriots relied on a freak lapse in tackling and coverage at the end of the first half on a long Rhamondre Stevenson touchdown reception, which kept this game very competitive. New England wasn’t bad in the game, but the Bears handled their business at home. No. 11 — Detroit Lions (4-2) | (13th) 📈 2 spots The Detroit Lions came out of their bye week with a 20-17 win against the Green Bay Packers. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards with some very impressive tosses, along with two touchdowns, as Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries. No. 12— Cleveland Browns (5-2) | (13th) 📈 4 spots The Browns are playing good football right now. They’re well coached, and they’re getting the most out of their quarterback situation. Second-year running back Quinshon Judkins rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns against the Tennessee Titans, who led 14-0 early. I have my reservations about Cleveland’s run defense after allowing Tony Pollard to rush for 129 yards with a hat trick. Still, the Browns have severely exceeded my expectations in 2026. No. 13 — Baltimore Ravens (4-3) | (10th) 📉 3 spots Cincinnati stomped the Ravens at home, 35-13. Lamar Jackson should return soon, which should change the team’s fortunes. Although, this injury situation seems to be lingering. No. 14 — Green Bay Packers (4-3) | 📉 2 spots Jordan Love is playing excellent football, and his two star receivers are struggling with drops. The Rams had a 28-6 lead, and the Raiders scored 15 points in the fourth quarter to make the score more respectable. The team responded to critical coaching and dominated both sides of the football. Still, overtime was necessary because of two missed kicks, among a few other things. Nevertheless, the Giants forced their fifth three-and-out in overtime and scored three plays later on a 30-yard touchdown run. The Giants are a different team under John Harbaugh. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants are in first place in the NFC East. Presser Points: Takeaways from GM Joe Schoen | Giants.com Jaxson Dart has been around the building during his rehab process. “He’s not weight-bearing yet. So he’s on his crutches. But he’s staying as positive as he can. He’s around, which I think is good, you know, mentally being around the guys, being around football still. And, you know, he still thinks if we make the playoffs that he’s going to be able to come back. So, you know, that’s just his mindset. That’s just his mindset. I mean, he got hurt in the Rams game. He’s in the locker room trying to do pass sets, dying to go back in the game. So, you know, he’s one of those guys you appreciate his toughness and grit.” The John Harbaugh effect The Giants completely overhauled the organization with one hire — John Harbaugh. pic.twitter.com/dr8Dn7jftv — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) October 26, 2026 How John Harbaugh put on a coaching masterclass in lead-up to Giants’ Week 7 win | The Athletic Harbaugh didn’t hesitate to address the biggest issues facing his team. He cut veteran running back Najee Harris, who had been ineffective and then griped about his role after getting only four carries against the Saints. That paved the way for Harbaugh to turn back to Skattebo, who handled a demotion against New Orleans with professionalism, then responded with a career-high 124 rushing yards against a stout Texans run defense. Making the right read on which buttons to push is an intangible quality for a coach. Harbaugh’s successful 18-year run in Baltimore provided belief that he had that touch when the Giants made the ballyhooed hiring this offseason. Harbaugh made all the right calls last week, which helped deliver the type of win that has him confident “We’re going to be in this thing until the end now.” The Winners and Losers of NFL Week 7 | The Ringer Winner: J.J. McCarthy, Giants Savior. One month after the Vikings gave up on the no. 10 pick in the 2024 draft by trading him to another NFC team for a future fifth-rounder, J.J. McCarthy has the Giants in the driver’s seat to win their division. The quarterback made his first start for New York as a double-digit road underdog against the Texans, and he pulled off the upset in a 27-21 overtime victory that’s the highlight of the Giants’ season so far. Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell once said that “organizations fail young quarterbacks before young quarterbacks fail organizations.” It’s a thought worth revisiting with McCarthy playing well so soon after his turbulent tenure in Minnesota came to an end. While a strained relationship with the Vikings’ coaching staff didn’t help, injuries were McCarthy’s biggest issue during his first few years in the league. If he can stay healthy, the Giants might have found something here—and it’s worth noting that Sunday marked only his 11th professional start. Abdul Carter urged Giants to empty the tank. Now go win the NFC East | The Record When Abdul Carter speaks up, the New York Giants pay attention. Because the messaging is often spot on. Jaxson Dart was the heart and Brian Burns the soul of the team, but both players are out for the season following knee surgeries. What’s become clear is Carter, for all intents and purposes, has an intrinsic ability to feel the Giants’ pulse. NFL Insider: Giants bully ball taking root “[The Giants are] playing a type of bully-ball that travels.” Manti making the case for the New York Giants as the team to beat in the NFC East 😤 pic.twitter.com/WkcFLi5CQK — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) October 27, 2026 NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Trend to watch: Deonte Banks’ strong coverage. The rejuvenated Giants cornerback locked up Texans top receiver Nico Collins most of the afternoon. The Texans completed just four of seven passes for 25 yards when throwing in Banks’ direction, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Collins finished with two catches on five targets for 6 yards, thanks in large part to Banks. J.J. McCarthy’s resurgence took root long before joining Giants — with plenty of room to grow | New York Post Despite his struggles with the Vikings, McCarthy said Sunday he began feeling more comfortable in the league in a Week 14 win over Washington. Coming off three straight losses in which he threw six interceptions and just two touchdowns, McCarthy — after missing a week in the concussion protocol — carved up the Commanders on 16-for-23 passing for 163 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. He then won his final three starts, though he missed another with a hand injury. “Just being able to really start feeling like the defense is slowing down and understanding concepts, intent of plays, understanding the situation,’’ McCarthy said. “There’s a lot of things that go into playing NFL quarterback and it takes a little bit to figure those things out. I really feel like I was on an upward trajectory after that game. I continue to just refine my craft and get better every day.’’ Baldy on the Giants run game Brian Baldinger on Week 7's run game — New York Giants (@Giants) October 27, 2026 Giants’ John Harbaugh echoes Cam Skattebo’s criticism of NFL for penalty | NJ.com “That’s how I felt about it,” he said. “I mean, I understand the idea, but I also understand human physiology and anatomy and the way the body works. Skatt runs low. You have to run low. You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can’t run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head is down there, too. You can’t move your head off your shoulders. It’s a physical impossibility. I’m quite sure Skatt’s not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram. “It’s not the way he’s thinking. He’s leading with his shoulder. That’s what he’s trying to do. He’s trying to keep his head in a good, strong, upright position. But his pads are down there low. He runs low to the ground. That’s the way you’re supposed to run. That’s how you protect yourself and the football. So I didn’t have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven’t heard from the league. Maybe they’ll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it, in terms of what they want us to teach. And that would be great.” From Big Blue View 4 takeaways from Giants GM Joe Schoen: Trade deadline, J.J. title: The Jets Can’t Fire Their Way Into an Answer
summary: The Jets are 2-5 after losing to Miami 28-25, and Aaron Glenn is now 5-19 as a head coach. Four of the five losses came by a touchdown or less, which is exactly the kind of stat that keeps a coach employed and keeps a team losing. Meanwhile Darren Mougey has built the best war […]
full_text: The Jets are 2-5 after losing to Miami 28-25, and Aaron Glenn is now 5-19 as a head coach. Four of the five losses came by a touchdown or less, which is exactly the kind of stat that keeps a coach employed and keeps a team losing. Meanwhile Darren Mougey has built the best war chest this franchise has had in years. Three first round picks in 2027, well over $100 million in projected cap space, a 2026 draft class that looks like it hit, and even Brandon Stephens, the corner everybody laughed at in March 2025, settling in as a solid starter. So the real question isn’t whether Glenn has been good enough. He hasn’t. It’s whether you can fire him without losing whatever is making this roster better. There’s a real case that Glenn is part of the evaluation. He spent two years as a Jets scout after he retired, and he and Mougey were hired as a pair, which usually means a shared board. The popular version of the argument goes further. Glenn drives the draft, Mougey owns free agency, because pro scouting happens during the season while Glenn is busy coaching. That doesn’t hold up. College area scouts are on the road all fall too, and both the draft board and the free agent decisions get made in March and April, when the head coach is in the room for all of it. The honest answer is that nobody outside the building knows who’s hitting on these guys. Woody does, and that should be the first question in the end of year review. So you have to compare the two ways this can go wrong. Fire Glenn, and it turns out he really was the evaluator. The drafts slip some, but the scouting staff, the picks and the cap space all stay, and you find out within a draft or two. Keep Glenn, and it turns out he’s just not a head coach. The quarterback they take in 2027 spends his first, most important years under a defensive coach with no track record developing one, and the Jets burn the most attractive head coaching opening they’ve had since Rex Ryan walked in. One mistake costs you a couple of drafts. The other costs you a quarterback. That’s not close. And if Mougey turns out to be a lesser GM without Glenn, the timelines actually work in the Jets’ favor. A young quarterback is tied to his head coach and his system, not the guy who drafted him, so you can replace a GM in year two or three without touching the QB’s development. Replace the coach and you start the kid over. The one real exposure is the 2027 pick itself, which could be Mougey’s first big call without Glenn, so that quarterback has to be the new coach’s pick as much as the GM’s. Which brings up Mike Tomlin, the name a lot of people want. He stepped away from Pittsburgh in January for what Art Rooney called mostly family reasons, and the Steelers still hold his rights so getting him costs picks on top of the money. The bigger problem is the quarterback. His ring came with Big Ben, whom Bill Cowher’s staff drafted three years before Tomlin got there. Every quarterback Tomlin had to find himself, Kenny Pickett as a first rounder, Mason Rudolph didn’t stick, and his coordinator hires, Todd Haley, Matt Canada and Arthur Smith, aren’t exactly a QB factory. The fair counter is that he never picked in the top ten because he kept winning, but Jalen Hurts and Brock Purdy weren’t top ten picks either. Somebody developed them. Tomlin is a great culture coach for a team that already has its quarterback. The Jets are about to draft theirs. The tempting move is to clean house, fire both, and go big game hunting for a coach and a GM. Don’t. A GM hired in late January gets about three months before he picks the franchise quarterback, off a board somebody else built, with scouts he doesn’t know yet, and he’ll probably bring in his own people and toss the work that built this war chest. The one constant through every Jets reset has been ownership, and two hires at once just doubles the bet on the part with the worst track record. Here’s the path. Let Glenn finish the season, because a midseason firing buys you nothing but an interim coach. Then make the change, keep Mougey with final say on the roster, and hire an offensive head coach whose whole résumé is developing quarterbacks. Hold on to the defensive assistants and the people who turned the secondary around, since that’s the part of Glenn’s tenure actually worth keeping, and if the review shows Glenn was the guy on the board, offer him a personnel role and see if he takes it. The pitch to candidates sells itself: picks, cap space, a rookie quarterback to shape, and a GM who has already proven he can stack assets. The Jets don’t have a talent problem anymore. They have a coaching problem, and for once they’re in position to fix it the right way.

title: Jets currently own three pick in the top 12 of the 2026 NFL Draft
summary: Week 7 was a frustrating one for fans of the New York Jets. The team lost in ugly fashion to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. There is a bit of good news for the team when it comes to NFL Draft position. Not only do the Jets own three first round picks, but the Indianapolis […]
full_text: New York Jets general manager Darren Mougey answers questions during a press conference following a practice for the New York Jets at their training facility on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in Florham Park. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Week 7 was a frustrating one for fans of the New York Jets. The team lost in ugly fashion to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. There is a bit of good news for the team when it comes to NFL Draft position. Not only do the Jets own three first round picks, but the Indianapolis Colts, whose final record impacts one of those picks, appear to have raised the white flag and gone into seller mode ahead of the trade deadline. After Week 7 of the NFL season, the Jets are in position to own three of the top twelve pick in next year’s NFL Draft. The current order per Tankathon : Chargers 0-6 Titans 1-6 Dolphins 1-5 Commanders 1-4-1 Texans 2-5 Eagles 2-5 Jets (from Colts 2-5) Cardinals 2-5 Buccaneers 2-5 Jets 2-5 Saints 2-5 Jets (from Cowboys 3-4) Raiders 3-4 Browns (from Rams 3-4) Falcons 3-4 Ravens 4-3 Seahawks 4-3 Patriots 4-3 Picks 19 through 32 are determined by the outcome of games in the NFL Playoffs The Jets appear on their way to another disappointing season, but there is at least some reason for hope. The team’s rookie class is playing at a pretty high level generally speaking, and the team has three early picks in what appears to be a deep Draft.

title: Eagles roster news includes Dameon Pierce to injured reserve
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five moves on Wednesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DAMEON PIERCE Pierce suffered an injury during the fourth quarter of the Eagles’ loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Despite this, he led all Eagles running backs in touches on Monday night since Saquon […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Dameon Pierce #39 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field for halftime during the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five moves on Wednesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: RB Dameon Pierce was placed on injured reserve. RB Jaydon Blue was signed from the practice squad to the active roster. OG Evan Beerntsen, WR Quentin Skinner, and DB Shaun Wade were signed to the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DAMEON PIERCE Pierce suffered an injury during the fourth quarter of the Eagles’ loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Despite this, he led all Eagles running backs in touches on Monday night since Saquon Barkley wasn’t healthy enough to take his normal workload. This development means that the Eagles’ second (Tank Bigsby), third (Will Shipley), and fourth (Pierce) backfield options are all now on injured reserve. The Eagles’ fifth option (Carson Steele) was recently waived from IR with an injury settlement. And Barkley seemingly still remains less than 100%. All of this is to say that the Eagles are REALLY banged up at running back this season. Bad luck there. Making matters worse is that the Eagles haven’t exactly had good run blocking for most of this season. The extent of Pierce’s injury is currently unclear as of me typing this sentence. At the very least, he will be required to miss four games. Bigsby is eligible to return to the active roster after Week 8. It’s Week 9 for Shipley. JAYDON BLUE The Eagles previously called up Blue, a former Dallas Cowboys draft pick, from the practice squad to their roster on October 22. He suited up for their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers but did not play a snap. The Eagles then waived him and brought him back on the practice squad. With Pierce going on IR and Barkley still banged up, the Eagles needed to add another RB to their roster. Blue is seemingly in line to have a role against the Washington Commanders in Week 8. EVAN BEERNTSEN The Eagles recently brought Beerntsen, who played right guard at South Dakota State and Northwestern, to Philly for a visit. The 26-year-old rookie was originally selected by the Baltimore Ravens with a seventh-round pick (No. 253 overall, the fifth-to-last selection) in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Ravens cut him in late August and then he spent some time on the Seattle Seahawks’ practice squad before they also cut him. Now in Philly, Beerntsen will help to provide some more interior offensive line depth. Pre-draft scouting report via NFL.com : Beerntsen has consistent run blocking tape but a lack of length that could get spell trouble in the NFL. He has 51 career starts under his belt, but he’ll be an older rookie after seven college seasons. He makes smart use of his angles and is stout at the point of attack, consistently straining to neutralize big men in front of him. He can be outreached in protection or have his punch wiped away, though. There are inconsistencies with patching up his edges against twists. Beerntsen is tough, but he might need a move to center to boost his roster potential. Spider graph via Mockdraftable : QUENTIN SKINNER The 6’5”, 195 pound Skinner played college football for Kansas before going unselected in the 2025 NFL Draft. He signed with the New York Jets and spent his rookie season on their practice squad, eventually getting temporarily elevated to their roster for one game. He played 16 snaps and logged one target for a 10-yard reception and a first down. Efficient! The Jets waived Skinner earlier this offseason, which led to him being claimed by the Buffalo Bills. But then they cut him after training camp. With DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and Britain Covey currently banged, the Eagles were in need of some more receiver depth. Now they’re getting a look at Skinner and his steamed hams. SHAUN WADE Shaun Wade is back! The peanut punching preseason standout is back in Philly after previously spending a multi-week stint on the Eagles’ practice squad earlier this season. He provides more cornerback depth.

title: Eagles-Cowboys Film Review: Some positives on offense, for once
summary: I thought the Eagles’ offense was far more competent against the Cowboys. After the past few weeks, I was happy to see that. However, they still only scored 21 points against a terrible Cowboys defense. It will take a lot more than this to convince me that this offense is suddenly well-designed and well-coached. The […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images I thought the Eagles’ offense was far more competent against the Cowboys. After the past few weeks, I was happy to see that. However, they still only scored 21 points against a terrible Cowboys defense. It will take a lot more than this to convince me that this offense is suddenly well-designed and well-coached. The numbers reflect an uneven performance. As always, the advanced data here comes courtesy of Fantasy Points Data Suite . The Eagles finished with 321 yards, a passing EPA of −0.11 per play, and +0.05 on the ground. They put together touchdown drives of 75, 76, and 84 yards, but did not score again after taking a 21–20 lead in the third quarter. There was some good football, followed by a familiar lack of answers when they needed to drop back and throw. For once, though, the offense gave me more to feel positive about than the defense. What a weird thing to write this season. Offense I have spent weeks asking the Eagles to stop forcing the under-center play-action game, so naturally they opened with it and completed a pass against pressure. Fair enough! I sort of respect Sean Mannion’s willingness to stick with it on the very first snap. I respect it, because if this went wrong, he would have looked incredibly dumb. He clearly believes in this approach, and getting something positive from it immediately was better than another opening disaster. However, look at how the completion happens. The Eagles still blow the protection and allow a free rusher at Tanner McKee. The downfield route combination does not work, but the Cowboys leave Barkley completely uncovered in the flat. McKee finds the available answer, which is good, but this is hardly evidence that all the issues with this part of the offense have disappeared. I’ll take the completion, but I’ll keep a pretty big question mark next to the process. Eagles' Offense All22 Thread vs. Cowboys. 1) Hey, it's not what I wanted to see, but I sort of respect the guts from Sean Mannion to run under-center play action on the first play of the game. And it works! Against pressure! I mean, the Eagles still blow the protection, and a… pic.twitter.com/euTIk6PmQe — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 28, 2026 Barkley is a superstar. Even looking something like 80% healthy, he was the best offensive player on the field. His vision and ability to make defenders miss change what this offense can produce. I think a fully healthy Barkley scores on this run, which tells you both how good he is and how obvious it was that he wasn’t quite right. Dickerson makes a difference here, too. He does not look like the player who could simply move people wherever he wanted, but he understands how to create space. Barkley appears to anticipate what Dickerson will do before bouncing the run outside. Then look at Darius Cooper and Lemon blocking downfield. In my view, those are the Eagles’ two best blocking receivers, and having them involved more helped turn some of these runs into much better plays. I’m proud of Barkley for the effort, and I respect him enormously for wanting to be out there. I still have no clue why the Eagles played him. Considering where this team is at, watching him clearly short of full fitness felt somewhat mental to me. He finished with 62 yards on seven carries, and even that limited workload showed how much better the offense is with him. Like the rest of you, I am in full rebuild mode now. But I would struggle to trade Barkley unless a really good offer came in. I just want to watch him on my football team for as long as possible. I can’t help it! 2) Saquon Barkley, man. What a superstar. I don't think he should have been out there, but even at 80%, he was the best player on the field on offense. If he's 100% healthy, this is a touchdown. Having Landon Dickerson back at LG made a difference in the run game, and Barkley… pic.twitter.com/2rCU29dym0 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 28, 2026 One thing I repeatedly called for in the preview was attacking the edge of this Cowboys defense, particularly Rashan Gary. It’s always nice when something you wrote about shows up immediately! Barkley gets to the edge here despite clearly lacking his usual burst. This run shows his intelligence as well as athletic ability. Barkley sees where the space is and knows how to get there. The physical talent gets most of the attention, understandably, but his feel for a run is outstanding. 3) Barkley clearly wasn't right, and he's still beating the Cowboys' defense to the edge. Just a special talent. It's great when something you said in the preview comes true instantly! In the preview, I repeatedly called for the Eagles to attack the edge, and especially Rashan… pic.twitter.com/gZzGMgq3DQ — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 28, 2026 Another excellent rep from Barkley, supported by a very good double team from Markel Bell and Dallas Goedert. Grant Calcaterra does a decent job, too, although the Cowboys’ edge defender offers very little resistance. I thought this was their best game of the season for run blocking from the tight ends and receivers. Goedert really showed up there, and Cooper and Lemon gave them something on the perimeter. Early on, I liked the simpler approach with inside zone and duo rather than immediately making everything about outside zone. There were concepts here that suited the players doing the blocking, and the offense benefited. 4) Again, very good vision on show from Barkley. Heck of a double team from Markel Bell and Dallal Goedert. The Eagles' offensive line was much improved in the run game. Calcaterra does quite well (!), but the Cowboys' edge defender doesn't put up much of a fight. I thought… pic.twitter.com/dS91NxDXcj — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 28, 2026 Did the Eagles actually run a successful screen? They moved away from the bubble screen here and tried a tunnel screen, bringing Cooper back inside toward the blocking. I liked seeing a different answer, even if the execution out front wasn’t particularly good. Cooper does a lot of the work himself by forcing defenders to miss. This is also where the quality of the Cowboys’ defense has to stay part of the discussion. On a third-down play like this, how much credit belongs to the offense for improving, and how much belongs to a defense that cannot finish the play? There is room to like the change while acknowledging that this is a pretty horrible defensive rep by the Cowboys. It worked, but I wouldn’t want to rely on that every week. It’s hard to judge this game on the offense, because you can’t ignore how poor the Cowboys have been. 5) Did the Eagles run a successful screen pass? They mixed it up and ran a tunnel screen instead of the bubble screen, which worked a lot better! The blocking out in front isn't actually very good, but Darius Cooper makes a few defenders miss. Again, this is one of those… pic.twitter.com/GkSRBYOzvP — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 28, 2026 Dameon Pierce looked better than he had in previous weeks, so of course he ended up going off injured. There was more purpose to some of his running, and the blocking gave him a chance. Jordan Mailata creates a huge lane on the edge here, and the Cowboys again struggle badly to defend the perimeter. This has been their biggest issue all season long. Even Marquise Brown gets involved with a block! The offense showed some fight in this game, and the receivers contributed to that. I’ve criticized the way the Eagles have asked certain players to block this season, but I liked the collective effort here. When the line creates room and the receivers sustain their blocks, a back has a much better chance of getting something worthwhile out of the play. 6) Dameon Pierce looked better than he had in…

title: Several Eagles players listed among top 25 trade candidates ahead of the deadline
summary: This season went sideways quickly for the Eagles, and as we approach the NFL trade deadline (Tuesday, November 10) it looks like Howie Roseman could consider moving some guys. ESPN’s Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler put out their Top 25 trade candidates by potential value, and included several Eagles. At No. 8 on the list […]
full_text: Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images | DeFodi Images via Getty Images This season went sideways quickly for the Eagles, and as we approach the NFL trade deadline (Tuesday, November 10) it looks like Howie Roseman could consider moving some guys. ESPN’s Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler put out their Top 25 trade candidates by potential value, and included several Eagles. At No. 8 on the list is CB Riq Woolen, who is considered a fit for teams like the Lions, Panthers, and Steelers. “ What Fowler is hearing: When I talk to rival teams about which players Philly might move, Woolen’s name comes up fairly often. He’s a high-upside corner and 2027 free agent whose $1.26 million base salary could help facilitate a trade (much of his $12 million in guarantees came via signing or restructured bonuses). Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%“ Eagles guard Landon Dickerson sits at No. 12 on the list, with Fowler explaining that the relationship between Dickerson and the team doesn’t feel right — something we’ve covered, as well . The NFL insider also noted that the Eagles are in position to recoup some draft capital as they look to go younger up front. Still, they only put Dickerson’s chance of being traded around 25 percent. Tight end Dallas Goedert and wide receiver Hollywood Brown were also honorable mentions on the list, which makes sense given that they’re playing on one-year contracts. The Eagles were also listed among the list as a potential landing spot for Bengals EDGE Shemar Stewart, a trade that Fowler suggests would be for a third-rounder. “ What Bowen sees on tape: Stewart has played just eight snaps this season, so teams would be betting on potential with the 2025 first-rounder. Stewart is an explosive mover with the physical profile to play on the edge, but he has yet to develop a refined pass-rush plan. He has two career sacks.“ Coming off a Monday night game and with a short week, Howie Roseman and team’s front office might be taking their time to picture their overall approach to building this roster over the next few years. But the GM has some big decisions to make about the direction of the team this year, and moving forward.

title: Eagles News: Nick Foles says “there is dysfunction in Philly”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Accurate or not, these are the kind of sentiments that will be expressed when a team is on a big losing streak. It is notable that Nick Foles, who usually seems pretty positive in his analysis, is more harsh here. Let’s […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 26: Former quarterback Nick Foles hugs the Philadelphia Eagles mascot prior to the NFC Championship Game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Accurate or not, these are the kind of sentiments that will be expressed when a team is on a big losing streak. It is notable that Nick Foles, who usually seems pretty positive in his analysis, is more harsh here. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles legend calls Philly’s culture dysfunctional — Nick Sirianni responds: ‘That crap’ – NJ.com “There is dysfunction in Philly,” Foles said on his podcast. “It was little things for me. It wasn’t the execution that got me. It was culture things. The number one thing isn’t scheme, a fancy coordinator, it’s culture. In Philadelphia, for the better of the past couple decades, they have had really good culture. Something is changing.” During the offseason, Foles feared that the Eagles would fall apart after they pushed a legendary coach out of the building. “When they got rid of [former Eagles offensive line coach] Jeff Stoutland, that really pissed me off,” Foles said. “I knew something bad was gonna happen. He is a great coach. For him not to get the respect that he deserves, that frustrates me. When guys are getting hit and offensive lineman are near them, is someone going to pick up the running back? He just got hit in the backfield. That culture with Jeff, that would never fly. When we got hit, we were picked up right away by the offensive line.“ Eagles-Cowboys Film Review: Most annoying defensive performance of the Vic Fangio era – BGN I have made plenty of excuses for the Eagles’ defense this year. There have been games when I thought this unit fought hard and received very little help from the other side of the ball. There is absolutely no excuse for this one. Monday Night Football. At home against the Cowboys. Most of the defense’s best players were available, including the expensive “superstars” up front. And this was the performance? I can’t remember coming away from a game this annoyed about a defense since the Super Bowl LVII defeat vs. the Chiefs. The Cowboys scored on seven of nine possessions, rushed for 204 yards, and finished with 416 total yards at 6.4 yards per play. The Eagles recorded zero sacks, zero quarterback hits, and zero rushing tackles for loss. After the offense opened the second half with a 17-play touchdown drive that took 9:16 off the clock, the defense immediately surrendered another touchdown. We cannot blame the offense for that. This defense had a long rest and a lead, and still couldn’t get a stop. NFL Week 8 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we’re hearing – ESPN Fowler: Mystery surrounds the Eagles’ plans. It’s unclear at this point whether GM Howie Roseman conducts a fire sale. But some rival teams are expecting at least mild unloading. Perhaps the most interesting team is the Tampa Bay Bucs, who typically are not subtractors by nature. Normally, this would be a natural time for a roster mini-reset. But despite the 2-5 record, the Bucs are alive in the NFC South, which they’ve won four of the past five years. Win enough divisional games and the overall record doesn’t matter as much. I do believe, had the Bucs lost last week to fall to 1-6, they would be actively discussing dealing players. Graziano: We didn’t really address the Eagles in our trade-deadline portion of this column, but my sense is that things could go either way — or a little bit of both — for them ahead of the trade deadline. They have veterans on expiring contracts (cornerback Riq Woolen, receiver Hollywood Brown and tight end Dallas Goedert) who could be of interest to contending teams and help Philly out with draft-pick compensation. But the Eagles are loaded with picks already thanks to previous trades. They dealt their 2027 third-rounder for Jonathan Greenard but are projected to get a third-round compensatory pick due to the free agent loss of Jaelan Phillips. And they have extra first- and second-round picks in the 2028 draft due to the trades of A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens. The Eagles aren’t desperate to refill their coffers. But they’ll always listen, in both directions. If they get a good enough offer for a player who isn’t part of their future plans, as was the case with Jurgens a couple of weeks ago, they’ll be open to it. And if they see a chance to add a player who might be more than a two-month rental, as the Texans did with Marvin Harrison Jr., they’ll be open to that as well. Will the Eagles be sellers at the trade deadline? A look at Howie Roseman’s options – The Athletic There have been trade deadlines when Roseman was not an aggressive buyer. He was also a strategic seller at times (such as trading veteran Isaac Sopoaga in 2013 when Bennie Logan was ready to take over at nose tackle). But no deadline has looked like this, with a losing record and attractive pending free agents available. That’s why the focus should be on players such as Ojomo, Woolen and Goedert. One factor to consider is whether the Eagles would prefer to keep Ojomo and Woolen and benefit from the compensatory formula. (Goedert, who is expected to be a post-June 1 cut because of a poison pill in his contract, would not qualify for a compensatory pick.) The Eagles have benefited from compensatory picks in recent years, though they also needed those pending free agents to contribute down the stretch. That might not be the case this December. Trading the player at the deadline rather than letting him leave in the offseason could mean the pick arrives as early as April’s draft, and it also lets the Eagles be aggressive in free agency if they choose. (Incoming free agents could cancel out outgoing free agents in the compensatory pick formula.) Which Eagles players are untouchable at the trade deadline? – PhillyVoice Nobody is trading for them in their current state. QB Jalen Hurts: Hurts of course has blood clots in his lungs, and his season is over. Depending on how things play out after this mess of a season is over, particularly in the case of a head coaching change, a trade of Hurts should be viewed as a possibility, but not until the offseason. Selling – Iggles Blitz The trade deadline isn’t until November 10th so it is interesting that the Colts made these moves so early. They set the market. That should lead to more calls between teams. The Niners and Seahawks just got better. That could cause the Bears, Lions, Rams, or other NFC contenders to feel forced to make a move. Buffalo needs help for their defense. The Chiefs need a WR. There should be plenty of activity. Nick Sirianni talked about the Eagles going 6-2 down the stretch in 2021 and how that helped the 2022 and 2024 teams make the Super Bowl. That’s why the Eagles will keep competing and doing everything they can to win. NFL players also have short careers. You don’t want to throw away a season. You don’t want apathy to set in. You don’t want to ruin good culture. We can debate if that has already started to go. I still think the Eagles have the right kind of guys in the building. We’ll find out more about that over the final 10 games. I mentioned players playing for their jobs. Sirianni will be coaching for his. We’ll find out just how much the players think of him with the way they play for the rest of the season. What we learned from Eagles-Cowboys: Forget 2021 comparisons, Howie Roseman should sell at the trade deadline – PHLY Eagles Going back through some of the media scrums I missed while attending Nick Sirianni’s news conference last night, this quote from Cooper DeJean about mentally handling the adversity the team is facing jumped out to me. “It’s been tough, to be honest,” DeJean said. “With the success that…

The practice marked his first participation since Week 5. Joining Skowronek as limited on Wednesday was outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, with a groin injury; Highsmith was limited with the same injury last week but still played versus New Orleans in Week 7. A trio of defensive backs — Brandin Echols (hamstring), Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring) — did not participate Wednesday. Echols missed the Steelers’ game against the Saints, while Ramsey has been playing through his wrist injury despite missing practice reps in recent weeks. Slaughter is a new addition to the report. Elsewhere on the Steelers’ participation report, defensive tackle Cam Heyward, outside linebacker T.J. Watt and tight end Darnell Washington did not participate Wednesday with a rest designation. The Steelers’ Week 8 opponent, the Cleveland Browns, have yet to release their Wednesday practice report at the time of this writing.

title: Kurt Warner sees low ceiling for Steelers
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have opened the 2026 season with a 5-2 record, but their early success has not convinced everyone that they are legitimate contenders in the AFC. Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner is among those expressing skepticism, pointing to Pittsburgh’s offensive limitations as a potential obstacle to making a deep postseason […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have opened the 2026 season with a 5-2 record, but their early success has not convinced everyone that they are legitimate contenders in the AFC. Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner is among those expressing skepticism, pointing to Pittsburgh’s offensive limitations as a potential obstacle to making a deep postseason run. Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Warner questioned whether the Steelers can generate enough points to keep pace with the AFC’s top offenses, particularly as the competition intensifies over the second half of the season. “When you look at the AFC and the teams that are going to be around, they can all score points,” Warner said. “That’s the challenge for the Steelers right now, is how do you score points?” Warner’s concerns center on Pittsburgh’s ability to sustain drives and consistently finish possessions with touchdowns. While the Steelers have managed to win games, their offensive production has raised questions about whether they can keep up with teams capable of putting points on the board in bunches. “I don’t think [the Steelers are] gonna go very far.” @kurt13warner is skeptical about Pittsburgh despite their 5-2 start 😬 (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/6DDWXHjric — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 28, 2026 “Any defense would line up against a team that has to go 10-12 plays per drive to score a touchdown,” Warner said. The issue becomes particularly concerning when considering Pittsburgh’s struggles to establish a consistent rushing attack near the goal line. Warner notes that the Steelers have scored just one rushing touchdown all season, an indication of the difficulties they have experienced turning offensive opportunities into points on the ground. The Steelers’ 5-2 record provides a strong foundation heading into the remainder of the season, but Warner’s criticism highlights the difference between winning games and developing into a legitimate Super Bowl contender. Pittsburgh’s defense can help keep games competitive, but the offense will likely need to demonstrate greater consistency and scoring ability to compete with the conference’s elite. For Pittsburgh, the challenge is straightforward: turn its winning start into an offense capable of matching the firepower of the teams it hopes to beat in January. title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba nabs weekly award after monster performance against Chiefs
summary: Coming off a historic 2025 campaign where he racked up a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is now on pace to one-up last year’s performance and has earned another weekly award. Alongside Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, the superstar wideout was named a FedEx Ground & Air Player of the […]
full_text: Coming off a historic 2025 campaign where he racked up a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is now on pace to one-up last year’s performance and has earned another weekly award. Alongside Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, the superstar wideout was named a FedEx Ground & Air Player of the Week following another dominant game against the Kansas City Chiefs, where he recorded nine receptions, 150 yards and a touchdown—while playing a significant role in the Seahawks 20-3 upset win. Unlike the NFL’s Player of the Week awards, the FedEx Ground & Air winners are chosen by fans. Another one for JSN 🏆 Read more » https://t.co/2SUjnzDzJc pic.twitter.com/FuLTfpzm5c — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 28, 2026 His monster game against Kansas City was highlighted by a 28-yard score with just under two minutes remaining in the first half when he hauled in an over the shoulder catch while covered by Chiefs star rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane. It marked the second time in 2026 Smith-Njigba has been named Player of the Week , with the first following his nine catch, 155 yard, three touchdown performance against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. With two weekly awards under his belt, it should come as no surprise the Seahawks star receiver leads the league with an astounding 867 yards across just seven games, over 200 more than Dallas’ Ceedee Lamb (651). Smith-Njigba also ranks first in receiving touchdowns (8), yards per game (123.9) and second in receptions (58). With his remarkable Week 7 performance, the fourth year superstar became just the sixth wideout in NFL history to record 100+ yards in six or more of his team’s first seven games and he’ll look to stay hot when Seattle hosts the Chicago Bears on Monday night as they look to inch one step closer to first place in the NFC West.
